News.title: Shameless ‘broke’ finance worker, 29, stole £92k from breast cancer charity to pay for wedding and honeymoon
News.content:
I DOUGH Shameless ‘broke’ finance worker, 29, stole £92k from breast cancer charity to pay for wedding and honeymoon

A SHAMELESS “broke” finance worker who stole almost £92,000 from a breast cancer charity to pay for his wedding and honeymoon has been jailed.

Tameem Choudhury, 29, “exploited” his role at Breast Cancer Now to redirect a payment intended for the charity to his own bank account.



Choudhury, of Hackney, north London, was jailed for two and a half years at the Royal Courts of Justice on Tuesday after pleading guilty to fraud and money laundering offences.

In August 2023, Choudhury, who worked in the charity’s finance team, intercepted a refund payment of £91,966.72 from The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust.



Using his work email account, Choudhury sent the trust the details of his personal bank account, on Breast Cancer Now headed paper, according to City of London Police.

Within weeks of receiving the payment, he used the stolen money to fund his wedding and honeymoon expenses.



He also purchased luxury items – including an Alexander Brown ring worth £14,000 – paid off his personal debts and withdrew cash, the force added.

Detective Constable Yusuf Meerza, of the fraud operations team at the City of London Police, said Choudhury “abused a position of trust” within the charity.



Dc Meerza added: “The generosity of donors enables charities such as Breast Cancer Now to support vital research and provide help to those affected by breast cancer.

“Choudhury’s actions betrayed that trust and placed charitable funds at risk for his own personal gain.”

In messages found on Choudhury’s phone during the police investigation, he described himself as “borderline broke” shortly before committing the offences, the force said.

Police also found evidence linking the stolen cash to payments Choudhury made to debt collection agencies, plane tickets to Qatar and transfers to relatives.

Some £42,866 was recovered from Choudhury’s account after it was frozen by his bank when suspicious activity was detected.



Choudhury was arrested in June last year after Breast Cancer Now reported him to the police.

A spokesperson for the charity said it takes the matter “extremely seriously” and has conducted a “thorough review” of its processes.

The spokesperson added: “People affected by breast cancer are at the heart of all we do.

“Through life-saving research, life-changing support and change-making campaigns, we’re changing the future of breast cancer, and we’re committed to upholding the highest standards to ensure all funds so generously donated to the charity help those affected by this devastating disease, as intended.

“Funds have been recovered and the charity has not experienced any financial loss.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Launched in 2015, Breast Cancer Now funds research into the disease, and offers sufferers opportunities to speak to specialist nurses, join support groups and access help and resources.

With the King as its royal patron, the charity has high-profile supporters, including broadcasters Lisa Snowdon and Julia Bradbury – who documented her own battle with breast cancer in a documentary released in 2022.

News.title: Ukraine oligarch reveals mistress spent month in coma & is only just talking again after ‘losing legs’ in Monaco bombing
News.content:
BOMBER’S VICTIM Ukraine oligarch reveals mistress spent month in coma & is only just talking again after ‘losing legs’ in Monaco bombing

THE girlfriend of a Ukrainian-born multimillionaire targeted in a Monaco bombing has started speaking again after suffering catastrophic injuries.

Property tycoon Vadym Ermolaev, his partner Anna Nasobina and their son, 13, were wounded when a bomb packed with bolts and pellets ripped through the entrance to the Sun Palace apartment building in June.



London-based lover Nasobina lost both legs in the blast and suffered serious chemical burns.

She was rushed to hospital in nearby Nice, where she remained critically ill.



Speaking from the luxury block where he was bombed, exiled tycoon Ermolaev told Ukrainska Pravda: “Anna spent a month in a coma.

“She is only now beginning to speak a little. She is only now beginning to move her arms. It was a powerful explosion.”



Their son suffered burns, a broken leg and injuries requiring skin grafts.

Moments before the terrifying explosion, Ermolaev recalled returning home from an impromptu meal at a waterfront cafe and swiping his magnetic key at the door.

The moment the magnet made contact a bomb stuffed with bolts exploded, ripping through the apartment.

“The enormous doors, which are impossible to lift, were ripped out by the explosion and shattered into splinters” he said.



“When it happened, I turned around and saw my son waving his bloodied hands. His hands, legs and everything else were covered in blood.”

Rumours are swirling as to who exactly co-ordinated the attack with the Ukrainian multimillionaire previously slamming his own country’s secret service for planting the booby-trapped backpack.

In July, Ermolaev said that there was “no doubt” that “serving officers of the main intelligence directorate of the military of defence of Ukraine” had organised the bombing.



Since the attack, he said that he and his partner were being threatened with ominous messages telling them to “keep quiet” and “think about their families”.

Ermolaev confessed he had no idea who was sending the chilling threats – but said he did not believe it was Volodymr Zelensky’s office.

Nonetheless, the property mogul, 58, has slammed the Nation Police investigations which he says have “begun slowing down”.

In a shcoking admission, the tycoon – who faces sanctions from Ukraine for operating his business in Russia-occupied Crimea – revealed he had visited Ukraine just two weeks before the bombing.

In a previously undisclosed secret visit he spent two days in Dnipro from May 16 – his first trip to Ukraine in three years.



Brushing off claims that the visit was linked to the attack, he said: “It was a private trip. I had not been there for a long time”.

Ermolaev claimed that CCTV in Monaco – where the device exploded – showed that the suspected bomber had been stalking the apartment from as early as April or May.

Single mother and Ukrainian national Anastasiia Berezovska, 39, had previously been accused of planting the explosive.

Captured on CCTV, the snake-tattooeed bomber can be seen dropping off a backpack at the luxury flat before fleeing the scene.

Just weeks later, Berezovska was found dead in a forest in Kyiv with four bullet wounds to the back of her head.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Two Ukrainian spies – Liuetnant Colonel Vladyslav Reut and security officer Vitalii Zhykovich – have been arrested for her murder.

News.title: Trump orders fresh wave of missile strikes on Iran & warns nation not to retaliate as US will ‘hit back harder’
News.content:
DON'S BLITZ Trump orders fresh wave of missile strikes on Iran & warns nation not to retaliate as US will ‘hit back harder’

DONALD Trump has unleashed a fresh round of strikes in a furious blitz on the Strait of Hormuz after Iran tried to litter the waterway with sea mines.

More than a dozen ballistic missiles have rained down on the region – targeting Iranian radar systems and military assets along the coastline.



The fiery onslaught comes in retaliation to Iran‘s weekend attacks in which they fired eight drones at a US air base in Jordan.

Late on Monday night the Islamic regime also bombed two supertankers travelling through the strait – all while attempting to litter the waterway with sea mines.



In a post on Truth Social, the president said that he was battering Iran in a “very justified attack” with strikes that are “large and powerful”.

He vowed that any retaliatory strikes from Iran will result in being “hit again at a much harder and higher level”.

In a final bit of scabre-rattling, Trump said: “It will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings and, when it is over, there will be very little left of the Islamic Republic of Iran!.”

Iranian state media have reported explosions on the country’s oil-rich Qeshm Island on the northern side of the strait.



Eruptions have also been recorded in the southern port cities of Bandar Abbas and Chabahar, said state-linked news outlet Nour News.

The US “will regret its attacks” a spokesperson for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps told Fars news agency.

The US Embassy in Qatar urged Americans currently in the Middle East to exercise “heightened vigilance and be aware of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions”.



It comes after the US president’s reopened the floodgates of war on an attack on Iran two days ago – the first strike in a month.

This latest round of bombings has quashed any hopes that the exchange of fire over the weekend might not escalate back into all-out war.

With tensions spiralling once again, the cost of crude oil has shot up by 4 per cent to $94 a barrel.

The US and Iran signed a peace deal back in June – but before the ink had dried the nations had resumed tit-for-tat strikes in the Middle East.

The ceasefire agreement officially ended on August 17 – and so far, no new deal has been struck between the warring nations.



Peace talks have churned to a standstill as Trump said in August: “They’re not going to make the kind of a deal that I feel is necessary.”

Trump had previously appeared to pivot from bombs to banks as he threatened to launch “economic D-Day” on Iran.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Last week the US President unleashed “Operation Economic Outcast” in which he planned to strangle Iran’s economy until they agreed to dismantle their nuclear programme.

Crippling sanctions will be also be levied onto any nation found to be propping up the tyrant regime.

News.title: Moment disgruntled worker smashes up boss’ Grade II-listed home & car with TRAFFIC CONE in row over docked wages
News.content:
THIS is the moment a disgruntled worker smashed up his boss’ Grade II-listed home with a traffic cone in a row over wages.

Lucasz Dabrowski, 27, was captured causing carnage at Abrar Mohammed’s house as he ransacked it with the cone and a claw hammer.



The footage shows him shattering the front bay windows before he entered the home with the road equipment.

Dabrowski then hurled the cone through another window before heading back outside to target his boss’ car.



The yob could be seen attacking the Hyundai i800 – shattering the back windows and leaving a trail of glass on the road.

Dabrowski caused £14,000 worth of damage in the attack on May 4 this year.



He pleaded guilty to two offences of criminal damage and one count of burglary.

Dabrowski also admitted assaulting a police constable after spitting at an officer following his arrest.



He has been jailed for 17 months and handed a two-year restraining order banning him from having any contact with Abrar.

Canterbury Crown Court heard he launched the attack after having money docked from his wages.

Dabrowski was then said to have “lost the plot” over his belief his employer, who was letting him stay at the home, had exploited him.

Just a few days earlier on May 1, police were called to the property after receiving a report that windows were being broken from inside the house.

His first rampage caused about £5,000 of damage and ended with police having to negotiate with him as he stood on scaffolding outside.



After he was arrested and released on bail, he returned three days later and went on the second wrecking spree.

News.title: Chinese antique bought for £1 at car boot sale turns out to be rare 600-year-old relic from Ming dynasty worth £10k
News.content:
JADE MY DAY Chinese antique bought for £1 at car boot sale turns out to be rare 600-year-old relic from Ming dynasty worth £10k

A RARE Chinese jade dog which is more than 600 years old could fetch up to £10,000 after it was bought for £1 at a car boot sale.

The animal, measuring 8.5cm long and made of the mottled black and green stone, was carved with its head turned back and tail and legs curled up.



The item is estimated to be from the early years of the Ming dynasty, made approximately between 1380 and 1420.

Auctioneer Charles Hanson said the dog, which was bought at a car boot sale just two months ago, has a “magical history”.



The dog is going on sale at Hansons Auctioneers in Etwall, Derbyshire, on Wednesday.

Mr Hanson said: “We always think we need to be at a car boot sale really early – six in the morning ‘wakey, wakey’.



“But one of our clients went to a car boot sale very late, getting towards midday, and left on a stall, in a box, was this fairly unassuming chap behind me.

“What we’ve got is what we might call an archaic seated recumbent dog in black and green jade. But it’s Chinese and it’s a really important late Song, early Ming.

“We believe this little dog to be probably late 14th, early 15th century and there’s many ways we’ve been able to confirm that.”

He added: “It’s an important Chinese jade and being picked up for £1 only about two months ago, we expect it ought to realise up to £10,000.



“The vendor had an idea it was jade. It’s the rarer jade in this green and black.

“Furthermore to that, the vendor had an inclination it might be old.

“It still shows what can be lost and found, and the art of uncovering treasure around the United Kingdom.”

Mr Hanson said jade was a “mystical, magical substance” in Chinese society and was believed to bring good fortune.

He said: “There is some scratching, but (it has) the condition of something, which if you imagine was made probably at our time of the Black Death, was made 200 years or 150 years before Henry VIII came on the throne.



“This dog has a magical history from China and it’s revered by the Chinese today who, as back then, adore jade and collect these hard stone animals.”

News.title: Ex-Labour minister and MP Phil Woolas left huge six-figure sum for his wife after death aged 66 earlier this year
News.content:
FINAL FORTUNE Ex-Labour minister and MP Phil Woolas left huge six-figure sum for his wife after death aged 66 earlier this year

FORMER Labour minister Phil Woolas left nearly half a million pounds in his will, The Sun can reveal.

Woolas, who served as immigration minister under Gordon Brown, died in March aged 66 after a battle with brain cancer.



The top Labour figure was infamously banned from Parliament in 2010 when a court found he had lied about his election opponent.

Documents obtained by The Sun show he left his estate to his wife Tracey Allen.



The couple’s West London home was also held in trust for their two sons after her death.

Court records show Woolas left an estate worth £446,000, which was reduced to £420,000 after debts and costs were deducted.

His will was signed in May 2021 and a grant was issued by the High Court last month.

In the five-page document, Woolas placed his share of his family home in Brentford into a protection trust.

It gives his widow the right to live there rent-free for life before it passes to sons Joshua and Jed in equal shares.

The ex-minister also asked to be cremated.



Woolas served as MP for Oldham East and Saddleworth between 1997 and 2010 and took ministerial jobs under both Tony Blair and Brown.

He lost the seat in December 2010 after an election court found he had knowingly lied about Lib Dem rival Elwyn Watkins in that year’s general election.

It meant he became the first MP to be disqualified from Parliament since 1911.

Woolas had won the seat by just 103 votes.

Labour won the resulting by-election but the scandal all but ended Woolas’s Westminster career as he was banned from office for three years.



After leaving politics, he ran his own political consultancy firm.

The former MP was also chairman of The Ace Centre, an Oldham charity supporting people with difficulties communicating, for more than 25 years.

Sir Tony Blair led tributes to his former minister, calling him “an outstanding member of the New Labour government” and “a greatly respected and admired colleague.”

Former Labour prime minister Gordon Brown also penned a tribute to Mr Woolas and said: “Phil Woolas was a brilliant MP, a highly-effective minister and a very generous and popular friend who fought a brave struggle against an incurable cancer and will be sorely missed.

“My thoughts are with his devoted wife Tracey and the whole family.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A statement attributed to his family and close friends announcing his death in March said: “For more than a year he battled the brain cancer, glioblastoma.

“He leaves his wife Tracey, his sons Josh and Jed and a new grandson, and many friends and former colleagues who will all miss him greatly.”

News.title: Andy Burnham accused of being ‘stuck in past’ after using first Commons speech to attack Thatcher and Brexit
News.content:
NEW PM Andy Burnham was accused of being stuck in the past today after using his first Commons speech to moan about Brexit and Margaret Thatcher.

The Labour leader said that “Britain is not where any of us would wish it to be” and blamed “a series of wrong turns in the 1980s” as well as the decision to leave the EU.



He faced MPs for the first time since entering No10 six weeks ago and embarking on a summer tour announcing relatively small cost of living giveaways.

But yesterday he faced a grilling from MPs on pressing issues including immigration, welfare and defence as Parliament returned from holiday.



Speaking at the dispatch box for the first time in 16 years, Mr Burnham said: “Britain is not where any of us would wish it to be. Things are not working as they should. Life is too expensive and too hard for too many.”

The former Manchester Mayor said his decade away from Westminster politics had given him a “clear diagnosis” of the source of the UK’s woes.

The PM took aim at the legacy of Ms Thatcher and her mass programme of privatisation as well as pulling out of the EU.

He said: “Political power was centralised, economic power privatised, the country deindustrialised, austerity followed, hollowing out councils and depriving them of the agency to act to reverse any of this.”

He added: “Then Brexit compounded the damage, ushering in a decade of low growth and stalled regeneration.

“Far from taking back control, the combination of these policies took control out of the hands of communities up and down Britain for 40 years, too many places have been drifting.”



Tory leader Kemi Badenoch attacked Mr Burnham for living in the past when he should be focused on the future.

She hit back: “The year is 2026 yet the prime minister said in his statement that everything has gone wrong since the 1980s, still complaining about Margaret Thatcher. I am 46 years old, I may not look it but I’m 46 years old.

“He is talking about a woman who became prime minister before I was born. He is living in the past and he wants to take us back to the 1970s.

“On this side of the House, we are for the future not the past. That is the difference between them and us.

“His ideas are all about more government control, more spending, more tax, more politicians.”



She blamed the £70billion of tax rises under Labour for the sluggish growth dogging the British economy.

Analysis By Martina Bet, Chief Political Correspondent ANDY Burnham made his first big speech to the Commons as Prime Minister. It should have been an easy ride. He spent the summer touring the country, promising to tackle voters’ biggest grievances, ease the cost-of-living squeeze and give families some much-needed “breathing space”. The TikToks have been slick. The promises have so far been quite cheap. And the King of the North has long been hailed as one of Labour’s smoothest communicators. His MPs should have been bouncing off the green benches.

After all, they have all just returned from their summer holidays having successfully knifed Sir Keir Starmer and installed the man many of them hope will save their seats at the next election. But the atmosphere in the Commons was strangely muted. Some Labour MPs were texting, others were chatting among themselves, smiles were in short supply and the cheers hardly threatened to bring the roof down. To be fair, even Burnham was making their job difficult. A politician who prides himself on talking straight chose his first statement to introduce Britain to a “triple helix approach” to economic development. It means bringing together “business, academia, and government”.

Try chanting that from the back benches. “Triple helix! Triple helix!” No, thought not. Perhaps Labour MPs were simply conserving their energy. And that’s because beyond the glossy videos and summer honeymoon sits an autumn in-tray from hell.

This evening, Justice secretary Alex Norris made a statement to the Commons announcing a crackdown on the controversial prisoner early release scheme.

He said certain groups of prisoners, including those convicted of manslaughter, will no longer be eligible.

Foreign criminals will also be deported in a bid to tackle the prison overcrowding crisis.

“Next year, we will begin removing foreign national offenders serving determinate sentences immediately after sentencing,” he said.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

He added: “If you break our laws, if you abuse Britain’s hospitality, we will permanently remove you.”

Mr Norris also said “work will begin immediately” to bring forward laws to end IPP (imprisonment for public protection) sentences but conceded “it will take time to get this right”.

News.title: Banking VP stabbed to death by knife-wielding woman in Times Square just after her 2nd wedding anniversary is pictured
News.content:
A VP at Bank of America has been pictured as the victim of a knife-wielding woman in yesterday’s Times Square rampage.

Erin Piacenti, 32, of Chester, New Jersey, was fatally stabbed in the horror attack on Monday.



Erin worked as the Vice President of Business Selection and Conflicts at the bank, sources told The New York Post.

She had just celebrated her second wedding anniversary.



She graduated from the University of Pennsylvania in 2016 and from Fordham Law School in 2021, according to LinkedIn.

Bank of America wrote in a tribute to Erin: “We are shocked and deeply saddened by the tragic loss of our colleague. ​

“She was a valued teammate who will be greatly ​missed.

“Our hearts go out to her family and ⁠all of her loved ones.”



The suspect also wounded an elderly man in the violent attack before being shot dead by cops at the scene.

Chilling footage showed Pamela Cisneros, 49, refusing to drop two blades during a hectic confrontation with New York cops before they opened fire.

Police used tasers twice to try and stop the suspect before they fatally shot her, authorities said.



Just minutes before the chaotic standoff, mayhem erupted when Cisneros stabbed a 68-year-old man and Erin in the space of about 20 seconds.

Both were stabbed in the abdomen with kitchen knives.

Eyewitnesses said Cisneros had been threatening tourists in the packed square before stabbing the two victims.

Cops described the suspect as “emotionally disturbed”.

Cisneros is said to have stabbed the older man before going on to kill bank VP Erin.



Police said the suspect fled the scene and raced north, being met by cops at Seventh Avenue West and 42nd and 43rd Streets.

She charged at police and was shot.

Cisneros was then rushed to hospital in critical condition but later succumbed to her injuries.

The attack was initially reported as a knifepoint robbery, but police now believe the woman had no clear motive, police said.

Her brother revealed that Cisneros had struggled with her mental health for decades.



Patrick Peralta, 59, told the New York Post: “She never showed any aggressiveness or being violent. I don’t know what happened.”

He said she may have been diagnosed with bipolar and received monthly injections to treat her mental illness.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Patrick said: “I think maybe she stopped the injection she was getting and that caused her to act the way she was.”

News.title: Andy Burnham LIVE: PM blasts Brexit and austerity for '10 years of stalled growth'
News.content:
Starmer's resignation statement in full

In a statement issued on X, Sir Keir Starmer said it was the right time to “hand the baton over to a successor”.

He said: “Over the summer, I have had time to reflect and consider my future. I have decided that now is the right time to step down as MP for Holborn and St Pancras and hand the baton over to a successor.

“It’s been an honour and privilege to represent the best constituency in the country since taking over from the great Frank Dobson 11 years ago. But it is now time to step aside and focus on other issues: international affairs including defence, security, trade and technology in a fast changing world. I will also continue working with others as I have done over many decades to tackle violence against women and girls.

“As I do that, I will always remain immensely proud to have represented the place Vic, the kids and I call home.

“I look back with pride on what my constituency team and I have delivered in Holborn and St Pancras since 2015 and I thank all those who I was privileged to work with on so many issues of local concern: affordable housing projects, delivering first class education and tackling youth violence through our Camden Youth Safety Taskforce.

“I want to thank my CLP team who have always stood firmly by me, and given me the support I needed as I stood for leader of the Labour Party and then as I took my party from political, moral and financial ruin to an historic landslide election win in 2024 and two years as prime minister when we stabilised the economy, rebuilt our public services, invested record amounts in our defence and security, began lifting hundreds of thousands of children out of poverty and transformed Britain’s reputation with international partners.

“I want to thank my constituency staff who, throughout all those 11 years, have worked tirelessly on casework and helped me do my utmost to serve the people of Holborn and St Pancras. I could not have done this job without them.

“There will now be a process to appoint my successor ahead of a by-election. Whoever is lucky enough to become the Labour candidate here will have my full support and backing and I will continue to give my full support to the Prime Minister and this Labour government.

“Keir Starmer.”

News.title: Galopin Des Champs tragedy as dual Cheltenham Gold Cup hero dies five days after retirement
News.content:
Galopin Des Champs tragedy as dual Cheltenham Gold Cup hero dies five days after retirement

The 10-year-old who won the Cheltenham Gold Cup in 2023 and 2024 and finished second in 2025 for trainer Willie Mullins suffered a fatal injury in a field

View 2 Images Galopin Des Champs (Image: Niall Carson/PA Wire)

Legendary dual Cheltenham Gold Cup winner Galopin Des Champs has died just five days after he retired

‌



The 10-year-old became one of the most popular jumpers of recent times, winning 12 races at Grade 1 level, including the most prestigious race of all, the Gold Cup at the 2023 and 2024 Cheltenham Festivals.

‌



He attempted to join an elite group of three-time winners of the big race in 2025 only to finish second to Inothewayurthinkin and missed the race this year due to an injury setback. He last raced at Leopardstown in February in the Paddy Power Irish Gold Cup where he finished a below par third behind stablemate Fact To File.

‌



Trainer involved in extraordinary betting coup suspended after winner fails drugs test READ MORE :

Value Scope Extra: Steve Jones marks your card on the big races ahead READ MORE :

But last week Willie Mullins announced he would not race again.

He said: "We took a collective decision to retire Galopin Des Champs at his age because we felt he could not do himself justice at the level he was used to.

“He retires a good, sound horse who will hopefully have a good second career as a sport horse."

‌



Galopin Des Champs was to spend his retirement with former stable jockey Ruby Walsh, whose daughter was going retrain the horse.

But on Tuesday, Walsh had to break the terrible news that he had passed away as a result of a serious injury.

View 2 Images Galopin Des Champs in Cheltenham action (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

In a statement, Walsh said: "Sadly, Galopin Des Champs suffered an injury in his field this morning and could not be saved.

"He was checked a few times throughout the morning, but late in the morning when I went to get him for exercise, I found him with a severe injury, high up on his near front leg. He was attended to by our vets immediately, but X-rays revealed extensive, unrepairable damage.

"He was a fabulous horse whose short time with us has left lots of broken hearts, but none more so than those of Grey, Audrey and Sarah Turley, and Adam Connolly, who looked after him for so long. He will be sadly missed."

News.title: Harper Beckham's birthday message to Romeo saying 'I'll always look up to you' but Brooklyn silent
News.content:
Harper Beckham's birthday message to Romeo saying 'I'll always look up to you' but Brooklyn silent

Harper Beckham has sent a sweet birthday message to her big brother Romeo but Brooklyn is yet to acknowledge his sibling publicly amid their infamous family feud

View 4 Images Harper Beckham has sent a sweet birthday message to her big brother Romeo (Image: Matt Baron/BEI/Shutterstock)

Harper Beckham has sent a sweet birthday message to her big brother Romeo. The second-eldest son of David and Victoria Beckham celebrated his 24th birthday on Tuesday and his sister Harper, 14, made sure to acknowledge him on social media.

‌



She wrote on Instagram: "Happy birthday @romeobeckham. Today is all about celebrating you, and I hope you know just how loved and appreciated you are. You'll always be one of the biggest role models in my life, and I'll forever look up to you and everything you are.

‌



"I'm so lucky to have you as my brother, and I genuinely don't know what I'd do without you. Thank you for always being someone I can look up to and be proud of.

‌



"I hope this year brings you so much happiness love and everything you've been wishing for, because you truly deserve it all. Have the best birthday Romeo Love you always. Happy birthday, Romeo!"

4 View 4 Images Harper posted this image onto her Instagram (Image: romeobeckham/Instagram) 4 View 4 Images Romeo turned 24 on Tuesday (Image: PA)

‌



Meanwhile, David and Victoria each marked the occasion by sharing a series of throwback snaps to their Instagram pages. Former Spice Girl Victoria said: "We all love you so much!"

Football legend David said: "Happy birthday mate, we love you so much and I'm so proud of you for all you are as a person, sweet kind and just an amazing young man. Love you so so much, have the best day ever, you deserve it."

Cruz Beckham also made sure to send his brother a shoutout, as he said: ""happy birthday man i love you xx," alongside a photo of them both as children.

‌



There was a notable since from Brooklyn Beckham, who, at the time of writing has not issued a public statement regarding his brother's birthday. Earlier this year, Brooklyn released a now-viral social media statement explaining why he had chosen distance himself from his family.

View 4 Images Brooklyn appears to be the only Beckham child to not have publicly acknowledged Romeo on his birthday (Image: Samir Hussein/WireImage)

Brooklyn accused his parents of manipulating his life, trying to sabotage his relationship with wife Nicola and damaging his mental health in their quest to keep 'brand Beckham' moving along.

‌



He wrote: "I have been silent for years and made every effort to keep these matters private. Unfortunately, my parents and their team have continued to go to the press, leaving me with no choice but to speak for myself and tell the truth about only some of the lies that have been printed.

"I do not want to reconcile with my family. I'm not being controlled, I'm standing up for myself for the first time in my life. For my entire life, my parents have controlled narratives in the press about our family. The performative social media posts, family events and inauthentic relationships have been a fixture of the life I was born into.

"Recently, I have seen with my own eyes the lengths that they'll go through to place countless lies in the media, mostly at the expense of innocent people, to preserve their own façade. But I believe the truth always comes out."

News.title: Brit pulled alive from rubble in Nepal almost one week after devastating floods
News.content:
Brit pulled alive from rubble in Nepal almost one week after devastating floods

The unnamed British survivor was among 119 people pulled alive from mud and debris after catastrophic floods struck Nepal and neighbouring China.

View 4 Images A British man has been rescued alive nearly a week after devastating flash floods in Nepal. (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

A British man has been rescued alive nearly a week after devastating flash floods killed more than 1,000 people across Nepal and neighbouring China.

‌



He was among 119 people rescued from mud and debris during search and rescue operations in Nepal on Tuesday afternoon.

‌



The survivor had been among 33 British nationals reported missing in Nepal, while a further 15 were listed as missing in Tibet two days ago, bringing the total across both areas to 48.

‌



View 4 Images A British man has been rescued alive nearly a week after devastating flash floods in Nepal. (Image: NEPAL ARMY/AFP via Getty Images)

An army spokesperson said 118 Nepalese people had been rescued, including 44 women and 74 men, along with one British man.

A UK rapid deployment team arrived in Nepal on Saturday to help British nationals and their families. Specially trained crisis response staff are working with the British embassy and local authorities.

‌



More than 4,500 people remain missing overall following the catastrophic floods, according to reports, as rescue teams continue searching across the region.

View 4 Images Rescue teams continue searching for thousands of people still missing in Nepal. (Image: YONHAP/EPA/Shutterstock)

The scale of the death toll is also creating difficulties for authorities trying to identify and return victims to their families. Only 20 of those killed have reportedly so far been reunited with loved ones.

‌



Those reported missing from Britain include a 13-year-old girl and a 14-year-old boy.

An NHS nurse and a Hindu priest from south London who had been leading a tour of the region are also among those unaccounted for, while an 18-year-old from Surrey who had recently completed his A-levels is feared missing.

View 4 Images A British man has been rescued alive nearly a week after devastating flash floods in Nepal. (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Article continues below

Hundreds of hydropower workers are also among those missing, with around 933 believed to have been trapped across 11 projects in Nepal’s hydroelectric network.

Around 21,000 people have joined rescue efforts in Nepal as teams attempt to reach those stranded in hills, settlements, river areas and tunnels blocked by huge amounts of mud and debris.

Foreign teams have been assisting local rescuers at the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project, while rescue workers have also been battling deep mud as they try to gain access to other sites.

News.title: OAP, 83, guilty of murdering nephew in knife attack over inheritance row
News.content:
OAP, 83, guilty of murdering nephew in knife attack over inheritance row

Alan Wotton, 83, was convicted of stabbing his nephew 65-year-old Andrew Avery to death following an argument over his inheritance

View 3 Images Andrew Avery, 83, was found guilty of murdering his nephew after he stabbed him to death over a £20,000 inheritance row (Image: Solent News)

An 83-year-old man has been found guilty of the murder of his nephew whom he stabbed to death before setting fire to his own home following an argument over his inheritance.

‌



Alan Wotton was convicted following a trial at Portsmouth Crown Court of killing 65-year-old Andrew Avery at the house in Exmouth Road, Gosport, Hampshire, on November 29 2024.

‌



He had previously pleaded guilty to arson being reckless as to whether life is endangered.

‌



View 3 Images Alan Wotton, who has a heart condition and wears a hearing aid, stabbed his nephew 11 times before setting fire to his late sister's home where he had been staying. (Image: CPS/Solent News)

A Crown Prosecution Service spokesman said: “Andrew Avery had been helping Wotton move out of the property following its sale and had arranged alternative accommodation for him.

“On the day he was due to leave, Wotton attacked his nephew with a kitchen knife, inflicting 11 stab wounds. Mr Avery sadly died from those injuries.

‌



“Wotton then deliberately started fires inside the property before leaving Mr Avery in the smoke-filled house. Fire investigators identified three separate seats of fire and concluded they had been started deliberately.”

View 3 Images The house was destroyed in the blaze (Image: CPS/Solent News)

The spokesman said that Wotton had claimed to have acted in self-defence but said the prosecution had proven that he was the aggressor following a “dispute over inheritance money and his impending move from the property”.

‌



Simon Clark, senior crown prosecutor, said: “Alan Wotton carried out a ruthless attack on his nephew before setting fire to the property.

“The prosecution case drew together compelling witness accounts, forensic evidence and admissions made by Wotton himself in the immediate aftermath of the murder.

“Andrew Avery had been helping his uncle and arranging for his future. Instead, he lost his life in a horrific and wholly unnecessary act of violence.

Article continues below

“Our thoughts remain with Andrew’s family and loved ones and we hope today’s verdict provides them with some measure of justice.”

Wotton will be sentenced on October 22.

News.title: Mass burials carried out across flood-hit Nepal as search for missing Brits continues
News.content:
Mass burials carried out across flood-hit Nepal as search for missing Brits continues

Among the 48 Brits still unaccounted for across Nepal and China is Hindu priest Nabhi Nandan Das, 64, who was leading a pilgrimage tour when the floods hit on August 26

View 5 Images Across Nepal, the authorities have been forced to dig mass graves after 900 people were killed in devastating flash floods (Image: Getty Images)

Mass burials are being carried out across flood-hit Nepal as the death toll reached more than 1,000 people.

‌



Desperate efforts to trace thousands of people were continuing as Nepal's disaster agency said 1,003 deaths had been counted there, with 3,916 people missing, including 583 foreign nationals. Among the 48 Brits still unaccounted for across Nepal and China is a Hindu priest from south London who was leading a pilgrimage.

‌



Nabhi Nandan Das, 64, who runs the Sanatan Mandir and Community Centre in Coulsdon, was leading a pilgrimage tour, which included 11 British nationals, for Alpine Eco Trek when a glacier collapse triggered devastating the floods hit on August 26. The tour group was on a nine-day tour to Mount Kailash in Nepal and had just crossed into China.

‌



View 5 Images Nabhi Das, from south London, had been leading a tour group at the time of the floods (Image: Facebook)

Nepal flood disaster survivor shares details of miraculous escape READ MORE :

Final happy photo of Brits on Nepal tour - then they were gone READ MORE :

Mr Das' family have not heard from him since he sent them a message the day before the disaster. Dee Shah said the priest, who is her mother's cousin, has been leading pilgrimages in the area for more than 20 years. She said: "He went out there with 16 others and on the day it happened they had crossed the Nepal border into China.

"I think they think they're now just going to get a body - but they want to find the body as it's been too long not having a body. I think they just want to get closure."

‌



She said Mr Das' wife and son are now in Nepal, but have not yet got permission to cross the border into China. They have provided DNA to assist with identification, she added. Ms Shah has launched a GoFundMe fundraiser, which has raised more than £10,000 and will be used to help with the family's travel costs and assist search and rescue teams.

View 5 Images Surrounded by razor wire, mass burials have taken place in a jungle on the outskirts of Kathmandu (Image: Sanjit Pariyar/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

She said money may also be used towards funerals of those missing on the tour group and any remaining will be donated to the Red Cross in Nepal. "The reason I started the fundraiser was because of a lack of communication from the Foreign Office," Ms Shah said.

‌



"Every time we've been ringing them they just say they don't know anything further - we've been ringing every few hours but being told there is no further information."

Rescue teams with search dogs continued to search through mud, rocks and debris on the border with Nepal and China for thousands of people still missing following the catastrophic floods.

View 5 Images Trenches were also dug in Chitwan, Nepal, so the authorities can bury those killed in the tragedy (Image: AP Photo/Nisha Shrestha)

‌



In Kathmandu, police worked in heavy rain to begin burying dozens of bodies in multiple trenches next to a forested area. Barbed wire was erected around the site, while blue numbered markers identified the graves of people whose names were not yet known.

Authorities in Nepal have been burying bodies in temporary graves until they can be identified. They are preserving DNA samples, photographing distinguishing facial features and recording other identifying details. Each body is assigned a reference number to help families identify and claim the remains later.

Rescue teams are also working to assist survivors in areas where roads and other transportation routes have been damaged or cut off. The immediate priority remains finding at least 900 workers who are missing from 12 hydropower projects damaged by the flash floods, about 500 of whom are believed to be trapped inside tunnels.

‌



View 5 Images Massive rescue efforts have been launched to recover trapped tunnel workers (Image: Prime Minister Secretariat, Nepal/AFP via Getty Images)

Brigadier General Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal's army spokesperson, said teams assisted by foreign experts were working at several hydropower projects to reach people trapped in blocked tunnels. Visuals released by the army showed rescue teams entering dark, debris-filled tunnels, wading through mud and water and climbing over rocks as they searched for signs of life.

At the Upper Trishuli 3A site, rescuers broke through into the upper part of a mud-swamped tunnel, pumping air inside, then using drilling and excavator machines to dig down. A spokesperson said: "When members of the team descended using ropes and called out to those inside, there was no response."

‌



Sita Pandey, whose husband Jiblal was working in one of the tunnels, told local media: "I still have a 50 per cent hope that he is alive because there is an oxygen system inside." She revealed that she last spoke to him on Wednesday morning, hours before the flood hit.

Desperately hoping that he is found quickly, she added: "We can understand that the rescue operation is technically complex. But we cannot accept delays. Our people are inside there. For us, every second counts."

Bimal Sharma, a helicopter pilot who has been flying rescue missions since the disaster began, said he was shocked to see the devastation in Timure, a border town close to Tibet that he has known for years.

Article continues below

He said: "It felt like I was flying over an entirely different landscape." At least 11,814 people have been rescued so far, according to Nepalese authorities.

News.title: Met Office reveals summer 2026 UK's hottest on record as horror heat driven by climate change
News.content:
Met Office reveals summer 2026 UK's hottest on record as horror heat driven by climate change

Weather forecasters have released provisional figures indicating the average temperature for the months of June, July and August blew past previous records by 0.4C

View 7 Images Summer 2026 is provisionally the hottest on record (Image: Amer Ghazzal/Shutterstock)

Summer 2026 was the warmest in the UK since records began nearly 150 years ago, according to new provisional figures released by the Met Office.

‌



The UK's national weather agency found that the country warmed to an average of 16.5C in June, July and August, a significant 0.4C warmer than the previous record, set just last year. The data collected by the agency, which started collating annual temperature records in 1884, means the top six warmest summers on record have all occurred this century, including three this decade: 2026 in first place, followed by 2025, 2018, 2006, 2003 and 2022.

‌



The weather has been compounded by climate change, making this year's "remarkable" searing heat a "one in nine year event", and devastating consequences like droughts and wildfires more likely in the years to come.

‌



UK weather maps show 1C chill with every single county to plunge lower than 10C READ MORE :

Brits rock up to beautiful beach only to find 'hellish' nightmare crammed with thousands READ MORE :

View 7 Images Vast tracts of the country were left completely parched by the severe lack of rainfall this summer (Image: Maureen McLean/Shutterstock)

Summer this year was characterised by several days' worth of sky-high nearly 40C temperatures split across five distinct heatwaves and record low rainfall. Figures from the agency revealed that England and Wales had their driest Julys on record, and southern England the driest month ever recorded since 1836.

Just one month prior, the agency released a rare red alert for extreme heat as temperatures peaked at 38C in Lingwood, Norfolk, a new record high for the month.

‌



The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) estimates these extreme conditions estimated in 2,877 deaths across England in May and June alone. The latest heatwave struck in mid-August and baked other parts of the nation, inching upwards of 38C in Kew Gardens, where highs reached 38.1C on August 13.

View 7 Images The extreme dry weather produced kindling for wildfires across the UK (Image: PA Wire)

The mercury readings for the day were the hottest of the year, and made 2026 the first year to see three separate days where temperatures exceeded 37C.

‌



Met Office head of climate attribution, Dr Mark McCarthy, said: “The summer of 2026 has been remarkable and is an example of the extremes we can expect to see more frequently as a consequence of human induced climate change.

“Our analysis shows a summer like the one we’ve just experienced is now around 130 times more likely because of climate change. In a climate unaffected by human emissions of greenhouse gases, a summer like this would be exceptionally unlikely – one in over 1,000 years."

View 7 Images Large wildfires caused the destruction of several homes in Stoke-on-Trent (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



“In our current climate, which is changing because of the effect of burning of fossil fuels, we should now expect this to be roughly a one in nine year event.”

The punishing heat and lack of rainfall meant wildfires were common across the UK. A blaze in the Cairngorms mountain range in Scotland that started in mid-July burned for more than a month across 10 square miles of moorland and forestry, while a fire on hills above Blaenavon in south Wales started in late July and continued for several weeks.

More recently, 19 homes in Stourbridge were destroyed by wildfires in mid-August. Fire and rescue services in England and Wales had responded to 1,132 wildfires so far this year as of August 16, surpassing the 1,017 total for the whole of 2025, according to the National Fire Chiefs Council.

‌



View 7 Images Armned forces members were called in to help with firefighting efforts (Image: Cpl Christian P Delice/MOD/SWNS)

Elsewhere, the Met Office weather station at Wisley in Surrey recorded 62 consecutive days with no rain, while those at Heathrow Airport in London and Odiham in Hampshire clocked up dry spells that lasted 56 days.

Responding to the provisional figures, Katie White, Minister for Climate Transition, said: “Our hottest summer ever is a brutal reminder that we’re not waiting for climate change to arrive in Britain, we’re living in the middle of it. With kids too hot to sleep, families worrying about older relatives, farmers watching fields dry out, and firefighters and our Armed Forces battling wildfires, we’ve all woken up to a reality none of us wants for the people and places we love.

‌



“That makes us more determined to act, with some of the biggest and boldest action in a generation to electrify our economy and tackle climate change with clean energy made in Britain."

View 7 Images Severe droughts left massive reservoirs unnaturally depleted (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

“We’re seizing the opportunity to upgrade Britain, backing our best scientists, entrepreneurs and technologies to make us happier, healthier and wealthier.” The persistent dry weather and extreme heat of the past few months continue to have an impact on the UK, despite recent rainfall.

‌



Most of England and all of Wales remain officially in drought, the exceptions being the North East, North West and Yorkshire. Bristol Water last week became the latest company to announce a hosepipe ban, meaning around 30 million people in England now have restrictions on their use of water.

Reservoir storage in England currently stands at 60%, 18 percentage points below the average for this time of year, with nine reservoirs classed by the Environment Agency as having exceptionally low levels. These include Wimbleball and Clatworthy reservoirs in Somerset, where storage is currently 37% and 40% respectively, Ardingley in West Sussex (44%) and Hanningfield in Essex (49%).

View 7 Images Rain has fallen for the first time in months across some areas over the last two weeks (Image: Katy Blackwood/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Article continues below

No droughts have been declared in Scotland or Northern Ireland, though two areas in south-west Scotland have “significant scarcity” of water, according to the Scottish Environment Protection Agency.

The National Drought Group continues to meet weekly to coordinate action and monitor risks across the country. Earlier this month, the Government announced a £65 million package to support farmers, who have reported their earliest harvest in 20 years, with yields impacted by the intense heat stress and dry weather.

News.title: Brits taking more business trips than pre-pandemic - but it's not all bad
News.content:
Brits taking more business trips than pre-pandemic - but it's not all bad

A new study suggests one in four workers are travelling more for business than before the pandemic, with many embracing the new 'bleisure' trend.

View 2 Images Business travel is back on the rise (Image: Getty Images)

A quarter of workers are now travelling more for business than they did before the pandemic, research has revealed. A study of 2,000 adults who have previously travelled for work discovered 18% have undertaken 12 or more business trips in the past year.

‌



During that period, the busiest months for travel were May, September and April, with the average employer willing to splash out £165 for accommodation. Meanwhile, £68 was the average daily allowance for meals and transport.

‌



The research was commissioned by Hotels.com, which has introduced a new business travel experience through its app to make work trips quicker and simpler to arrange.

‌



The app allows business travellers to save work-trip preferences, locate business-ready hotels, rebook favoured stays and earn rewards on corporate trip.

View 2 Images Workers are now embracing having to travel and visit cities like New York and London (Image: Getty Images)

The study also forms part of the global marketplace's Booked for Business report, which discovered 48% of workers believe the finest business travel destinations combine work and leisure, reflecting what it describes as "the growing importance of 'bleisure' travel".

‌



According to those surveyed, cities London, New York and Paris epitomise this 'bleisure' travel trend the most, making them the optimal destinations for work-related travel.

Business travellers are also placing greater emphasis on the benefits they receive when travelling for their jobs – with 26% revealing they make a hotel stay "great."

These include a complimentary breakfast (51%), room upgrades (32%) and flexible check-in (26%).

Article continues below

But when it comes to completing the job, 57% said access to high-speed Wi-Fi is a crucial priority.

Melanie Fish, travel expert and spokesperson for Hotels.com, said : "Business travel is no longer just about getting from one meeting to the next. Travellers want a hotel and destination that can keep up with both sides of their personality.

From high-speed Wi-Fi and an early breakfast before a big presentation to a great location and a comfortable place to unwind afterwards."

News.title: UK long-term borrowing costs highest since 1998 ahead of October Budget
News.content:
Long-term government borrowing costs have risen to a 28-year high, putting further pressure on Prime Minister Andy Burnham ahead of his first Budget next month.

The yield on a 30-year gilt â a loan to the British government â rose to 5.89% on Tuesday, the highest since 1998.

Borrowing costs in the US, Japan and Europe have hit similar highs in recent days, reflecting investors' concerns about inflation, state borrowing levels and spending levels by large tech companies on AI.

Burnham told the House of Commons his government's "bedrock", as it seeks to tackle the cost-of-living crisis, will be "fiscal responsibility".

All of those factors will make the Budget process trickier for Burnham, who on Tuesday addressed MPs for the first time as prime minister, and his Chancellor John Healey.

Burnham told the House of Commons the economy and the cost of living were "the biggest issues facing the country".

Higher borrowing costs will reduce the amount of headroom the government has against its self-imposed fiscal rules, limiting the amount Healey can spend on consumer-friendly measures to ease the cost of living.

Despite the squeezed public finances, Burnham said said he would bring about "more substantial change" to ease living costs.

"Britain is not where any of us would wish it to be," he added.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused Burnham of "living in the past".

"His diagnosis is completely wrong," she told the House of Commons. "His theory of growth is completely wrong. He thinks that if Government spends more money, we will all get richer.

"That is not how this works."

The chancellor has previously said he will stick to a set of fiscal rules imposed by his predecessor Rachel Reeves that restrict borrowing. These rules are designed to help markets have clarity about the path of borrowing.

The more that is forecast to be spent on interest payments, the more likely that there will be a squeeze on spending or some form of tax rise to meet these rules.

On top of that, higher government rates can feed through to higher business and household borrowing costs, and so weigh on the economy.

Burnham was already facing a tough balancing act with taxing and spending, due to pressures on defence and the cost of living.

As well as the rise to 30-year gilt yields, the yield on the benchmark 10-year gilt rose to 5.22% on Tuesday. This is its highest rate since June 2008, at the height of the global financial crisis.

Gilt yields move counter to the value of the bonds, meaning their prices fall when yields rise.

News.title: Keir Starmer announces he is standing down as MP
News.content:
Former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer has announced he is to stand down as an MP to focus on a role in international affairs.

The move will trigger a by-election in the London seat of Holborn and St Pancras, long a Labour stronghold, which he has represented since 2015.

Sir Keir, who left Downing Street in July, had previously said he would stay on as an MP until the next UK general election, which is not due until 2029.

But in a surprise statement hours before his successor Andy Burnham made his debut in the House of Commons, he said he was resigning to work on issues such as international affairs and violence against women and girls.

Paying tribute to his predecessor, Burnham highlighted Sir Keir's work with Ukraine and the Hillsborough Law drawn up under his government to improve the accountability of public officials, which is going through Parliament.

"He has given this country a lifetime of public service, particularly for those fighting for justice," he added.

"His leadership took our party from one of its worst defeats to its best victories and created a platform to change this country for the better. We will use it well, and we wish his family the very best for the future."

Announcing his resignation, Sir Keir told the Camden New Journal, external it had been a "huge honour and privilege" to represent the London constituency for 11 years, ending weeks of speculation about whether he would remain an MP.

He added he was ready to "pass the baton to a successor", telling the newspaper it was the "right time" for him to leave Parliament.

He said: "I will now focus on other things and that will be international affairs including defence, security, trade and technology in a fast-changing world.

"I will also continue, as I have done for a long time now with others, to work on combating violence against women and girls; that is an issue that matters to me hugely.

"It's work I started before I became an MP and it's work I'm keen to continue after I'm an MP. So international affairs on the one hand, and continuing my work on violence against women and girls on the other."

Sir Keir became prime minister after winning a landslide majority at the 2024 election, but quit No 10 after pressure from Labour MPs to stand aside.

News.title: Watch: Norway's new king takes oath as mourners pay respects to his late father
News.content:
Norway's Haakon VIII has sworn an oath before parliament in Oslo in the first major step of his reign as King.

During Tuesday's ceremony, parliament also held a minute's silence for Haakon's father, the late King Harald V, who died on Friday.

Haakon's wife, Queen Mette-Marit, was absent from the formalities as she continues to recover from a lung transplant.

Following the ceremony, mourners began paying their respects at the late King's coffin, which is lying in state at the Royal Palace until 8 September.

News.title: Baby girl who died at Sheffield house was stabbed, police say
News.content:
A newborn baby girl who was discovered fatally injured at a house in Sheffield died as a result of stab wounds, police have said.

The baby was found at a house on Holywell Heights in the Wincobank area on Sunday morning, after police were called to reports of concern for her safety.

South Yorkshire Police said despite the best efforts of police and paramedics, the baby died at the scene.

Seven people aged between 15 and 37 were arrested on suspicion of her murder. Two of them, aged 26 and 37, were later bailed, but police confirmed on Tuesday a warrant had been obtained to extend time in custody for the remaining five as inquiries continued.

Det Ch Insp Tom Woodward, leading the investigation, said: "We recognise this is deeply distressing for those who would have loved to have a chance to love this baby girl, for the emergency services who responded and for the community who will inevitably be shocked by this incident.

"Everyone involved in responding to this tragedy - from the first officers and paramedics on the scene to the detectives now leading the investigation - has felt the profound impact of this investigation."

He added: "Our commitment to this little girl is unwavering. We will confront every difficult and distressing challenge and pursue every line of inquiry with determination and care to secure justice for her.

"We know the local community will hold her in their thoughts and support us as we work through this complex investigation."

A South Yorkshire Police spokesperson said officers were continuing their investigations in the Holywell Heights area and asked anyone with information which might be useful to contact them.

News.title: US launches more strikes on Iran as state media reports explosions
News.content:
American forces resumed strikes against Iran on Tuesday, US Central Command said in a statement.

It accused the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of "recent attempted attacks" against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and "American service members deployed to the region".

Centcom said US forces began striking IRGC targets at 12:00 ET (16:00 GMT). Iran state media reported the country's deputy governor for security as saying four projectiles had hit the counties of Chabahar and Konarak.

The IRGC said the US would regret the strikes, as US President Donald Trump warned that Iran would be hit again at "a much harder and higher level" if it retaliated.

The attack follows the first known US strikes on Iran since late July earlier this week, when forces attacked two rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait.

Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency reported that several explosions were also heard on Qeshm Island on Tuesday, as well as Konarak and Bandar Abbas.

Donald Trump confirmed the "large and powerful" strikes, which he said were in response to Iran shooting eight missiles at a US military base in Jordan, adding the country had "failed" at adding sea mines to the Strait.

Regarding his threat of a further attack in the case of Iranian retaliation, he added: "It will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings and, when it is over, there will be very little left of the Islamic Republic of Iran."

IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi said that severe punishment awaited the US and the country would regret the new attacks.

News.title: Family mourn 'deeply loved' girl killed in Middlesbrough fire
News.content:
The family of a seven-year-old girl killed in a house fire said their lives had been changed forever by her "devastating loss".

Valentina Foster died alongside her aunt Natalie McDonald, 34, in the blaze at Grangetown, near Middlesbrough, in the early hours of 26 August. A man has been charged with their murders.

In a tribute, the youngster's parents said their daughter would "always be in our hearts, and her memory will live with us forever".

"She was deeply loved and will be missed beyond words by her family, friends, and everyone whose life she touched," they said.

"Our lives have changed forever, and we are struggling to come to terms with this devastating loss."

They added she would be "forever missed" by her brothers and sisters.

News.title: Spaces in male prisons fall to lowest level of year, sources say
News.content:
An investment of Â£110m, which will come from existing budgets, will be used to convert unused office space, laundry rooms and storage space into cells, the MoJ said.

The justice secretary told the BBC prisoners being released early did not mean "freedom" and victims would have a say in restrictions placed on those criminals.

Asked where clothes would be washed if laundry rooms were converted into cells, Norris told BBC Breakfast: "Of course we're going to make sure that the prisons can still function properly.

"This is a creative look, as I say, around our estate and being able to use some space that we can re-prioritise."

Norris said he suspected the number of extra prison spaces created from freeing up existing space within prisons would be "landing somewhere in the middle" of 200 and 900.

But the chairman of the Prison Officers' Association, Mark Fairhurst, said: "You can create as much additional space as you like, and build as many new prisons as you like, but where are the staff coming from to supervise people? Nobody wants to be a prison officer anymore."

Prisons in England and Wales are running at 97% capacity.

Under the early release scheme some 4,500 prisoners are now expected to start being let out of prison in tranches from October.

On Sunday, the prime minister told BBC Breakfast anyone convicted of manslaughter would be excluded from the scheme, following a campaign from PC Andrew Harper's family to block the release of two men convicted over his killing in 2019.

Extra prison space would also be created by deporting more foreign prisoners and releasing some inmates serving indefinite sentences.

Government figures show there were 10,134 foreign nationals held in custody on 30 June, 3,283 of whom were on remand and would not be eligible for deportation.

In the year to June, 5,962 foreign offenders were sent back to their home countries - the highest rate of deportations since 2017 and a 12% increase on the previous year.

News.title: Why did Modi urge Putin to end Ukraine war - and will he listen?
News.content:
If anything, it is very much in line with India's policy of strategic autonomy. Which then begs the question: why would Modi say something on the war so publicly?

The answer lies in the long-standing Russia-India ties - the two countries have generally found a way to work together, even when they see geopolitics through different lenses.

Moscow has continued to be one of India's strongest allies despite Delhi forging closer relationships with Europe and the US in the past three decades.

Delhi is one of the founding members of the Brics grouping of nations along with Russia and China, and it is also a member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation with the two countries.

But at the same time, Delhi is also a member of the Quad group with Australia, Japan and the US - Moscow has not been happy about this association.

Still, Moscow and Delhi tend to work through these differences. Moreover, Russia still supplies around 40% of India's defence imports and it has also been a steady supplier of Delhi's energy needs.

So, Modi's latest statement is not expected to cause any rift in Moscow-Delhi relations and analysts say it's unlikely that it would have come as a surprise to Putin or his diplomats.

As for the West and Modi's critics in India, they will feel that the prime minister should have been even more direct in his criticism of the war.

News.title: Briton among 119 rescued in Nepal after deadly floods, army says
News.content:
A Briton is among 119 people to have been rescued in Nepal following deadly floods, a spokesperson for the country's army said.

It comes nearly a week after the devastating floods hit the country and neighbouring Tibet, killing more than 1,000 people, with more than 3,900 still missing.

The British male, who has not yet been identified, was rescued using air resources, the Nepali army said. It is not yet known whether he was in the country at the time the floods hit.

There were also 118 Nepalese people rescued, of whom 44 were female and 74 male, the spokesperson said from Bidur army camp in the Trishuli Nuwakot district.

The BBC has contacted the UK Foreign Office for comment.

It has been previously reported that 33 British nationals are missing in Nepal in the wake of the floods.

More than 600 are workers believed to be trapped in a vast network of mud-filled tunnels at hydropower sites along Trishuli River are among the thousands who are still missing.

Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah said on Monday that 279 people had been rescued from the sites.

The rescue operation is being spearheaded by an international team made up of Chinese and Nepalese military personnel, while experts from India, Korea and Australia are also involved.

On Tuesday, the Nepalese Tourist Board said it had rescued 330 foreign nationals in total.

Saturday saw a rapid development team from the UK arrive in Nepal to provide support for Britons and their families.

News.title: Summer 2026 was UK's hottest on record, Met Office says
News.content:
In a rapid attribution study - which looks at how much of a role climate change plays - the Met Office say the average temperature was made around 130 times more likely due to human-induced climate change.

And step back from this summer and there is clue to our changing climate in the temperature record itself.

In a climate that isn't changing, new records should become progressively rarer, because every time a record falls, it raises the bar for the next one.

Think about the 100m race. Each time someone sets a new record, it becomes harder to beat. And there's another thing. Typically records are only ever broken by a few fractions of a second â often just a millisecond or two.

In June 1991, for example, Leroy Burrell ran 9.90 seconds, beating Carl Lewis's 1988 world record of 9.92 seconds by just two hundredths of a second.

Now look at the UK summer temperature record. Until last year, the four hottest summers on record were separated by just five hundredths of a degree.

Then 2025 beat the previous record by 0.34C. And this summer has beaten that new record by another 0.40C.

So after years when the record moved by tiny fractions, in just two summers the bar has been raised by 0.74C.

Head of Climate Attribution at the Met Office, Dr Mark McCarthy said that summer 2026 was "remarkable" and we can expect to see extremes occurring more frequently in the future because of climate change.

So why is this happening so quickly here? The UK sits on the western edge of Europe, the fastest-warming continent on Earth - warming at roughly twice the global rate.

There are a few reasons for that. Land heats up faster than the oceans, parts of Europe stretch into the rapidly warming Arctic, and changes in weather patterns have favoured more frequent and intense summer heatwaves.

Scientists are still working out exactly how much each factor contributes, but the result is clear: the background climate in which British weather happens is getting warmer.

None of this means the UK will break its summer record every year. Weather will always give us cooler summers as well as hotter ones. But the pattern is becoming unmistakable: records that once marked the extreme edge of the UK's climate are being overtaken with remarkable speed.

So the question is not whether the UK will experience summers hotter than this one. It is how often they will come - and how much hotter they might be.

News.title: Trump says US position on Falklands 'one of many' under review
News.content:
Donald Trump has said the United States' position on the Falkland Islands is "one of many" under review, as he pressed the UK to increase military spending.

The US president said the UK has "got some problems, but they'll get solved" when asked about defence funding as a follow-up question to his response on the Falklands.

It comes after The Daily Telegraph reported, external US defence officials were drawing up proposals to incentivise Nato allies to meet their spending pledges, with a threat to oppose UK sovereignty over the Falklands among the possible options.

The UK government responded by saying Falkland islanders "are British with a right to determine their own future".

A spokesperson added: "The islanders have repeatedly expressed their wish to remain a British overseas territory and our commitment to them is unwavering."

The Falkland Islands, in the south-west Atlantic Ocean, remain the subject of a sovereignty dispute between Britain and Argentina.

The two countries waged a brief but bitter war over the territory in 1982. A British military task force ejected Argentine forces, which had landed on the Falklands to stake a territorial claim.

The 74-day conflict led to the deaths of 255 British military personnel, three islanders and 649 Argentine military personnel.

Previous US administrations have formally recognised the UK's de facto administration of the islands, but have not taken a formal position regarding sovereignty.

Speaking to reporters on Monday, Trump was asked by the BBC if he was reviewing the US position on the Falkland Islands.

The president replied: "I always review every position. That's just one of many."

Trump's remarks were labelled "nonsense" by Labour MP Dame Emily Thornberry, who chairs the Commons foreign affairs committee, as she asked the UK government to issue an official response in the House of Commons.

Foreign Office Minister Uma Kumaran replied: "The UK has no doubt about its sovereignty over the Falkland Islands.

"They are and will always remain a British overseas territory in line with the wishes of the Falkland islanders.

"The UK is steadfast in our support for the islanders' rights of self-determination."

Kumaran said she had seen Trump's comments, adding: "Our position remains unchanged."

News.title: Two-day sea search for missing teen on holiday is called off
News.content:
A major sea search for a missing 15-year-old boy has been called off after two days, the coastguard has said.

At about 15:30 BST on Sunday, HM Coastguard received a report that three people were experiencing difficulty in the water at Marloes Sands beach, Pembrokeshire.

Two managed to get out of the water, but the teenage boy, who was visiting the area on holiday from Yorkshire, was unaccounted for. The search was suspended at 19:30 BST on Monday.

The Maritime and Coastguard Agency told the BBC that there were currently no plans to resume the search.

Pembrokeshire councillor Claire George said the community had been in shock.

She said: "We're absolutely distraught that somebody has come to harm when they've come to enjoy our wonderful coastline. It's most upsetting for all of us."

Marloes, she said, was remote and hard to access, adding that some beaches were safer than others.

She said: "It's a very dynamic environment. The sea can change at any minute, the weather can change at any minute, so people need to be aware of the risks."

On social media, Angle Lifeboat RNLI said its crew "worked tirelessly" for 22 hours at sea in a major, multi-agency search for the missing swimmer.

On Sunday, Broad Haven and Dale coastguard rescue teams were in attendance, alongside RNLI lifeboats from Angle, Tenby and St Davids and a pilot boat.

A coastguard helicopter and a HM Coastguard fixed wing aircraft were sent, along with the Welsh Ambulance Service.

The search was suspended at about 03:30 BST on Monday and started again later that morning, before being called off in the evening.

The Maritime and Coastguard Agency said, despite an extensive search, "sadly, no sign of the missing person was found".

Angle Lifeboat RNLI added its crew had "shown immense dedication over the past two days".

It thanked the Milford Haven Coastguard for "their fantastic coordination and support" in what they said has been a "lengthy and tiring incident".

"Our thoughts are with the swimmer's family and friends at this difficult time," it added.

News.title: Noughties garage track named TikTok's UK song of the summer
News.content:
British singer Kyla's Do You Mind has been named as TikTok's song of the summer in the UK after the noughties garage track experienced a resurgence on the app.

The song gained popularity when it was first released in 2008, but it became known worldwide in 2016 when Canadian rapper Drake sampled it on his chart-topping single One Dance.

It has now found a new audience by trending on TikTok, generating more than 500 million views from about 650,000 videos posted in the UK over the summer, according to the platform.

Kyla, who created the song with her husband DJ Paleface, tells BBC Newsbeat it is "surreal" but "incredible" that Do You Mind is getting another moment nearly 20 years on.

News.title: Watch: Notting Hill Carnival celebrates 60th anniversary
News.content:
London's Notting Hill Carnival celebrated its 60th anniversary with hundreds of dancers, drummers and other performers celebrating Caribbean arts and culture.

"Notting Hill Carnival is about community, it's about having fun, celebrating history and culture", said a festival-goer.

"It's so fun, it's a good energy", said another participant on the last day of the event.

The three-day event in west London normally attracts about two million people each year.

Follow the BBC's coverage of this year's Notting Hill Carnival for all the best moments.

News.title: 'It's destroying our town': Residents tell of concern after violent incidents near Middlesbrough
News.content:
Residents near Middlesbrough have told the BBC of their concern after a spate of violent incidents in their area, including a crash that killed seven people including two police officers and a house fire that killed a woman and a seven-year-old girl.

Police have said the two incidents are not connected. They have made a series of arrests in relation to the crash and two arrests in relation to the house fire.

On Friday Redcar MP Anna Turley said disorder at a balloon release for one of the young men who died in the crash was "unacceptable".

News.title: Video appears to show police chase minutes before fatal A66 crash
News.content:
Security camera footage appears to show several police vehicles chasing a car just minutes before a fatal crash that killed seven people, including two police officers, near Middlesbrough.

The clip is thought to have been filmed on Lime Road at 03:36 BST on Saturday morning, around three minutes before a Volkswagen Passat travelling the wrong way on the A66 nearby collided into a marked police vehicle.

The BBC understands the police car involved in the crash was not part of the pursuit and that the chase had stopped before the collision.

Following a mandatory referral from Cleveland Police, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) has opened an investigation into the circumstances of the crash.
