A piece of art protesting President Donald Trump using the numbers “8647” was removed from the Minnesota State Fair after the artist allegedly received death threats.

A spokesperson for the fair said the artist asked to have the piece, made from dried beans, taken down, according to CBS News.

The crop art included the numbers "8647," which have been used to protest Trump. The number 86 is slang typically meaning "to throw out" or "remove," according to Merriam-Webster dictionary. Trump is the 47th president.

Trump's Department of Justice has stated that using the phrase "8647" constitutes a "serious expression of an intent to do harm to the President of the United States."

Fair-goer Tyler Breuch told the Minnesota Star Tribune that the supervisor who removed the art had told him the artist received death threats about piece, causing them to leave the state.

open image in gallery A piece of art, made from beans, that stated ‘8647’ was removed from the Minnesota State Fair ( Social media )

"Over this piece, which just seems ludicrous that someone who misunderstands slang is threatening to kill somebody over dried beans," Breuch told CBS News in a statement.

The Independent has requested comment from the Minnesota State Fair.

A conservative website, Alpha News, reportedly ran a story about the crop art Saturday, according to the Tribune.

The 8647 piece was placed in an exhibit with other political crop art. One piece read "AI is making me sad," while another proclaimed "Fairgoers say ICE OUT." A third read: "FAUCI LIED."

The slang "8647" may have been especially triggering for Trump supporters after an incident involving the former FBI Director James Comey. In May 2025, Comey posted a photo to Instagram that showed the numbers "8647" made out of seashells he found on a North Carolina beach.

open image in gallery Former FBI Director James Comey was indicted by the Department of Justice after he posted a photo to Instagram showing seashells that formed the numbers ‘8647.’ The Justice Department said the post was a threat against President Donald Trump ( AFP/Getty )

In April, Trump’s Justice Department announced Comey was being indicted by a grand jury over the post.

"James Comey disgracefully encouraged a threat on President Trump’s life and posted it on Instagram for the world to see," FBI Director Kash Patel said at the time.

"As the former Director of the FBI, he knew full well the attention and consequences of making such a post. This FBI and our DOJ partners pursued a rigorous investigation that followed the facts - and now Mr. Comey will be held fully accountable for his actions."

Comey's case will go to trial this fall.

A Pennsylvania police officer has been charged with voluntary manslaughter after killing Glenn Pysher, a college student who mistakenly tried to enter a stranger’s home after a night out drinking with friends.

Pysher, 22, was celebrating a friend’s birthday at a bar in Upper Pottsgrove, about 45 miles northwest of Philadelphia, last month, when his friends decided to take the party to one of their houses. Kevin Sorbo does not regret leaving California.

After the Hercules: The Legendary Journeys actor, 67, traded Hollywood for the Sunshine State seven years ago, the MAGA supporter told Fox News in an interview Sunday that part of the reason he left California was that he was “canceled” due to his political beliefs as a conservative Christian — but he had other complaints too.

Sorbo told the right-wing outlet that although he misses the weather, his old house and his local golf course, three factors keep him from returning to the Golden State.

“I mean, here in Florida, yeah, we get five months of pretty high humidity,” the Andromeda star acknowledged. “It’s pretty hot, but the winters here are really quite amazing. But yeah, there are things I miss, but they can keep their taxes, they can keep their traffic, and they can keep their negativity, I’m done.”

He went on to say that Florida has given him more “acceptance” since he relocated with his family.

open image in gallery Kevin Sorbo has spoken out about why he left California ( Getty )

Sorbo is known as a vocal critic of Hollywood, and he often claims that the entertainment industry is biased against people who have conservative or Christian views.

“It's just ridiculous and childish to me,” he said. “We all have different opinions. There's nothing wrong with that.”

He went on to say that people in Hollywood dismissed him after he became outspoken about his support for President Donald Trump.

“It’s the conservatives that are in the closet now because they saw me get canceled,” he explained. “But I’m still working.”

open image in gallery Kevin Sorbo and his wife Sam Sorbo have lived in Florida for seven years ( Getty )

Sorbo is best known for his lead role as the ancient Greek demigod Hercules in the Nineties TV series Hercules: The Legendary Journey, which followed a series of five television films. After Hercules ended in 1999, Sorbo played Captain Dylan Hunt in the sci-fi drama Andromeda from 2005 to 2006. He also appeared on the final season of The O.C.

In recent years, he has focused largely on producing, directing and acting in faith-based films, with his latest project being a Christian movie about a rockstar titled Elijah Peel.

He also has worked on several family-oriented movies. Sorbo and his wife, conservative activist and actor Sam Sorbo, have three children together whom they homeschooled, including their son Braeden Sorbo, who is an actor and the author of a pro-masculinity book.

Braeden made headlines last year when he said on a podcast appearance that he thinks only married couples with property should have the right to vote.

The UK is almost tripling its funding to tackle the deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), announcing a further £51.8 million as the virus continues to spread rapidly.

Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCD) minister Kirsty McNeill told MPs on Tuesday that the additional funding would take the UK’s total commitment to the response to £78.7 million.

The announcement comes as the outbreak continues to outpace the response, killing 2,950 people since the epidemic was declared in mid-May, with 6,100 cases confirmed.

It is the fastest-spreading outbreak ever and the DRC’s deadliest on record, with the World Health Organisation warning that it is on track to surpass the deadliest anywhere – the 2014 to 2016 outbreak in West Africa, which killed more than 11,000 people

UN health workers warned in August that the outbreak in the DRC is continuing to spread “exponentially”, with the wider response hampered in part by cuts to international aid by both the US and UK over the last 18 months. The Independent has repeatedly reported on the growing calls for more aid to be sent to DRC as quickly as possible.

During Foreign Office questions in the House of Commons on Tuesday, Ms McNeill said that the government is working closely with international partners to support the “African-led” Ebola response.

In comments received by The Independent on Monday in response to questions about further funding allocations amid surging case numbers and a doubling of maternal deaths, Ms McNeill said the UK’S Public Health Rapid Support Team has deployed thirteen experts to date to support the response.

The UK is working to “limit the outbreak, model the trajectory and nature of its development, and reduce its wider health and humanitarian impacts, including maternal deaths”, she said.

The FCDO continues to fund the Women’s Integrated Sexual Health (WISH) programme, which supports the delivery of sexual and reproductive healthcare, she added.

They are also working with partners to scale up programmes to protect maternity services, to provide personal protective equipment to frontline responders, improve water, sanitation and hygiene, and strengthen containment measures such as surveillance.

The Independent reported exclusively last week that maternal deaths in the Ebola-affected regions have almost doubled, with women now also accounting for more than half of cases due to taking on traditional roles as carers in the home.

Women also make up a disproportionate number of nurses and midwives, who are among those most at risk of contracting the virus.

In May, as the outbreak was officially confirmed, Rory Stewart, who previously served as the UK’s Africa minister, said of the impact of widespread aid cuts: "Pandemic preparedness – in other words, dealing with an Ebola outbreak or even a new version of a Covid outbreak – requires lots of people on the ground in places like DRC... who are able to detect cases, respond to them, quarantine and prepare responses.”

“It’s all the infrastructure behind that which is being undermined at the moment. And that’s a real threat, of course, to the world,” he told BBC Radio 4.

The additional funds have therefore been welcomed by NGOs, who said it was a clear sign the UK government had “been listening”.

"Today's announcement shows what's possible when the public makes its voice heard in a crisis,” said Adrian Lovett, UK Executive Director of the ONE Campaign, who work to end extreme poverty and preventable disease.

open image in gallery Over 2,500 lives have been claimed by the fastest spreading Ebola outbreak ever. ( AP )

"This money can now be turned into contact tracers, treatment beds and protective equipment on the ground. We urge the government to work with health leaders and local partners to get it there as fast as possible,” he added.

Mr Lovett said they had asked prime minister Andy Burnham to redirect savings from the falling cost of refugee accommodation in the UK, which has come out of the foreign aid budget, rather than taking the additional funds from emergency reserves. “We are seeking further reassurance on this point,” he said.

Caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, authorities believe the current outbreak had been spreading undetected among communities since at least February.

There is no approved vaccine or treatment, but DRC authorities have begun distributing thousands of Ervebo vaccine, which the WHO said might provide some protection.

Efforts to contain the outbreak have come up against conflict between the government and rebel groups in the eastern region, attacks on health workers and widespread displacement. Misinformation and aid cuts, further decimating and already weak health system, have also slowed the response.

Health workers have gone on several strikes to protest delays in payments, further complicating the situation.

On Tuesday, schools in the DRC reopened despite calls from the country’s teaching union for a delay in restarting classes and sparking fear that it would impact efforts to contain the spread.

Members of the House voted have passed a short-term funding measure to keep the federal government open into early December and prevent a shutdown as lawmakers campaign for reelection.

Action was needed before the fiscal year ends in late September to avoid a funding gap and lawmakers were keen to avoid bumping against that deadline during election season following last year's historic closures.

The House approved the bill 370-48. Because the Senate already passed the measure overwhelmingly, it now moves to President Donald Trump’s desk for his signature.

"It gives the nation and our constituents certainty, certainty that the government will remain open, certainty that our service members will be paid," said Rep. Tom Cole, the Republican chairman of the House Appropriations Committee.

The House approved the bill 370-48 and it now heads to Trump’s desk for his signature ( Getty Images )

A record 43-day shutdown occurred last fall over an expiring tax credit lowering health coverage costs through Affordable Care Act marketplaces. A 76-day closure of the Department of Homeland Security followed, ending when lawmakers funded most operations excluding immigration enforcement.

Representatives were anxious to prevent a repeat ahead of the vote and blamed their opponents for recent gridlock.

"We’re going to avoid the threat of another Democratic shutdown," House Speaker Mike Johnson told reporters in advance of the vote.

Rep. Rosa DeLauro, the lead Democrat on the House Appropriations Committee, urged her colleagues to support the bill during a closed-door meeting Tuesday morning.

She highlighted key improvements over the version passed by the House earlier this summer on a mostly party-line vote. Senate revisions prevent the Department of Homeland Security from shifting funds to the Border Patrol and delay a rule granting political appointees in the Trump administration more power to halt federal grants for programs conflicting with the president’s agenda.

Democrats fear the rule could steer money away from Democratic-led states. DeLauro called the delay an important first step, but said more must be done to block the policy.

"Whether a community receives disaster relief should not depend on who they voted for in the last election," DeLauro said.

The temporary resolution continues agency funding largely at existing levels through Dec. 11, offering lawmakers extra time to negotiate a full-year agreement, though reaching a deal will be difficult.

Republicans want hundreds of billions in new military spending alongside cuts to non-defense programs. Democrats insist on a bipartisan framework that keeps domestic and military funding equal.

Photos taken hours after revellers left this year’s Reading Festival reveal thousands of tents and piles of rubbish were left behind on the site.

More than 100,000 people attended the festival at Little John's Farm in the Berkshire town on August bank holiday.

Drone footage showed piles of waste remained on the grounds after everyone vacated, including food packaging, broken tents, sleeping bags, and blow-up mattress.

The event takes place with the blessing of Reading councillors, who request a report each year allowing them to scrutinise the organisers.

Those reports show that the issue of abandoned tents is not a new one.

open image in gallery Broken tents, sleeping bags, and blow-up mattresses can be seen in drone footage ( Chris Gorman/Big Ladder )

In 2024, Festival Republic, which runs Reading and Leeds festivals, said that 702 tonnes of waste was produced.

That was down from 780 tonnes in 2023.

In 2024, 71 tonnes – about 10 per cent of the total waste – was made up of tents, while in 2023, the leftover tents weighed 80 tonnes.

Some people mistakenly believe that leaving tents and camping gear behind will result in the kit being automatically packed up and donated to charity.

However, while some leftover camping gear does get donated, it mostly ends up discarded.

open image in gallery 71 tonnes of tents were left behind in 2024 ( Chris Gorman/Big Ladder )

Festival goers are urged to take their belongings home with them to reduce waste or use the designated on-site donation points, rather than just leaving it in the field.

In a post on Facebook, FatFranks Festival-essentials, which provides camping gear, urged people to donate their unwanted items.

It said: “If you’ve decided you no longer want to keep your camping equipment, please consider donating any reusable items at one of the donation points at each stall.

“Your unwanted equipment can be put to good use and donated to local charities, animal sanctuaries and schools, helping people and organisations in our communities who need it.

“Don’t leave it behind, donate it and give it a second life!”

open image in gallery Festivalgoers are urged to use the designated on-site donation points instead of dumping their gear ( Chris Gorman/Big Ladder )

Festival-goers can also donate broken or damaged items, including campsite gear and clothing, to support charities, according to the festival organisers.

Reading Repairium collects the donations and the proceeds go to Berkshire Youth, a local charity dedicated to supporting young people.

News.title: Transfer deadline day LIVE: Man City agree record Enzo Fernandez fee, Chelsea chase replacement, Arsenal miss out on Alvarez alternative
News.content:
Transfer deadline day has arrived with two of the biggest sagas of the summer still to be resolved: will Arsenal sign Julian Alvarez and could Enzo Fernandez be swapping Chelsea for Manchester City before tonight’s 11pm deadline?

Well, Manchester City have reached an agreement with Chelsea to sign the midfielder for £125m, matching the British record transfer fee Liverpool paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak last summer. The move completes City’s expensive midfield rebuild and will see Fernandez reunite with Enzo Maresca at the Etihad. Chelsea want to ensure they have a suitable replacement lined up, with Monaco’s Lamine Camara top of Xabi Alonso’s list and talks continuing over a £60m deal for the 22-year-old midfielder.

Premier League champions Arsenal have pursued Alvarez all window but are running out of time to submit an offer to Atletico Madrid, despite selling Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus to free up space for the 26-year-old forward. It means the Gunners could be left short in attack if they do not meet Atletico’s €150m asking price and so have explored alternatives – though they have turned down a possible deal for Malick Fofana. The Lyon forward is now set to join Crystal Palace or Sunderland.

Manchester United have still not signed a left back, but have made swift progress over a possible deadline day deal for Leicester City youngster Louis Page, while Liverpool’s business appears done after signing Bradley Barcola and rejecting Manchester City’s approach for Cody Gakpo. City have agreed a £60m deal with Everton to buy Iliman Ndiaye. That could have an impact on Everton’s pursuit of Jack Grealish and Richarlison, with Tottenham still wanting to sign a new forward too.

News.title: Newborn baby girl found in Sheffield house died from stab wounds, police say
News.content:

A newborn baby who was found dead in a Sheffield property died from stab wounds, police said.

A murder investigation was launched after the baby girl was found dead in the Wincobank area of Sheffield on Sunday.

Officers received reports of concern for the safety of a baby at 5.58am, South Yorkshire Police said.

They searched a property on Holywell Heights where the baby girl was found.

Despite the best efforts of officers and paramedics, the baby was pronounced dead at the scene, the force said.

Police said a forensic post-mortem examination on Tuesday had found that the baby girl died as a result of stab wounds.

Seven people aged between 15 and 38 were arrested on suspicion of murder.

Two of them, aged 26 and 37, have since been bailed.

open image in gallery Seven people aged between 15 and 38 were arrested on suspicion of murder ( Getty/iStock )

A force spokesman said detectives had obtained a warrant to extend the time the remaining five people can be held in custody.

Detective Chief Inspector Tom Woodward said: “We recognise this is deeply distressing for those who would have loved to have a chance to love this baby girl, for the emergency services who responded and for the community who will inevitably be shocked by this incident.

“Everyone involved in responding to this tragedy – from the first officers and paramedics on the scene to the detectives now leading the investigation – has felt the profound impact of this investigation.

“Our commitment to this little girl is unwavering.

“We will confront every difficult and distressing challenge and pursue every line of inquiry with determination and care to secure justice for her.

“We know the local community will hold her in their thoughts and support us as we work through this complex investigation.”

Police and specialist search officers will continue to conduct enquiries around the Wincobank area.

Senior investigating officer Detective Chief Inspector Emma Knight said on Sunday: “We are aware news of this will be deeply concerning and I want to reassure our local communities that we have a dedicated team of detectives and officers hard at work to ensure justice is secured for the baby girl at the heart of this investigation.”

She added: “Our investigation is in its early stages and we would like to remind people to avoid speculating about this incident.”

Anyone with any information about this incident which could assist the investigation is asked to contact the force online or call 101, quoting incident number 194 of 30 August 2026.

News.title: Borrowing cost surge leaves Healey with £10bn headache
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs have surged at one of the fastest paces in the world in a move that threatens to blow a near £10bn hole in Chancellor John Healey’s fiscal plans.

Interest rates on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for Treasury borrowing costs, rose to the highest level since 2008 on Tuesday amid a global bond market rout.

Britain’s cost to borrow over 20 years rose to its highest level since 1998, signalling growing stress in the market.

Government borrowing costs around the world have climbed sharply in recent weeks, amid concerns about unsustainable debts and persistent inflation.

However, Britain suffered the biggest increase in bond yields in the G7 on Tuesday as economists warned that investors were particularly nervous ahead of Mr Healey’s first Budget.

News.title: Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals
News.content:
Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

News.title: Robinson’s Victorian-style bowling figures secure series victory over Pakistan
News.content:
The only missing aspect was a five-fer which would have brought a 100th Test wicket. Even so, his career average is now 19.53, the best for England since Frank Tyson of those with 50 or more wickets.

Mr Nude Nuts, as Matthew Hayden called him, could be devastating against Australia and, like Root the captain, deserves to be judged on what happens in his second incarnation rather than what went before.

Robinson’s pace has lingered around the 79mph mark and inevitably that throws up Rob Key’s assertion you cannot succeed in Test cricket bowling in the 70s with the keeper standing up. Key was referring to county bowlers pitching it up and relying on the Dukes ball to do the rest.

It was thrown in his face in Australia but Michael Neser and Scott Boland are not county trundlers: they extract more energy off the pitch than that.

Robinson is also no dobber. His high release point combined with a mastery of length means he is always threatening the top of off stump. He also knows which way the ball is going to nip, giving no clues to the batsmen due to his sleight of hand skills.

With Jamie Smith improving under the tutelage of Sarah Taylor, he can operate with the keeper standing up which pins batsmen in the crease, bringing all modes of dismissals into play. Robinson was as effective with the new ball as the old: his two seven-over spells were two for 13 and two for 11.

How snarling Robinson adds edge and precision

At 32, he has become a combination of Stuart Broad and James Anderson, although down on their pace with the height and bounce of the former, and tricks of the latter. He can move the new ball further either way than Anderson or Broad but the question is whether he has their durability and sheer competitiveness.

He has not been tested this summer by pitches or opponents. He has not bowled more than 18 overs in an innings and was injured when England played on the best batting pitch at the Oval. He was not trusted at Trent Bridge because the old management had burned their fingers before. That decision may well have cost the coach his job.

Like Broad and Anderson he has a snarl too, sending Abdullah Shafique on his way with a word or two. There was no need for that but maybe it was just a carried away reaction to bowling an absolute beauty that angled in, seamed away and hit the top of off.

News.title: Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness
News.content:
Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

News.title: Moses Itauma lifted out of ring after losing IBF title bout to Filip Hrgovic
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the heavyweight clash between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic.

Itauma is on the cusp of becoming a British boxing star, but for now there remain questions. It is not that people doubt his talents, more that he needs to prove them emphatically to the wider boxing world.

At just 21, Itauma has been creating rumblings since 2023. He has 10 straight knockouts. He is undefeated. His last two wins were against Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin, but he is yet to beat a fighter you might regard as a gatekeeper to a title fight.

Hrgovic might normally be seen as that gatekeeper. At 34, the Croatian has plenty of experience in the ring, with 21 fights bringing 20 wins, 15 of them by knockout. His only loss was against Daniel Dubois in 2024, but his wins since then have been against Joe Joyce, David Adeleye and Dave Allen. Not the highest quality, by any means. Hrgovic, then, has something to prove to us too.

However, this is no eliminator, this is for the full IBF world heavyweight championship. A win for Itauma would see him become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in boxing history.

As Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury circle one another, threatening to never fight at all, Itauma looks set to be Britain’s next heavyweight star. All he has to do is win at the O2 Arena tonight. If he does that, he could then be a fixture at the top of the sport for a decade, perhaps more.

Ringwalks are expected at around 10.30pm for the main event. So if men in dressing gowns is your thing, get ready.

News.title: £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle
News.content:
“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

Sports.title: Chelsea ‘dealt double midfield blow after Enzo Fernandez Man City transfer as new Camara bid rejected and Kone staying’
Sports.content:
CHELSEA have reportedly been dealt a double transfer blow after they saw bids for two midfield targets rejected.

The Blues are on the verge of selling Enzo Fernandez for a British transfer record fee of £125million.



But club transfer chiefs have pushed to sign a late replacement for the Argentine.

A £38.5m bid for Monaco’s Lamine Camara was submitted before a second offer of £50m was also rejected, according to RMC Sport.



Meanwhile, Fabrice Hawkins adds another target in Roma‘s Manu Kone is also staying put where he is.

And SunSport understands Chelsea are now unlikely to sign a replacement for Fernandez.



The 25-year-old broke the British transfer record when he arrived in London from Benfica in a £106m deal in January 2023.

But now he is set to reunite with former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca, who succeeded Pep Guardiola, at the Etihad.

And the fee the Manchester-based club are paying to prise him away from Chelsea is equal to what Liverpool paid Newcastle for Alexander Isak a year ago.

Fernandez has pushed to leave Stamford Bridge since March, and did not feature in the club’s wins over Luton in the League Cup or the Brighton win last weekend under Xabi Alonso.

Chelsea had expected him to stay after receiving no bids on their asking price of £120m before a self-imposed August 14 deadline.

However, deadline day madness has now seen City finally move to complete a deal £5m above the original asking price.

Chelsea had put together a five-man shortlist to replace Fernandez, but have thus far found no luck in acquiring any.

As well as moves for Camara and Kone, an approach for Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi was knocked back, while a deal for Bournemouth’s Alex Scott has also been explored.

Sports.title: What is a deal sheet and when is it needed on transfer Deadline Day?
Sports.content:
CLUBS face a race against time to get deals done on Deadline Day.

This year, the window slams shut at 11pm on Tuesday, September 1 for Premier League and EFL clubs.



The likes of Jack Grealish, Enzo Fernandez and Iliman Ndiaye could all be on the move today.

And there is a chance some of the biggest signings of the day require a deal sheet.



What is a deal sheet?

A deal sheet allows clubs to confirm the signing of new players after the 11pm deadline providing much of the paperwork is done.

Teams can complete a deal sheet at 9pm earliest and the last must be submitted at 11pm.

It must state the player on the move, the two clubs involved in the transfer and the fee.

Without it, a last-gasp transfer cannot go ahead and it is not a legally binding contract.

Once it arrives on Premier League or EFL chiefs’ desks, clubs have a further two hours – until 1am – to get a deal sorted and complete the remaining documentation.

When are the transfer deadlines around the world?

Ligue 1: Tuesday, 1 September – 18:59

Serie A: Tuesday, 1 September – 19:00

La Liga: Tuesday, 1 September – 22:59

*All times BST

Sports.title: Arsenal and Man Utd ‘handed major transfer deadline day blow as Inter Milan striker Pio Esposito signs new contract’
Sports.content:
PIO ESPOSITO has reportedly dealt Arsenal and Manchester United a deadline-day blow by penning a new contract with Inter Milan.

The 21-year-old forward caught the eye of several clubs across Europe with a string of impressive displays for the Nerazzurri last season.

Arsenal and United both held an interest in acquiring the striker’s services, with SunSport exclusively revealing the Gunners sent scouts to watch the Italy international in pre-season action.



But those hopes have been dashed as he’s said to have inked a new deal with the Serie A giants.

According to multiple reports, Esposito put pen to paper on a new deal on September 1.

Esposito was seen leaving Inter’s city headquarters earlier today and was the picture of happiness as he posed with fans.

Inter have yet to officially announce his new deal.

But quizzed on his new contract, Esposito told Sky Sport Italia: “I am absolutely delighted.

“I always want to keep improving.”

Sports.title: Matias Fernandez-Pardo seals £51m Newcastle transfer as record buy Nick Woltemade makes deadline day switch to Juventus
Sports.content:
MATIAS FERNANDEZ-PARDO is Newcastle’s new No20 after completing his £51MILLION move from Lille.

The forward, 21, jetted to Tyneside on Monday and passed a medical late last night before penning a five-year contract at Toon.



The Belgian is in line to make his debut for Matthias Jaissle’s team at home to Bournemouth on Saturday after his move was confirmed on deadline day.

Fernandez-Pardo said: “I’m really, really happy to be here and very proud to be at such a big club.



“I spoke to the head coach and he really showed how much he wanted me to be here. In terms of my own career progression, it made complete sense to come so I didn’t hesitate at all.

“I know the club, I know about the stadium, I know it’s a fantastic atmosphere. I’ve followed the team. What I’ve seen is a team that’s very ambitious, wants to attack, get forward, really chase teams and go after them, and that’s really something I want to take part in as well.

“I’m still young, I’m still hungry, and that’s why I’m here, and I want to make that progress with Newcastle. I can’t wait to start the wonderful adventure here.”

The deal completes a huge reset at St James’ Park following a major summer of change.

Things looked grim for Newcastle after the exits of head coach Eddie Howe and the sales of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes.

However, Fernandez-Pardo is the EIGHTH new signing and his ability to play anywhere across the frontline made him new boss Jaissle’s top target to fill the void left by Gordon.



Newcastle United head coach, Matthias Jaissle, said: “I am very happy to welcome Matias to our club.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“We were all delighted when we knew we could complete this deal.

“Matias is a highly technical player with explosiveness in his game. He can score and assist, he has courage, and he has the ability to take players on.

“We’re sure our supporters will enjoy watching him play.



“He has already shown in Lille that he can perform on the big stage, and we will work closely with him to keep developing his game further.

“We are excited to see him in a Newcastle United shirt.”

Sporting director Ross Wilson, who has led Newcastle’s overhaul this summer, said: “Matias is a really important signing for us.

“As I said last week, we waited patiently on Nico Gonzalez, and this time we’ve done the same – only longer.

“Matias is a strong example of how a transfer window can unfold with twists and turns along the way.



“Back in May, he was our top target and we always remained engaged with him.

“Now, at the end of the window, he becomes our eighth addition to a refreshed Newcastle United, and we are excited to welcome him.

“A lot of hours went into this one, but we’re clear on our Newcastle United identity, and Matias, at 21 years old, has speed, intensity and work rate in abundance.

“We believe in his profile a great deal. Our fans will enjoy him, and I know he will also enjoy our amazing St James’ Park atmosphere.



“I’m confident that with Matthias Jaissle and our staff, he will strongly develop and continue to grow here in Newcastle.”

Fernandez-Pardo’s arrival gave Toon’s flop record signing Nick Woltemade the green light to join Juventus on loan.

The striker, 24, faded after a bright start with the Mags following his club record £69m arrival from Stuttgart 12 months ago.

He will look to resurrect his career in Italy after the Serie A giants agreed to pay £3.5m and cover the giant German’s wages.



Though the loan deal does not include either an option or obligation for Juve to buy him permanently.

Meanwhile, Newcastle rejected a £15m deadline day bid from Nottingham Forest, who had an initial £10m bid turned down last week, for winger Jacob Murphy.

Newcastle’s longest-serving player, who arrived from Norwich in 2017, has entered the final 12 months of his contract on Tyneside.

Wilson is well-aware of the need to make financially prudent decisions and knows the veteran could leave for nothing next summer.

However, new boss Jaissle does not want to lose Murphy’s experience and leadership from his youthful squad rebuild.



Talks could now take place over a potential contract extension.

Sports.title: Liverpool let Premier League cult hero’s son join Port Vale as part of plan to give goal-machine EFL experience
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL have sent Keyrol Figueroa on loan to Port Vale for the 2026/27 season.

Figueroa is the son of Premier League cult hero Maynor Figueroa, who made 179 appearances for Wigan and Hull in the English top flight between 2007 and 2015.



The 20-year-old’s dad is also the most- capped player for the Honduras national team with 181 caps.

However, Figueroa Jnr., who is a forward, will be hoping to score more goals than his father, who was a defender playing left-back or centre-back.



And to help him on that journey, he has been given a birthday gift of being sent on loan to League Two side Port Vale.

Figueroa moved to England from Honduras at an early age, and eventually joined the Liverpool academy.



He made his Under-18 debut for the Reds in October 2021 at the age of 15 before signing his first professional contract with the club in May 2024.

The winger stepped up the Under-21s in 2024/25 and was nominated for the PL2 Player of the Month award in January while finishing the campaign with 12 goals in 15 appearances.

But now it has been deemed his development is best served in a new environment.

A statement from Port Vale manager Jon Brady announcing the transfer said: “Keyrol comes from an outstanding football environment at Liverpool and has a really exciting attacking profile.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“He’s quick, direct and dynamic, with a real desire to threaten defenders and play on the front foot.

“He has the strength and technical ability to receive the ball under pressure and link play, while also having the pace and athleticism to run in behind, attack space and cause problems with his movement.

“There’s an unpredictability to him in attacking areas which I feel is something we need and will add another dimension to our team.

“His goalscoring record at PL2 level speaks for itself, particularly in terms of his goals-per-game return, but he’s still a young player with plenty of development ahead of him.

“We’re really excited to work with Keyrol, help him continue that development and give him the freedom to express the qualities he has.”



Figueroa’s exploits have also seen him star for the Honduras national team after switching to them from the United States, whom he had represented at youth level.

He made his senior bow for the senior team in June during a 2-0 friendly defeat against Argentina.

Sports.title: Aston Villa keeper Zion Suzuki reveals why he snubbed Man Utd transfer as he looks to finally prove himself in Prem
Sports.content:
ASTON VILLA keeper Zion Suzuki has revealed why he turned down Manchester United as he looks to finally prove himself in the Premier League.

The Japanese international, who has joined from Parma for £30million as Emi Martinez’s replacement, made his debut in English football in Monday’s 1-0 loss at home to Arsenal.



Suzuki had the chance to sign for United in 2023 but instead, opted to join Belgian club Sint-Truiden on a year’s loan from Japanese side Urawa Red Diamonds.

Asked about his United snub, Suzuki, 24, said: “It was my priority to play games so that is why I made the decision and I played in Belgium for one year, in Parma for two years. It was very important to play in Serie A for two years and now I am confident.



“I made good steps and now I am here to play for the club. I want to enjoy this moment and help the team.”

Suzuki, who played for Japan at the World Cup, was also close to a summer move to PSG this summer but that collapsed as his agents could not agree commission fees and the keeper ended up with the big task of succeeding Martinez, who has joined Chelsea.



He said: “In the end, I am here and playing for Villa. I just wanted to come here for this club.

“There are so many expectations. It is not easy to play after [Martinez] but I want to help the team and be like him.

“I trained with him a little bit but he’s a good person and I learned from him in a short time. So I think I am looking forward to playing against him.”

Suzuki is also looking forward to returning to Belgium next week to face Club Brugge in the Champions League but he knows Villa need to beat Hull in the Premier League this weekend as they have lost their opening two matches.

MANCHESTER UNITED have not ruled out a last-gasp move for Leicester teenage sensation Louis Page.

The Red Devils’ midfield rebuild continued when they splashed £70million on Carlos Baleba last week.

Sports.title: Dual Gold Cup winner Galopin Des Champs dies aged 10
Sports.content:
The 2023 and 2024 winner of the Cheltenham Gold Cup, Galopin Des Champs has tragically died following an accident in a field; The 10-year-old horse, who was trained by Willie Mullins, was found with a severe injury on his near front leg.

Galopin Des Champs has tragically died at the age of 10

Two-time Cheltenham Gold Cup hero Galopin Des Champs has died from injuries sustained in an accident in a field less than a week after being retired by connections.

Ruby Walsh revealed the news late on Tuesday evening that the 10-year-old gelding had suffered an injury to his near front leg which vets concluded was irreparable.

"Sadly Galopin Des Champs suffered an injury in his field this morning and could not be saved," Walsh said in a statement to Racing TV.

"He was checked a few times throughout the morning but late in the morning when I went to get him for exercise I found him with a severe injury, high up on his near front leg.

"He was attended to by our vets immediately but X-rays revealed extensive unrepairable damage."

Walsh paid tribute to a horse that won not only two Gold Cups at the Festival but three Irish Gold Cups at Leopardstown.

The statement continued: "He was a fabulous racehorse whose short time with us has left lots of broken hearts but none more so than those of Greg, Audrey and Sarah Turley and Adam Connolly who looked after him for so long. He will be sadly missed."

Sports.title: Man City agree record-equalling deal to sign Fernandez
Sports.content:
Manchester City have agreed a deal with Chelsea to sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m.

The deal matches the British record transfer fee Liverpool paid for Newcastle striker Alexander Isak during last year's summer Deadline Day.

Chelsea will make a £18m profit on the midfielder they signed for £107m three-and-a-half years ago.

Fernandez made it clear he wanted a move to City where he will be reunited with his former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca. The player will now take a medical and finalise his move to City.

Chelsea are working to bring in a replacement for the Argentina international. They have been pursuing Roma's Manu Kone and Monaco's Lamine Camara as well as exploring potential Premier League midfielders.

The transfer window shuts at 11pm but clubs can submit deal sheets to give themselves an extra two hours to complete deals beyond the deadline.

Chelsea and Man City the biggest spenders and sellers

As things stand, Chelsea have been the Premier League's biggest spenders and Man City have been the Premier League's biggest sellers in this window.

The deal for Enzo Fernandez will see the two clubs swap places in terms of the spending and selling rankings.

Chelsea will have made £415m from player sales alone in this window, which surpasses their own record set last summer (£314m).

It is higher if you include the £17m compensation they received from City for Enzo Maresca. Chelsea have spent £342m on signings, which means they are currently in profit of £73m for the window.

Meanwhile, City's spending is set to hit £375m with the arrival of Fernandez. They have generated nearly £315m from player sales, leaving them with a net spend of £60m in this window.

Carragher: Man City now Arsenal's closest challengers

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher:

"Myself and plenty of others have felt Chelsea will have a really good season. And I still believe that a lot of that is on the back of not having European football, having a new manager, the front three that they've got.

"But they're losing Enzo Fernandez, who, for me has been one of the big players for Chelsea.

"Manchester City look a lot stronger now. I would say they're going to be the biggest challenges to Arsenal right now.

"It is a really good squad. There's no doubt about that. There's been a lot of turnover. Losing Rodri was a big thing and I thought it would be really difficult to recover from that.

But if you said at the end of last season, they would bring in Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez, you'd say, that's a top midfield. They've paid top dollar for it, so it should be.

"That gives them the greatest chance of being the main challengers and maybe the only team who can really wrestle this title from Arsenal."

Redknapp: This is a loss for Chelsea

Sky Sports' Jamie Redknapp:

"Enzo Fernandez definitely wins. His agent wins because he's had two incredible moves.

"What Chelsea are trying to create is a culture and if a player doesn't want to be there, you've got to let them go.

"It feels that it might be the right thing to do. He wants to go work for his previous boss and you're going to get good money in. Some people will say to just keep him but if he doesn't want to be there, then it becomes very difficult.

"It leaves Chelsea a bit short in that area. Moises Caicedo looked like he picked up a knock the other day. Can you rely on Romeo Lavia? He is a top player but his injury record isn't great. Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer aren't those types of player.

"If they don't get a player in, it won't look such a clever move.

"If they get a Manu Kone in, it will certainly soften the blow. But he will be a loss because he is a very good player. But for £120m, it will help balance the books and may look like a smart move in time."

Spurs pivoted to Ukraine international Mudryk on Monday after a dramatic finale to a remarkable summer transfer window for the north London club. Sports.title: ‘In my heart until I die’: Argentina says a tearful thank you to Lionel Messi
Sports.content:
Anyone who was present at Lionel Scaloni’s press conference immediately after the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina in New Jersey on 19 July and saw his tears, the sobs which prevented him from speaking while he got up and walked out, could tell this was a man weeping not because of defeat in a single match but because he was fully aware that what that particular group of men had been through for the past eight years had come to an end.

Messi’s announcement that he is retiring from international football, posted on Instagram on Monday complete with photos of three handwritten sheets of some anonymous yet corporate-looking headed paper and a Harry Potter Time Turner pen, to the soundtrack of Brindis sung by Soledad Pastorutti, instantly dominated the news and unleashed a barrage of homages, gratitude and joy from all corners. But it’s not exactly a surprise.

“How crazy that the day has come, dear Leo,” Cristian Romero posted, making it clear that this was expected in spite of the unexpectedness. “The day no one wanted to arrive has arrived,” echoed Giovani Lo Celso, who said he had “nine years listening to you, admiring you and learning by your side”. His international teammates highlight how in their childhood they dreamed of meeting him one day, let alone actually playing with him. Nico Paz says since he was four years old he “used to watch you play with my dad and we would calculate together whether I would be in time to play with you”.

It’s not just his teammates who are expressing gratitude and nostalgia. On a Buenos Aires street corner someone put a red telephone on a table with a sign saying: “What would you say to Messi?” Passersby picked up the receiver and talked into it: “I’m 86 years old and you have given me the greatest joys in my life. You will be in my heart until the day I die,” one gentleman said. A young boy saw the news and “burst into tears even though I was at school”. A well-spoken woman said “we will miss you because you are an extraordinary being”, a little girl added “you’re the best and the greatest”. An old man signed off “bye, son”.

Influencers, journalists, artists, cultural commentators and psychologists all expressed their gratefulness for Messi being a great human being. “Messi led by example,” the veteran sportswriter Matías Martin wrote, while the coach and motivational speaker Matias “Coco” Gallo Bevegni posted that the World Cup winner “taught me more in defeat than in victory”.

View image in fullscreen A message written by Lionel Messi and posted to Instagram explaining his retirement from the Argentina team. Photograph: Lionel Messi/Instagram/Reuters

The football pundit Morena Beltrán could not hold back the tears as she explained to her older colleagues that for her generation there is a sense of mourning and emptiness which can only be filled by gratitude, which maybe they have already experienced, because they have seen another God. The psychoanalyst Milagros Filgueras praised the decision to hand-write the note, saying some goodbyes need the body involved. The journalist Pablo Perantuono devoted his column to the “epistolary genre”, noting that a handwritten letter in this day and age is almost a countercultural act of originality.

The writer Andrés Burgo highlighted that in 10 of the past 12 World Cups, either Maradona or Messi played, so this truly marks the “end of an era in which grandparents, parents, sons and daughters and grandchildren enjoyed an incredible privilege during almost 45 years. The heir will arrive – we hope – but right now is a time of orphanage. And gratitude.”

View image in fullscreen Argentina fans wearing T-shirts depicting Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona. Photograph: Amanda Perobelli/Reuters

Messi revealed that this letter was actually written two days after the final, a cathartic diary-like release, but that on Monday, after “[what happened with] my dad” he was more convinced than ever. The note said: “It’s a decision that hurt and continues to hurt,” but that he understands this is the moment. The poet Valeria Correa Fiz pointed out that he originally wrote “I think”, crossed it out and replaced it with “I understand”. Messi swore he always gave his all, not only these past few years when “everything was won” (he never says “I won”; it’s always “we” or “it” was won) but he has nothing left to give. He’s emptied.

The 39-year-old, however, scored four goals for Inter Miami at the weekend and continues his career at club level, where he clearly still has much to give. He is not retiring from playing football, the thing he loves most. He is retiring from Argentina.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Messi shows off the World Cup trophy after winning the 2022 final against France. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

With two international dates coming up and no rival agreed, no doubt the clarification that there will be no Messi in the squad will impact on the potential fixtures. And not unlike the time when he quit Argentina before, in 2016, the country’s football is in a bit of turmoil.

The context and climate include scandals surrounding the Argentinian Football Association, the pressure by some lobbies to privatise football clubs, which are non-profit organisations, and the international furore caused by several incidents during the World Cup which have landed Argentina with some hefty fines, sanctions and suspensions.

The heaviness of the Argentina flag which for so many years visibly weighed him down, turned idyllic when it became the cloak of victory, mattered very much to his father, Jorge. Messi said he wanted to win another World Cup for him. Perhaps his death has somehow freed him from that aspect of his Argentinianness.

View image in fullscreen Supporters in Sydney, Australia, watch Messi on giant TV screens after Spain defeated Argentina in the 2026 World Cup final. Photograph: David Gray/AFP/Getty Images

And just like last time, the spontaneous visceral response from the Argentinian people is acceptance and relish at the good times lived. That inexplicable sense of pride that comes from being from the same soil as someone who is very good at something and whose magic is still untarnished by the sordid final match against Spain, or any of the criticisms directed at the squad and fans throughout the tournament. If anything, his final tears in front of the stands, like Scaloni’s tears at the press conference, are mirrored in a nation moved profoundly by the generations we have just lived through, perhaps not realising we were living through them.

The huge volume of emotive, sentimental outpouring is rather lovely, and amid it all an enduring image of three little boys walking down a Buenos Aires street with No 10 Messi shirts on their backs signals the way forward, towards a future unknown.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Tottenham and the rapid disappearance of their club hype man
Sports.content:
LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Before we get going, a reminder to join our team of writers for all the latest transfer deadline day updates before the window slams shut (in most major leagues) at 11pm BST. Get on it.

NOT SO HOT(SPURS)

While Football Daily isn’t going to claim to have looked too hard, the earliest mention we could find of Tottenham Hotspur being “in very real danger” of having to play Lincoln City home and away this season dates back to early March. Thomas Frank had been sacked a couple of weeks previously and fabled firefighter Igor Tudor had arrived in north London, only to lose his first two matches. While the weird but mercifully brief fever dream prompted a deluge of further hand-wringing, Spurs eventually avoided the drop thanks to replacing the Croat with Roberto De Zerbi. A more passable version of Red Adair, the Italian masterminded heroic wins over already-relegated Wolves, a Villa side focused entirely on Bigger Vase and an Everton team who had last done anything of interest 31 years previously. Not so much a miraculous escape, as a quite fortunate one aided by the benevolence of the fixture generator, it prompted the club hierarchy to hose cash in all directions, all the better to ensure Spurs never find themselves circling the drain again.

So how’s that going, eh? Just two top-flight games into the new campaign and De Zerbi’s much-bolstered squad is already rock bottom of the table and six points off the early pace set by their relegation rivals Hull City. And having completely embarrassed themselves at Brentford on the opening weekend of the season, you could have been forgiven for presuming their first home game of the campaign might have been prefaced by a modicum of humility. Eh? Eh? Oh. “We’ve spent and we’ve spent and we’ve spent!” whooped the designated club hype man in his pre-match address from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium sward, a field of nightmares upon which Beyoncé has played twice as many gigs as the three league wins Spurs managed last season. “We’re back! We’re going places! We’re huge!”

Approximately 90 minutes and a third consecutive home defeat at the hands of Newcastle later, there was scarcely a peep from said hype bro, so loud was the jeering of Geordies revelling in the obvious discomfort of their former midfielder Sandro Tonali, who could scarcely have done less to justify his £100m summer fee before being hooked in raucous ignominy. “Forget the result,” cooed De Zerbi, after witnessing his side go down to goals from Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa. “I am not angry, we are working well and were unlucky today with the result. There is no panic. I know where we are going and what the plan is.” Of course everyone has a plan until they get the kind of smacks in the face dished out by Brentford and Newcastle but De Zerbi can at least take heart from the fact that on Saturday, Tottenham looked pretty impressive until they didn’t. It’s a minor victory that will have to do until obliging Everton come to town in two games’ time.

RECOMMENDED FOLLOWING

Now on BlueSpace, TikBook, Instachat, all the lesser disgraces.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“It is a decision that hurts my soul but I know it is time. I love, have loved and I will always love being part of the national team. I have emptied myself: now I have nothing more to give and, besides, there are great young players coming through who deserve to be [selected]. I love you! I thank God for making me Argentinian” – Lionel Messi, with the heaviest of hearts, bids farewell to international duty.

View image in fullscreen An artist draws a painting of Lionel Messi, in Mumbai. We can’t draw for toffee so we’re in no position to criticise the likeness. Photograph: Divyakant Solanki/EPA

double quotation mark As probably the greatest player in history has announced his retirement from international football, I’d like to do likewise. Sure, the ingrates never picked me, overlooking my abilities through several World Cups and Euros, but I feel that, like Messi, the time has come to finally hang up my … ah, hopes of a call-up. But never say never, eh? Look all that happened when the little maestro changed his mind last time around! So, yes, I could still be talked out of this decision, should my country decide they need me. Thank you and …goodbye. For now, at least” – Justin Kavanagh.

double quotation mark Early days but Emi Martínez’s transfer for £7.5m seems like the bargain of the season. OK, he let in three against Brighton but saved many more and transformed Chelsea’s defence. I wonder how much they could sell Robert Sánchez on for? I predict, probably much more than £7.5m” – Nigel Sanders.

double quotation mark So August has just ended and my household is already in a contest to see ‘who can have the most miserable season’, which should cheer up anyone whose pre-season optimism has had an early blow. Me: Luton – one win from three in League One with 10 goals conceded. My wife and son: Spurs – say no more. My other son: West Ham – one win from three in the Championship. It’s going to be a long nine months” – Kevin Goddard.

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Justin Kavanagh. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Manchester United and Liverpool eye Kroupi? Vardy to Wrexham?
Sports.content:
The final day of the men’s transfer window is here, but there is still time for some rumourmongering, before a Supermarket Sweep-style trolley dash for 11th-hour signings.

Going wild in the aisles? Manchester United’s interest in a new left-back has been known all summer, yet here they stand without one on the final day of the window. While many are claiming United’s business could be done, RB Leipzig’s David Raum, Fulham stalwart Antonee Robinson and Fenerbahce’s English left-back Archie Brown have all been mentioned as possible last-minute acquisitions. Jorge Salinas of Racing Santander has been tracked by United throughout the window and some are reporting that deal could be done today for €16m (£13.7m). Burnley are keen on United’s own youngster Harry Amass, but his departure may depend on a left-back coming in.

Speaking of United, remember Jadon Sancho? Well, the one-time £74m Old Trafford signing is still a free agent after his contract expired, with his former club Borussia Dortmund ready to take a chance on him providing he signs a heavily incentivised contract.

United and Liverpool are also credited with an interest in the Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi, though they may not have much time to press on with the transfer. Arsenal have also glanced admiringly in the direction of the 20-year-old Frenchman, who is one of the jewels in the Cherries’ crown.

It appears Liverpool knocked back an audacious approach by Nottingham Forest for their young midfielder Trey Nyoni. The 19-year-old is rated highly by Andoni Iraola, and not even a £30m Forest bid tempted the Reds to sell.

Which midfielder will Chelsea sign if and when Manchester City’s pursuit of Enzo Fernández finally bears fruit? Alex Scott, Lamine Camara and Manu Koné have all been identified as targets for the Blues, but only one of those deals can feasibly be achieved on deadline day. Alternatively, is Eduardo Camavinga still attainable for Chelsea or someone else? Noises are coming out of Madrid suggesting Real could listen to offers of around £60m today.

Let’s move on to Everton, who look to have missed out on Richarlison and Stuttgart’s Jamie Leweling but should be able to bring Jack Grealish back on loan, as well as Kenny Tete from Fulham. Tim Iroegbunam is off to Hull and Iliman Ndiaye looks destined for Manchester City after their deal for Cody Gakpo hit the rocks.

The Championship is often where the juiciest deadline-day activity takes place, and Derby are battling Blackburn to re-sign the Brighton defender Eiran Cashin on loan. Meanwhile Wrexham, who were accused by Sheffield United’s Chris Wilder of “blanket bombing” in their bid to sign his player Callum O’Hare, are also considering Portsmouth’s Adrian Segecic and Bristol City’s Scott Twine, while an eye-catching free transfer for Jamie Vardy remains a possibility.

Sports.title: Barcelona breeze past Rayo but all eyes in Spain remain on Julián Álvarez
Sports.content:
If Raphinha has any misgivings about playing as a makeshift No 9 for Barcelona, he is doing a good job of hiding it. Julián Álvarez would have been proud of the Brazilian’s two neat finishes that inspired the Spanish champions to a 5-2 victory against Rayo Vallecano on Monday night, 24 hours before the transfer deadline. Lamine Yamal scored two wonderful goals of his own in a performance that reassured everyone he is back to his best. Add Anthony Gordon to the mix – impressive again in his link-up play – and you have a fluid, fearsome front three.

Yet after the departures of Ferran Torres, Robert Lewandowski and Marcus Rashford this summer, there is no doubt Barcelona not only still want a centre-forward but require one – at least one. Hansi Flick was very happy to see Gabriel Jesus, an £8.6m arrival from Arsenal, in the stands. “He’s a top striker,” the coach said. But Atlético Madrid’s Álvarez is the ultimate prize.

While Mikel Arteta has apparently attempted to speed up a possible deal with a phone call to Álvarez, the Barcelona president, Joan Laporta, has conducted his interest largely in public. He stirred the pot again last Wednesday after Arsenal’s interest was firmed up. “This whole situation has created a lot of noise,” said Laporta, who specialises in creating a lot of noise, in a video on Barça’s social channels. “Atlético told us they were not selling [Alvarez]. However, it looks like, from what we hear now, they are trying to reach agreements with other clubs.”

Laporta left little to the imagination: “We are very interested in buying Julián Álvarez. We would like our offer to be accepted.” Atlético are not playing ball – and who can blame them? Barcelona’s courting of Antoine Griezmann, who announced he was staying at Atlético in a TV documentary in 2018 only to move to the Camp Nou in 2019, still leaves a sour taste. Again they have shown disapproval at Barcelona’s behaviour in their pursuit of Álvarez. “This situation isn’t about money, it’s about dignity,” an embattled Atlético said in a statement the day after Laporta’s video message.

After the hostile reception he received from Atlético’s fans at the Metropolitano when coming on as a substitute against Villarreal the previous weekend, Álvarez missed some training sessions and the 3-1 win at Sevilla on Saturday. Atlético said the striker was unwell. He returned to training on Sunday, with Arsenal appearing his only route out by the end of Tuesday – “there is zero consideration of an Álvarez transfer to Barcelona,” Atlético said.

Álvarez’s absence was felt keenly at the Camp Nou on Monday – for about 20 minutes. After some sloppy Barcelona finishing and an emphatic strike from Rayo’s Sergio Camello, a striker who came through Atlético’s academy, the headlines were obvious. But the narrative did not come to the rescue of the Rayo centre-back Pathé Ciss, who ended up on his backside after Raphinha skipped past him and slotted in the equaliser.

View image in fullscreen Gabriel Jesus gestures upon arrival at the airport in Barcelona on Monday. Photograph: Enric Fontcuberta/EPA

On an evening when Argentina’s footballers were writing Instagram posts about international retiree Lionel Messi, Barcelona’s current No 10 paid tribute in his own way. Lamine Yamal cut inside and whipped a shot past the flying Dani Cárdenas, high at his near post, to establish a lead that was never surrendered. After rumours about the 19-year-old’s fitness and wellbeing circulated following his sluggish start to the season, Flick reminded everyone that the kid had only three weeks’ holiday since beating Messi and Argentina in the World Cup final. Lamine Yamal was reaching his “top level” in training, Flick insisted, and it was hard to argue with him.

It was also hard to argue with Florian Lejeune when the Rayo defender said in a half-time interview that Barcelona “are very good”. Six minutes after the restart, he turned the ball into his own net. Gordon, the most expensive outlay at the Camp Nou this summer except perhaps for the new roof that is still under construction, provided the cross for that own goal and a great deal more from the left wing. The England forward’s selfless passing and running has quickly endeared him to supporters and there were chants of “Gordon, Gordon, Gordon” from behind the goal. His backheel set up Raphinha’s second and Barça’s fourth to make it three assists in three games.

View image in fullscreen Raphinha (right) celebrates scoring Barcelona’s fourth goal with Lamine Yamal. Photograph: Lluís Gené/AFP/Getty Images

After an hour of chasing Pedri, Dani Olmo and Marc Bernal, Rayo’s midfield had to contend with Rodri off the bench. The marquee arrival from Manchester City did not have the chance to parade the World Cup he had won as Spain’s captain before his Barcelona debut in the win against Athletic last Thursday. Barça snubbed the trophy presentation following a row over the arrest of one of their supporters who was carrying an Estelada flag – a symbol of the Catalan independence movement – outside the stadium before their season opener at Elche. Athletic’s Spain players had faced whistles from some Basque fans when they presented the trophy in Bilbao. Real Madrid’s Marc Cucurella and Real Sociedad’s Mikel Oyarzabal were given a warm reception at the Bernabéu last week.

Lamine Yamal’s second against Rayo, another Messi-esque finish from the edge of the box, put the result beyond doubt. Barcelona and Real Madrid – the only teams with 100% records after three games – are yet to blink as the title race begins, but all eyes on transfer deadline day, you expect, will be on the exit door at Atlético’s training ground.

Talking points

While Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappé were on the scoresheet in Real Madrid’s 4-0 home win against Málaga, it was the performance of Trent Alexander-Arnold that was perhaps most striking. The former Liverpool right-back was a creative force, setting up Madrid’s third for Mbappé, in his first start under José Mourinho. Mbappé, tipped for the Ballon d’Or by Mourinho last week, topped the scoring charts for a day or so after his sweeping finish from Alexander-Arnold’s low cross.
