Thank you for your feedback.

Aside from Mbappé the most in-form striker in La Liga might be Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang. The 37-year-old scored for the third game in a row as Deportivo beat Valencia 3-1 at Riazor for their first top-flight victory since 2018. Aubameyang could not suppress a giggle at the mention of Adama Traoré in a post-match chat with the media – his former Barcelona teammate has just signed from West Ham: “I’ve told him: ‘We are waiting for you.’”

View image in fullscreen Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang finds the net again for Deportivo. Photograph: Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images

Despite competition from Deportivo’s Bright Ede, who crossed the ball into his own box for Valencia to score, defensive mishap of the weekend goes to Matías Dituro. The 39-year-old Elche goalkeeper tried to juggle the ball into his own penalty area to pick it up but was beaten to it by Levante’s Yassir Zabiri, who poked in the first of a hat-trick in Racing Santander’s first win in primera since 2012. “Matías is a very daring goalkeeper. We had spoken to Yassir: I thought he could win the ball off him – and look how it turned out,” said Racing’s prophetic head coach, José Alberto.

Sports.title: ‘I was scared to tell my old teammates’: Victoria Pelova on making leap from Arsenal to Spurs
Sports.content:
There is not the same intensity to club rivalries between women’s teams as there is between their men’s counterparts, but as the game grows that is changing. Increasingly, there is animosity from fans if a player leaves for a rival side.

Victoria Pelova’s move from Arsenal to Tottenham firmly bucks the trend, though. Despite arguably having her best years ahead of her, the 27-year-old departed with a lot of well wishes and love.

“I was really scared to tell my old teammates that I was going here,” Pelova says. “My close friends knew about it, obviously, but everyone responded so well. Everyone tells me that it reflects on the person I am. So, I’m actually really glad about that.”

Pelova has been an Arsenal fan favourite despite limited minutes in her three years at the club, during which she was hampered by an anterior cruciate ligament injury sustained on international duty in June 2024. Why is she so liked? She comes across as fun and is loved by her teammates, with a wicked and dry sense of humour.

Pelova was not worried what people would make of her move to Spurs, but the Netherlands midfielder did think about it. Ultimately, it was “an easy decision” to join Martin Ho’s squad.

“The way Martin approached me, what he said about how he sees me as a player, the videos he showed me and how he wants me to be, I’ve actually never had a coach talking like that about me. So, for me, it was a good decision. I talked a lot with my mum about it and she immediately said yes. That was actually the most important thing for me, what my mum thought.”

At the start of June, Pelova shared online that her mum had died. A carousel of moving photos of the pair through the years was captioned: “Your biggest fear was leaving me behind. My biggest fear was losing you. Rest now, Mum.”

Pelova is not ready to talk about the loss, but it sits in the background of the interview. Not having to move home as a result of her leaving Arsenal was important. “It does really help me that I have friends and family around me that take care of me,” she says.

View image in fullscreen Pelova slides in on Chelsea’s Alyssa Thompson during Arsenal’s 2-0 win at Stamford Bridge in January. Photograph: Alex Broadway/WSL Football/Getty Images

Reflecting on her spell at Arsenal, with her ACL injury coming at a time when it was believed she would start to get more playing time, she says: “There was a private situation going on, my mum was ill, and I didn’t get minutes. So, it was a really tough time and people didn’t know what I was going through.”

The goal now? “To be happy again, in football and outside football, and just day by day see how it goes.

“It sounds like I have not been happy, but I have been happy in the last year and in being with my friends. But when you’re not playing as regularly as you want to it’s inevitable that you’re not going to be totally happy, and when I’m the happiest person, I will be the best footballer I can be.”

The fresh start at Tottenham has been rejuvenating. “It’s nice to have no one know you. For me, that’s the way to go. I don’t know if I can explain it, but I feel like when everyone knows you, they focus on the things they know.”

Ho made an instant impression on Pelova. “All the coaches I’ve met are always like: ‘Oh, you can play there and there and there.’ Martin was like: ‘You’re this for me.’ He knew exactly where he wanted me and what he wanted from me. That, right away, set the tone for me and it was where and how I see myself as well. What I’ve seen so far is that he’s so detailed. He just wants to make you better. He’s very strict, but he wants to make you a better player and that’s why I’m here.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ho has “a lot” of confidence in her, and that is hugely freeing. “That’s the part I don’t have to worry about … and I can focus on other things.”

Pelova’s experience of Tottenham had been playing against them, and the more difficult that got, the more it contributed to her decision to join. “Defending was so hard,” she says of facing Spurs last season. “So, I already liked the style Martin had the team playing. I also already know Caitlin Dijkstra; I’ve known her for eight years and we lived together in Amsterdam so we know each other so well. She’s like my sister. I know Lize Kop, they’re also one of my closest friends. So, that has made the transition easy because I can always rely on them.

“I’m quite social so I’ve been trying to get to know everyone, the youngsters. It’s quite a hard job in the beginning, it’s intense, but I like it. On the pitch, you’re building relationships, pre-season is always heavy, you just need to grind, but it has been good.”

Pelova has belief in herself and her body, too. “We train really hard. That’s different to what I’m used to. So, obviously it goes up and down, but I’m confident that in a few weeks everything as a team will have progressed so much. Always with new players, it needs time. I’ve been in football a really long time so I know how it goes.”

Asked about Tottenham’s chances of disrupting things at the top, she flips the question, then says she relishes being outsiders. “You need to put us on as underdogs. The underdog position is the place to be.”

Now, Pelova is ready for the intensity of pre-season to end and for the games to begin at home against West Ham on Sunday. One, in particular, stands out, and it comes on 25 October at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. “Please, stop pre-season,” she says with a laugh. “I just want to start. I can’t wait to play against all the teams. I can’t wait to play against Arsenal.”

Sports.title: Janine Sonis: ‘63,000 fans in Denver proves a women’s team was way overdue’
Sports.content:
In the 13th minute of a 6-1 win against Chicago, Janine Sonis ran into the penalty area and stealthily positioned herself behind a line of defenders, before striking a crisp shot into the right corner. It was her ninth goal of the season, the most of any Denver Summit player, and joint-seventh in the NWSL.

Now playing for her hometown club in their debut season, the NWSL and Canada veteran feels that her happiness is translating on to the field. “I think it’s been a season that I’ve enjoyed myself more than any other season in my career, and I think that that’s showing in the way that I’m playing,” she said.

With family nearby, driving the same roads as when being driven to practice as a child, and captaining Colorado’s first women’s professional soccer team, Sonis said “it’s been, to be a little bit cliched, a dream come true to play here”, adding: “I didn’t think that Denver would get a professional women’s team while I was still playing. But it’s the 63,000 [fans at the team’s home opener at Empower Field at Mile High], the fans that continue to show up for us every week, [it] proves the point that it’s way overdue.”

The versatile 32-year-old, who is playing at left-back, has had a profound influence on their smooth transition into the league, adding a positivity to her play and a decisive impact on and off the ball in a season when many of the scorelines have been narrow. Having experienced some of the league’s growing pains, she acknowledges the progress made since its inception, leading to a moment where debutante teams such as Denver have smoother introductions.

“I think we’ve hit a point where the expectation in every environment around the NWSL is so high, especially with the CBA [collective bargaining agreement] and what the CBA requires. And so I think it’s been just really cool for me to see the evolution of the league, and then to join an expansion team and see where the floor is. I mean, with a brand new facility, building a stadium, like where teams are coming into now is just so significantly different than when I first started out.”

View image in fullscreen Janine Sonis of Denver Summit: ‘I’ve enjoyed myself more than any other season in my career.’ Photograph: Andrew Wevers/NWSL/Getty Images

Denver have spent the season looking up at the playoff positions, slowly moving up the table with a consistency of effort leading to seven wins, six draws and eight defeats, with only two losses by more than one goal. After this weekend (when Sonis also marked her 10,000th regular-season minute in the competition), the Summit are sitting just below the playoffs in ninth, with nine regular-season matches remaining.

On how to measure success for a league debutante, Sonis mentions the target of the playoffs, while noting myriad successes already achieved on and off the pitch: “It’s interesting because I think there’s two different answers. As a competitor, success to me is nothing less than making playoffs … We’re putting ourselves in incredible positions in games, we’re creating tons of opportunities, and we’re either drawing games or losing games by really small margins. I think that we have already found success in a lot of ways, and we’ve built a really clear identity and clear playing style, and have built a a solid culture in the locker room with people that are very clear about the fact that they want to be here and compete for this club.”

On what it will take to break into the playoff positions, and stay there, in an infamously chaotic and tightly packed table, Sonis said: “Our attacking relationships and the way that we create opportunities, continuing to build those partnerships in the front line. I know as a full-back, a big part of our game is getting our full-backs into the attack, so putting in quality service and helping create for those attacking players. And I think we need to be very clear that it’s one game at a time. Right now, we’re looking at it as a kind of a five-game season, and doing the most that we can in those five games to put ourselves in the best position.”

Having the Champions League winner and fellow Coloradan Lindsey Heaps on hand after she returned from playing in Europe this summer is also a boost: “I don’t think that anyone can deny when someone with that résumé and presence comes into an environment that they wouldn’t have an immediate impact on the field, but even just the culture in the locker room, her professionalism, the way that she takes care of herself, the way that she speaks, is just so influential to not just our younger players but for myself as well.”

What is Sonis’s favourite contribution of her own this season? A 94th-minute set-piece goal against the Utah Royals to secure a 2-1 win on 9 August. Of the well-rehearsed strike around the defensive wall, she said: “The free-kick was definitely special for me, just because I spend a lot of time working on them.”

Defensively, she emphasized the difficulty of defending some of the league’s elite attackers, such as Sophia Wilson: “I think my favourite thing has just been learning and getting better, and and similarly seeing the fruit of my labor and studying how to be a better defender and the art of it … I’ve been really proud of the evolution of our backline across the season, and we’ve put in so much intentional work, and it’s been really nice to see that come to life.”

Other favourite moments include games at the Colorado Rapids Stadium, where she played her state championships in high school, and, of course, setting the NWSL attendance record with 63,004 fans at Mile High Stadium. Sonis said: “I think there’s parts of it that felt like a fever dream.”

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 11: Manchester City
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 1st (NB: this is not necessarily Tom Garry’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 1st

Prospects

Champions again at last, after a 10-year wait, Manchester City now face an even tougher task: defending their title. They appear to have a good chance of succeeding, especially after keeping their star striker, Khadija “Bunny” Shaw. The WSL’s top scorer and best player of 2025-26 performed a dramatic U-turn by signing a new four-year contract in May rather than leaving on a free transfer, and that may prove crucial in continuing City’s positive momentum.

Their squad looks to be of a similar strength to last season. The Brazil forward Kerolin left for Barcelona but Beth Mead arriving from Arsenal in essence replaces her. Similarly, the exit of left-back Leila Ouahabi will be compensated for by the acquisition of Niamh Charles from Chelsea. Perhaps the only minor question is whether there is sufficient depth to sustain a challenge in the Women’s Champions League as well as domestically, but the core of regulars looks as formidable as any club in Europe.

The team scored plenty last term and had great success down the flanks, with the right-back Kerstin Casparij providing the joint-most assists in the division. Defensively they look solid. The most intriguing challenge could be psychological, as they switch from hunters to hunted, becoming the team that everybody wants to beat. They start at home to one of the promoted sides, Birmingham City, and first meet a fellow title hopeful – Arsenal – at the start of October, when they will aim to lay down a marker in the title race.

Off-field picture

Owned by City Football Group and led off the pitch by the managing director, Charlotte O’Neill, and director of football, Therese Sjögren, City enter the season with a new women’s team building at the training centre. The £10m building offers everything from underwater treadmills to a barista-style coffee machine in the canteen, with every element tailored towards maximising performance for female athletes. Previously the women’s team sometimes had to share a gym with City’s boys’ academy.

The manager

Andrée Jeglertz’s first season could scarcely have gone better, as he oversaw a league and cup double. He arrived in Manchester after a relatively uninspiring spell in charge of Denmark women but his CV is full of extensive high-level experience, including a 2004 European title with the Swedish club Umeå. The 54-year-old is a calm presence on the touchline, unwavering in his belief that his team will “find a way to win”, and has avoided controversy in press conferences, which he handles assuredly.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Beth Mead joins the champions from rivals Arsenal. Photograph: Kate Green/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images

Mead was the headline signing on a free transfer after nine years at Arsenal. City are hoping that the England forward – the Golden Boot winner and player of the tournament at the 2022 European Championship – is not past her best, at 31, and can flourish across a three-year contract. She is the all-time leading assist provider in the WSL. Mead also has 81 caps and will want to be part of any Lionesses squad at next summer’s World Cup.

Stat attack

If teams want to defend more effectively against the champions, they could start by focusing on free-kicks and corners. City scored at least twice as many set-piece goals as anyone else in 2025-26. As strong as they were elsewhere, this was their superpower.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Set for a breakthrough

The 18-year-old full-back Sacha Lewis signed her first professional contract with City in August, having been with the club since under-14 level. The younger sister of the club’s men’s first-team full-back Rico Lewis, she has been a regular for England Under-19s and has been named in the England Under-20 squad that will go to Poland for September’s Women’s Under-20 World Cup. She was the player of the season for Manchester City’s “Next Gen” team last term and, with City juggling European and domestic football, may get a chance in the first team.

What they say

“Our biggest challenge this year is to continue winning and, at the same, compete in other competitions and also want to win those. Winning in one year is one thing, but being able to win in the next year, that is even tougher. Of course we can do that [compete on multiple fronts] and we have good enough players to be able to play with one starting XI on Saturday and do a couple of changes on Wednesday and still win. That was our biggest challenge last year – we had too many good players that were not playing enough games, so this year we will have the possibility to explore the whole squad. Each player will be more important than they’ve ever been for the club” – Jeglertz speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live.

Where are they playing their home games?

The Joie Stadium is the women’s team’s usual home, across the road from the Etihad Stadium, where they will play two home league fixtures. Those will be against Arsenal on 4 October and against Manchester United on 14 February. The 7,000-capacity Joie Stadium, that hosted matches at Euro 2022, has been the women’s team’s home for more than a decade and they were unbeaten at home in the league last season. They haven’t lost a home WSL game at the Joie Stadiumsince a 4-3 thriller against Arsenal in February 2025.

Sports.title: Jurrien Timber’s brother Quinten could join Premier League club in late move
Sports.content:
Quinten Timber’s hopes of a dream Premier League switch hinge on the final hours of the transfer window.

The Marseille midfielder could join Crystal Palace but the Eagles are against the clock to get the deal done before the deadline.



3 Quinten and Jurrien Timber have both earned caps for the Netherlands Credit: Getty

Should Palace get the deal over the line, it would see him join Arsenal full-back and twin brother Jurrien in English football.

Timber has been tipped for a move to the Premier League since his brother’s move to the Emirates Stadium three years ago.

The Dutchman, who impressed for the Ligue 1 giants last season, is the subject of a £17million bid from Palace.



The south London club were not the only possible suitors this summer with FC Porto and Aston Villa have also been credited with an interest in him.

The Netherlands international arrived at Marseille in January following a three-and-a-half year spell with Feyenoord.



However, due to the club's tumultuous financial situation, Marseille need to offload their saleable assets to balance the books.

Marseille have already offloaded former Arsenal and Chelsea striker Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang.



They were also forced to sell ex-Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood to Turkish giants Fenerbahce.

Marseille boss Manager Bruno Genesio made clear his intention to hold onto Timber and it appears that he is not going to get his wish.

Long-standing interest

The 25-year-old first attracted interest from Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham back in 2023.

3 Timber has made a big impression since joining Marseille in January Credit: Getty



3 The 25-year-old featured for the Netherlands at the World Cup Credit: AFP

But a move to the Premier League failed to materialise prior to his move to the Stade Velodrome.

He clocked up 15 appearances for Marseille, helping the club to a fifth-placed finish in Ligue 1.

Despite swapping his homeland for Ligue 1 midway through the season, Timber was included in the Netherlands squad for the World Cup.



But his hopes of accompanying his brother in the squad this summer were dashed when Jurrien withdrew from the squad through injury just days before the tournament.

Timber is now expected to leave cash-strapped Marseille either on Tuesday night or January at the earliest.

He was handed his first start of the season in Sunday’s 2-0 defeat at Ligue 1 leaders Monaco.

Sports.title: Martin Keown explains why Arsenal do not need to make any more signings despite Gabriel Martinelli exit
Sports.content:
Martin Keown explains why Arsenal do not need to make any more signings despite Gabriel Martinelli exit

Martin Keown believes Max Dowman's omission from Arsenal's squad against Aston Villa proves they have enough firepower to compete.

Dowman, who plays as a forward, was not involved in the Gunners' 1-0 win over Villa on Monday evening.



3 Dowman was on the bench for the Community Shield and Arsenal's Premier League opener against Coventry Credit: Getty

Instead, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta opted for Eberechi Eze, Viktor Gyokeres and Noni Madueke as his attacking options on the bench.

Even then, Eze was the only member of the trio who came on against Villa, although the nature of the contest after Bukayo Saka's 59th-minute strike meant a more controlled approach was required.

However, there will come a time when Arteta needs to lean on the full range of attackers in the squad.



Which attacking players have left Arsenal this summer, and who has joined?

Worryingly, Arsenal look set to end the transfer window short on forwards as Gabriel Jesus and Leandro Trossard have both exited while Gabriel Martinelli is on the verge of joining Al Hilal for a club record figure.

Teenage star Ethan Nwaneri has also departed on loan to Borussia Dortmund.



In contrast, Christos Tszolis is the Gunners' sole attacking acquisition this summer.

Despite the imbalance in numbers, Keown believes it will be enough for Arsenal to defend their Premier League crown.



Martin Keown's verdict on Arsenal's depth

"I'm comfortable with the group," Keown said on talkSPORT's White and Jordan.

"Yes, numerically you need another wide player.

"But Max Dowman is a young player that couldn't even get on the bench, such is the quality of that group."

Keown also felt Dowman's exclusion gave weight to Arteta's push for larger Premier League matchday squads.

3 Any injuries to attacking players could have Arteta sweating nervously Credit: Getty



In the Premier League, teams can name up to 20 players for games.

It is a noticeably lower figure compared to other leading European leagues, as LaLiga clubs can name 23 players in their matchday squads while Serie A allows for 25.

"Maybe that's (larger matchday squads) something that needs to come in because one or two of these guys can't sit on the bench," Keown said.

Who has Arsenal attempted to sign this summer?

Should Arteta get his wish, he won't have a lengthy list of alternative attacking options to call on.

But it hasn't been for a lack of trying.

3 Arsenal could not turn their dream of signing Vini Jr a reality Credit: AFP



Arsenal targeted Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior, but neither pursuit was successful.

Rogers instead joined Chelsea for £117million while Vini Jr inked a new deal to remain at Real Madrid.

Belgian forward Malick Fofana was also offered to the Gunners but they chose not to pursue the deal with Fofana heading to Sunderland.

Sports.title: Ainsley Maitland-Niles set for surprise Premier League return three years after Arsenal exit
Sports.content:
Ainsley Maitland-Niles set for surprise Premier League return three years after Arsenal exit

Everton have agreed to sign former Arsenal man Ainsley Maitland-Niles from Lyon on deadline day, talkSPORT understands.

The deal is understood to be worth around £4.2million.

2 Maitland-Niles is due to sign for Everton ahead of the deadline Credit: Getty

Maitland-Niles is in the final year of his deal at French outfit Lyon.

The right-back will arrive at Hill Dickinson Stadium as competition for Merlin Rohl.

Meanwhile, Nathan Patterson is set to leave Everton for Torino ahead of the transfer deadline.

Maitland-Niles has not played in the Premier League since May 2023.

The 29-year-old spent 20 years on the books at Arsenal, having joined at the age of six.

He went on to make 72 senior appearances and win the FA Cup at the north Londoners.

Maitland-Niles spent the 2022/23 season, his last as an Arsenal player, on loan at Southampton.

With 119 matches played, he earned plenty more minutes with Lyon.

Everton's deadline day plans

talkSPORT understands that Jack Grealish is set to return to Everton from Manchester City on a season-long loan.

The 30-year-old joined the Toffees for the 2025/26 season and was a huge hit before injury brought an early end to his campaign.

2 Maitland-Niles will return to the Premier League three years on from his Arsenal exit Credit: Getty

Richarlison had been linked with a return to Everton, although he has all but confirmed that a switch won't take place.

He would have arrived from Tottenham Hotspur, whose move for Iliman Ndiaye has been hijacked by City in a £60m deal.

Everton have also eyed VfB Stuttgart forward Jamie Leweling ahead of the 11pm deadline.

However, their bid worth up to £36.8m has reportedly been rejected.

Elsewhere, Tim Iroegbunam is heading to Hull City for an initial £13m after two seasons at Everton.

Sports.title: New Chelsea signing has two transfer announcements as Blues find clever way to get around Premier League rules
Sports.content:
New Chelsea signing has two transfer announcements as Blues find clever way to get around Premier League rules

It's been quite the day for Honest Ahanor.

The defender has joined Crystal Palace on a season-long loan from Atalanta.

3 The 18-year-old has made just 41 senior appearances in his career Credit: Getty



Ahanor will then become a Chelsea player next summer as the Blues struck a £40million deal with Atalanta for the teenager.

The transfer chaos has meant Ahanor conducted two different photo shoots on deadline day, posing with Chelsea and Crystal Palace kits.

How could Honest Ahanor sign for both Chelsea and Crystal Palace on the same day?

Given the complexity of the deals along with the Premier League's transfer rules, some may be left questioning how it all works.

Per the Premier League's handbook, a club cannot sign more than one player from the same club.



Palace have already signed Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea for the season, meaning they could not sign Ahanor had he gone to the Blues right away.

Additionally, Premier League clubs are not permitted to loan a player to another Premier League club if they acquired the player in the same window.



Again, that would have ruled out Ahanor joining Palace if he completed a move to Chelsea this summer rather than in 2027.

But because the Blues struck an agreement with Atalanta to complete the deal next summer, Ahanor is free to get a full season of Premier League action under his belt.



Why did Crystal Palace push to sign a new centre-back?

Palace were in the market for additional help at centre-back after Chadi Riad sustained an ACL injury in their season opener against Everton.

The south London outfit swooped for Club Brugge's Joel Ordonez and had agreed a deal to sign him on loan with an obligation to buy.

3 Ahanor will get a taste of life in the Premier League with Palace before moving to Chelsea Credit: Getty

However, Palace withdrew over fears about Ordonez's recovery time from a broken metatarsal.



They have now landed Ahanor who, at just 18 years of age, has proved he can handle the big occasions.

Ahanor made 35 appearances across all competitions for Atalanta last term, including nine in the Champions League.

His impressive displays at club level earned him a call-up to the Italy squad last June, where he won two caps.

Ahanor will now be tasked with helping Palace, who are involved in this season's Europa League.



Steve Parish reacts to Crystal Palace signing Honest Ahanor

For Eagles chairman Steve Parish, the addition of Ahanor represents a major coup, especially so late in the window.

3 Palace boss Pierre Sage has brought in five new defensive players this summer Credit: Getty

"Honest is an exciting young talent whose arrival offers further competition for places ahead of another European campaign at Selhurst Park," Parish said.

"We are pleased to have him with us in South London."

Ahanor could make his Palace debut on Saturday when Pierre Sage's side take on Fulham at Craven Cottage, with kick-off scheduled for 3pm.

Sports.title: Ex-Chelsea starlet predicted to score bundles for EFL promotion challengers after bargain transfer
Sports.content:
Ex-Chelsea starlet predicted to score bundles for EFL promotion challengers after bargain transfer

Former Chelsea starlet Jimmy-Jay Morgan has been backed to score bundles this season after a fine start to life at West Bromwich Albion.

The 20-year-old has hit the ground running at the Baggies with four goals and two assists in his first five appearances for the club.



3 Morgan scored four times in the first month of the season Credit: Getty

The England Under-20 youth international joined the Chelsea academy at the age of eight before leaving for Southampton.

He was lured back to Cobham over the Saints in February 2023 but failed to make a single senior appearance with the Blues.

Jimmy-Jay Morgan stats

Morgan spent last season on loan at Peterborough, where he scored 12 goals in 34 League One matches before making the step up a division this summer.



Having joined Championship side West Brom on a four-year deal, the attacker has netted in two of his first three second-tier appearances.

The most recent of which came in Saturday's 3-1 defeat to Middlesbrough, which caught the attention of Adrian Clarke.



The former Arsenal midfielder told the EFL All Access panel that Morgan could prove to be a bargain for West Brom this campaign.

Reacting to West Brom's loss to Boro, Hugh Woozencroft said: "They looked great at times during this game - James Morrison's side.



"Isaac Price, and Jimmy-Jay Morgan linking up for the goal. Really well taken goal."

3 Morgan played for Chelsea's under-21s side but did not manage to break into the first team Credit: Getty

Jimmy-Jay Morgan's going under the radar

"I think Jimmy-Jay Morgan's going a little bit under the radar as well," Woozencroft added on the EFL All Access podcast.

"Coming from Chelsea, four goals, two assists for him.

"Now, obviously, they would have preferred the win, but they look a much more dynamic team than they did last season.



"And he did say after the game, James Morrison, he wants to add a couple more.

"They've added Toby Collyer, obviously, from Manchester United; if they can add a couple of quality players, they could be a team to really worry about."

3 West Brom currently sit in a playoff spot after winning two of their first three games Credit: Getty

Adrian Clarke, who tipped Morgan as among his standout Championship transfers last month, said of West Brom: "I like the midfield with [Ousmane] Diakité and [Jayson] Molumby.



"They're getting younger players, aren't they? And these are young, hungry players with a point to prove.

"Isaac Price, he's got his whole career ahead of him. He wants to make it to the very top. Same with Jimmy-Jay Morgan.

"He's got his move from Chelsea. Could be a bargain.

"I think it's £4million, which felt a lot because he wasn't amazing on loan at Peterborough last season.

"But Sam Parkin, our friend here at talkSPORT, he told me he watched Rotherham play against West Brom in the Carabao Cup.



"He said, Jimmy-Jay Morgan is going to score bundles this season. So he's seen something in him."

Sports.title: Premier League clubs questioned for snubbing midfielder Rio Ferdinand wanted at Man United
Sports.content:
Premier League clubs have been urged to shoot their shot to sign one of Europe's brightest young midfielders.

The midfield market has exploded for English top-flight clubs this summer, and is still set to be a major talking point on deadline day.



3 Kees Smit hasn't made a summer transfer despite being tracked by huge clubs Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands that Manchester City have seen a bid in excess of £120million for Enzo Fernandez rejected by Chelsea.

Enzo Maresca's side have already invested heavily in recruiting in the middle of the park, with Ayyoub Bouaddi becoming the most expensive teenager in Premier League history, after Elliot Anderson was bought for £116m.

Their city rivals Man United have also transformed their midfield, with Youri Tielemans arriving from Aston Villa for £35m, Andrey Santos joining from Chelsea in a £50m transfer and a package worth an initial £70m deal signed off for Carlos Baleba.



Ahead of that summer spree, Rio Ferdinand told talkSPORT in May that he didn't want his old club to miss out on Kees Smit.

Kees Smit transfer latest

The 20-year-old, who was named as one of the stars to watch in Europe at the start of last season, looked destined to be on the move this transfer window.



talkSPORT previously revealed that Newcastle and Crystal Palace were competing with Real Madrid to sign the Netherlands international.

However, despite the affordable price tag, with AZ seeking over £22m and the raft of Premier League clubs overhauling their midfield, Smit has stayed put.



European football expert Andy Brassell told talkSPORT.com: "I'm really surprised that he hasn't gone anywhere already this summer.

"A 20-year-old midfielder who can dictate already. AZ have had a great start to the season. He's been part of it."

3 Smit was a surprise omission from the Netherlands' World Cup squad after his impressive season Credit: Getty

Kees Smit next club

Brassell continued to talkSPORT: "Now, Newcastle were interested in him for a long time, and they went a bit cold because they felt that someone really big was going to get him.



"Like, really big. Like Real Madrid kind of big. So, I do wonder when you get closer to the deadline if there's a club that could make that kind of move.

"I think that would be really, really interesting. Obviously, a big deal to piece together in the last day.

"I don't know what more he could prove this season in the Eredivisie. Unless, like, AZ win the title and go the whole season unbeaten.

"What really could he do to prove any more?

3 Smit has already registered two assists in four Eredivisie games this season Credit: Getty



"People out there know he's a really good player, and he could get to that top level.

"But maybe, if that opportunity is not out there for him, maybe he does have to look to go to a less esteemed club in a bigger league.

"I mean, look, if you're anyone else in one of those big leagues, just shoot your shot already. You can only say no."

Sports.title: What is a deal sheet and how can Premier League clubs sign players after deadline?
Sports.content:
What is a deal sheet and how can Premier League clubs sign players after deadline?

The summer transfer window will dramatically draw to a close at 11pm on Tuesday night and Premier League clubs are ready for some last-minute action.

Clubs across Europe will conclude deadline day at various times depending on the specific league or competition.



3 Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea as their club-record signing Credit: Getty

This year's edition has seen the record fee for a British player broken twice - with Elliot Anderson's £116m move to Manchester City, closely followed by the signature of Morgan Rogers at Chelsea for £117m.

The Premier League champions Arsenal acquired Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle and Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa, with the transfers sparking debate over Premier League financial rules.

Tottenham have spent around £320m throughout the window and are expected not to stop there with a potential frantic final few hours.



What times do the transfer window close?

The summer transfer window closes on Tuesday, September 1 at 11pm BST for Premier League and EFL clubs.

After opening on June 15, Fifa rules state that the window cannot be open for more than 16 weeks at a time.



Last year, the final day of the window finished at 7pm in the UK; however, it has now changed back to its original time.

However, the rest of Europe do not follow the same rules:

Ligue 1: Tuesday, 1 September - 18:59 BST

Serie A: Tuesday, 1 September - 19:00 BST

Bundesliga: Tuesday, 1 September - 19:00 BST

La Liga: Tuesday, 1 September - 22:59 BST

Scottish Premiership: Thursday, 3 September - 17:00 BST

Women's Super League: Thursday, 3 September - 23:00 BST

Despite the strict deadline, there remains a way for clubs to complete late moves beyond the cutoff point.



What is a deal sheet?

It allows a club to confirm an agreement has been reached and also give themselves more time to submit the remaining documentation.

3 What a deal sheet looks like Credit: Premier League

A deal sheet must be completed by Premier League clubs in the last two hours of a transfer window.

For an 11pm deadline, the form cannot be used before 9pm and needs to arrive fully completed before the transfer window closes at 11pm.



Once the sheet arrives, clubs have another two hours to submit the full paperwork (1am).

How do clubs register a player?

The full paperwork includes the contract, the transfer agreement between the clubs involved in the deal, permission to work in the UK (if required), and international clearance if transferring from abroad.

The Premier League's Football Operations and Regulatory departments are staffed late into the night on deadline day.

Once the legal part is finished, it is cleared through the Premier League and Football Association rules. In some cases, the transfer needs to also comply with FIFA regulations.



3 Isak's move to Liverpool capped off a blockbuster transfer window for the Reds last summer Credit: Getty

Previous deadline day signings

Last summer, Alexander Isak departed St James' Park for Liverpool in a blockbusting deadline day switch that shattered the British transfer record.

Other final day transfers include:

Sports.title: Everton see ‘deadline day bid rejected’ for Premier League-ready winger
Sports.content:
Everton have reportedly submitted an official proposal for Stuttgart forward Jamie Leweling.

According to Sky Germany's Patrick Berger, the Toffees' bid was worth up to £36.8million.



3 Leweling has won six caps for Germany since 2024 Credit: Getty

However, Berger adds Leweling has already rejected Everton's advances and wishes to remain at Stuttgart.

Everton's interest in Leweling came after the 25-year-old registered 11 goals and 12 assists for Stuttgart last term.

Nine of Leweling's assists came in the Bundesliga, with only four players contributing more.



Although Leweling may not want to pursue a move to English shores yet, European football expert Andy Brassell believes he'd perfectly fit the rough and tumble of the Premier League.

Andy Brassell's verdict on Jamie Leweling

"Leweling feels a bit more Prem-ready," Brassell exclusively told talkSPORT.com.



"I think because he's quite a physical type of wide player.

"He's someone who's very direct. He's not someone who's slight and speedy and will-o'-the-wisp.

"He's someone who really engages with defenders, who tries to cut inside and scores goals. He's got a feeling that he's in a rush. He likes to do everything quickly. He's adaptable as well.



"I think he can play in a few different forward positions. He's come on so much since he was at Stuttgart, where he's been coached really well by Sebastian Hoeneß. Of course, there's the possibility that he goes to Roma as well. They've been looking for a wide player, particularly a wide left player, for a while now.

"But in terms of him adapting to the Premier League, look, there's been Premier League interest in him for well over a year. See him play a couple of times and you'll totally understand why."

3 Moyes has looked to revamp his attack this season Credit: Getty

Although Everton won't land Leweling, they look set to bring in new faces who can influence proceedings in the final third before the window slams shut.



Which players are set to join Everton late in the window?

talkSPORT understands Jack Grealish is set to rejoin the Toffees on another season-long loan from Manchester City.

Grealish had received interest from Sunderland and his boyhood club Aston Villa, but preferred a return to Everton.

Everton have also agreed a £40m deal to sign Folarin Balogun from Monaco.

Balogun, who came through Arsenal's academy, will replace Beto, who is bound for Fiorentina.



Another fresh face set to join is Ainsley Maitland-Niles, who is expected to move in a £4.2m deal from Lyon.

3 Grealish is in the last year of his contract with City, meaning he's effectively played his last game for the club Credit: Getty

The flurry of activity in Merseyside comes as star attacker Iliman Ndiaye prepares to leave.

Ndiaye is headed for City in a £60m deal, with £5m in add-ons.

It initially appeared that Ndiaye was bound for Tottenham, but City swooped and completed the hijack.

Sports.title: Man City agree Enzo Fernandez deal: Chelsea star FINALLY gets his move for joint-record British transfer fee of £125m as Blues cave in to rivals with no replacement incoming
Sports.content:
Man City agree Enzo Fernandez deal: Chelsea star FINALLY gets his move for joint-record British transfer fee of £125m as Blues cave in to rivals with no replacement incoming

Follow all the latest deadline day news and deals with Daily Mail Sport's live blog HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester City have struck a £125million deadline-day deal to secure Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea, with Enzo Maresca finally set to land his top target from his former employers.

It equals the British transfer record which was paid to Newcastle by Liverpool for Alexander Isak last summer, and is a fixed fee for the 25-year-old Argentinian with no add-ons involved.

While Chelsea reached an agreement which took their incomings towards the £500m mark for the summer – with club sources pointing out that is also a British record – they arguably caved to City by strengthening the squad of a rival and weakening their own with no replacement at the ready.

With City leaving it until the final two days of the window to open club-to-club talks, it left Chelsea with limited time to secure their own signing.

No breakthrough had been found for Roma’s Manu Kone and Monaco’s Lamine Camara at the time of accepting City’s £125m bid on Tuesday afternoon. Chelsea saw two offers worth £38.5m and £42.9m turned down for Camara earlier in the day.

Chelsea likewise bid for Alex Scott previously, but Bournemouth refused to sell this summer. There was also admiration for Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi and Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton.

Manchester City have reached an agreement with Chelsea for the signing of Enzo Fernandez

Central to Chelsea agreeing to a deal with City was Fernandez’s relationship with Maresca with the two wanting to work together again.

Fernandez was known to have been keen to leave, having flirted with that idea before the last season had even finished. Those inside Stamford Bridge say they intend to reassess midfield targets and intend on revisiting the issue in January and next summer.

With no Fernandez – and with Dario Essugo joining Strasbourg on loan – Chelsea’s senior midfield options are Moises Caicedo, Reece James, Romeo Lavia, Valentin Barco and Jordan Henderson.

Malo Gusto can also be used centrally if required. While Fernandez developed a helpful habit of scoring important goals, Xabi Alonso has an impressive attack, having signed Morgan Rogers for £117m this summer to form a front three with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro.

Chelsea fans may be glad that what turned into an exhausting saga is coming to an end at least.

Chelsea initially attempted to accelerate a conclusion by creating their own deadline for bids by Friday August 14 at 5pm.

That was for a £120m transfer and the terms were communicated to their Premier League counterparts via Fernandez’s camp, led by Javier Pastore. Chelsea’s hope was that it would give them ample time to replace their 2022 World Cup-winning midfielder.

However, City did not play along with Chelsea’s deadline. No offer was submitted, and Blues insiders claimed they ‘expected’ Fernandez to stay with them for the entirety of 2026-27.

He was even handed the captain’s armband when he appeared as a substitute in their final friendly at home to Real Sociedad, receiving a mixed reception inside Stamford Bridge.

Fernandez appeared in their Premier League opener at Fulham as a substitute. While the home fans inside Craven Cottage booed him after Argentina’s behaviour at the World Cup, the away end welcomed him warmly, with those Chelsea supporters even chanting his name.

Fernandez continued to train with his team-mates and in Alonso’s main squad rather than the second group including Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson, but then disappeared.

Following talks with Alonso, he was not involved in their Carabao Cup win over Luton, or in their Premier League victory against Brighton. Alonso insisted publicly it was his decision after speaking with the player, but did add he selected a squad that had the ‘desire to play’.

Maresca had a good relationship with Fernandez at Chelsea, where he often wore the captain’s armband in the absence of James. Maresca also handed him that armband barely a month after the Argentinian was accused of singing a racist song following his country’s 2024 Copa America triumph. That was in Chelsea’s Premier League opener at home to City.

When Maresca eventually exited Chelsea after speaking with City about succeeding Pep Guardiola, Fernandez was among those who spoke up, suggesting it ‘hurt’ the team. The Blues ended up finishing 10th in that season, leaving them with no European football under Alonso for this term.

Sports.title: Two-time Cheltenham Gold Cup winning horse Galopin Des Champs dies less than a week into retirement after suffering fatal injury
Sports.content:
Two-time Cheltenham Gold Cup hero Galopin Des Champs has died from injuries sustained in an accident in a field less than a week after being retired by connections.

Ruby Walsh revealed the news late on Tuesday evening that the 10-year-old gelding had suffered an injury to his near front leg which vets concluded was unrepairable.

'Sadly Galopin Des Champs suffered an injury in his field this morning and could not be saved,' Walsh said in a statement to Racing TV.

'He was checked a few times throughout the morning but late in the morning when I went to get him for exercise I found him with a severe injury, high up on his near front leg.

'He was attended to by our vets immediately but x-rays revealed extensive unrepairable damage.'

Walsh paid tribute to a horse that won not only two Gold Cups at the Festival but three Irish Gold Cups at Leopardstown.

Galopin Des Champs, pictured winning the Cheltenham Gold Cup in 2024, has died

The statement continued: 'He was a fabulous racehorse whose short time with us has left lots of broken hearts but none more so than those of Greg, Audrey and Sarah Turley and Adam Connolly who looked after him for so long. He will be sadly missed.'

Galopin Des Champs claimed victory in 12 races at Grade One level and the Cheltenham Gold Cup triumphs in 2023 and then a year later in 2024 made him one of the most popular horses in recent memory.

In 2025, when going for the hattrick of wins in the showpiece race he finished second to to Inothewayurthinkin.

It had been hoped that he'd participate again this year but was unable to race due to injury.

A third place finish in the Irish Gold Cup back in February proved to be his final outing.

Only last week, Willie Mullins confirmed that the legendary jumper was retired before the tragic accident five days later.

He said at the time: 'We took a collective decision to retire Galopin Des Champs at his age because we felt he could not do himself justice at the level he was used to.

'He retires a good, sound horse who will hopefully have a good second career as a sport horse.'

Arsenal have turned their attention away from a move for Atletico Madrid star Julian Alvarez

Sports.title: Why Man City had no doubts about £125million move for Enzo Fernandez - and the reasons Enzo Maresca believed there was only one man who could replace Rodri
Sports.content:
After months of chasing him, Enzo Maresca finally has his man. Enzo Fernandez is bound for the Etihad - and so what if it is costing Manchester City £125million. Relations between City and Chelsea, whom Fernandez joined for £107million in 2023, have been better. Maresca resigned as Chelsea manager in January with his heart set on the City job and his former team couldn’t even bring themselves to refer to him by name when they released a scathing statement in June to confirm they had agreed compensation that meant he could replace Pep Guardiola at the Etihad Stadium. So, what are City getting for ther joint-record British transfer fee? Well, what some might call a ‘character’. One who gets himself sent off in a World Cup final, one who tries to get his Chelsea team-mate Marc Cucurella sent off for Argentina in the same game. One who was frequently booked for dissent throughout last season, one who taunted England fans by cupping his ears after his equaliser in the World Cup semi-final, and one, most damningly, who was accused by his own club-mates of racism after live-streaming himself and team-mates chanting after Argentina won the Copa America two years ago. Maresca, though, gets a player he trusts more than any other. And if he is to succeed, he will need players he can trust. It said a lot that despite the racism row in 2024, Maresca still handed Fernandez the captain’s armband for the Premier League season opener against City. Maresca joked recently that Erling Haaland could not possibly be his captain at City because he demands that his skipper race over to him after every goal to receive fresh instructions, unless it was the captain who scored it. Haaland would clearly score too many. At Chelsea, though, even when club captain Reece James was on the pitch, Maresca would often still call Fernandez over once they scored. So, what are Manchester City getting for their £125million signing of Enzo Fernandez? Well, what some might call a ‘character’ This is a player who got himself sent off in a World Cup final. One who tried to get his Chelsea team-mate Marc Cucurella sent off for Argentina in the same game

Your browser does not support iframes.

Fernandez was so often Chelsea’s engine room. Last season, albeit one Maresca left halfway through, the club ranked rock bottom for how far their players ran in the Premier League yet Fernandez sat inside the top 10 for distance covered individually. Across Maresca’s 18 months at the club, no one played more league matches for Chelsea than Fernandez and only Mo Salah and Bruno Fernandes created more chances from open play across the division. Maresca is taking on arguably the most daunting succession in world football without the most influential midfielder in City’s recent history, Rodri. Without the most reliable metronome in world football, Maresca is going to have to find another way to make City’s midfield tick. Fernandez certainly isn’t a like-for-like replacement. Both are hugely authoritative and dominant but in different ways. Like Rodri, Fernandez is always at the heart of his team’s attacking play but more frequently at the business end of it. In his full season under Maresca in 2024-25, he played a part in 200 attacking moves that ended in a Chelsea shot, either taking it himself, creating the chance, or being a part of the build-up. Nearly 60 per cent of them were him having the shot or setting it up. Among midfielders last season, too, he ranked first for expected goals. By contrast, Rodri’s influence in the previous 2023-24 campaign, the one before he suffered his serious injury, was such that while he topped the list for involvements in his side’s attacking play, only 37 per cent of them were shots or chances he created. Across Maresca’s 18 months at the club, no one played more league matches for Chelsea than Fernandez and only Mo Salah and Bruno Fernandes created more chances from open play In Maresca's only full season at Chelsea, Fernandez was involved in attacking play as much as any player bar Cole Palmer Rodri was also heavily involved in City's offensive work - but earlier on in the build-up That season, Rodri averaged more than twice as many passes as Fernandez in 2024-25 and at a far higher completion rate with more than three times as many splitting opposition defensive lines. The Chelsea man, however, was much more direct when he got the ball, playing a higher percentage of his passes forward than Rodri and more of them into the box. Unsurprisingly, Fernandez commits more fouls. As one colleague who watches Fernandez often put it: ‘Rodri is like the dishwasher, keeps everything nice and clean. Enzo then smashes those dishes.’ One of the biggest differences, and one that Maresca will hope to make the most of, is Fernandez’s superb knack of crashing into the box. Rodri averages less than half a run into the penalty area per game. Fernandez usually makes at least five, and they frequently end up with him scoring. Like another Chelsea star who made the move to City, he’s Lampard-esque in his ability to find the net following his late runs into the box. See these examples below, beginning with a trip to Burnley in November, when he bursts forward late as team-mate Marc Guiu charges into the box. With Burnley’s Josh Cullen (24) distracted by the ball, Fernandez is able to sprint past on his blind side, get to the cutback before him, and strike a first-time shot into the net Against Brighton, Joao Pedro drops deep to collect the ball, drawing defenders. The ball is played out to Reece James on the right and Fernandez gets on to the end of a cross to head it in Against Liverpool at the end of the 2024-25 season, Fernandez calls for the ball from Pedro Neto, who cuts it back, by which time Fernandez is there to collect it, take a touch and score When Rodri was fit and at his peak, Guardiola prefered to use him as a single midfield pivot able to give others like Bernardo Silva the freedom to roam forward, safe in the knowledge that Rodri was there to clean up any mess. When he wasn’t fit, Guardiola would often switch to a two-man midfield. Maresca did the same in pre-season with Mateo Kovacic and Tijjani Reijnders there against Atletico Madrid in South Korea. The former sitting, the latter primed to burst forward. In terms of style, Fernandez is much more similar to Reijnders, who departed for Saudi side Al Qadsiah a fortnight ago. If you compare their heat maps (below), they are both at their most content getting on the ball in the channels. Rodri proved at the World Cup that he still has what it takes to be the best player on the biggest stage, but so much of the tournament was played at a slower pace due to the heat and altitude in the United States, Canada and Mexico. That allowed him to thrive. The Premier League is a less forgiving landscape with monsters more effective these days than metronomes. Between Fernandez, Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi, Maresca seems to have found his way to replace him. It’s just cost City more than £300million to do it.

Sports.title: BBC axe ANOTHER sports show as part of cost-saving drive: Iconic Ski Sunday comes to an end after more than 50 years... just four months after Football Focus was cancelled
Sports.content:
Ski Sunday - a staple of the BBC's sports coverage for more than 50 years on air - has been axed by the corporation as part of their latest cost-saving drive.

The programme, first aired in 1978, had become an iconic part of the winter sports calendar.

David Vine was the first presenter of the weekly show that created household names in the UK out of alpine skiers like Franz Klammer, Konrad Bartelski and Michela Figini.

It became equally famous for its theme tune, a stirring violin-led arrangement called ‘Pop Looks Bach’, which was composed by Sam Fontey.

The decision comes just over four months since long-running football show Football Focus was also axed.

Philip Bernie, Head of BBC Sport Events, explained the decision, saying: 'Ski Sunday has been a truly iconic programme and a much-loved part of BBC Sport's output for many years. Generations of viewers have enjoyed its coverage of the best in winter sports.

'We are enormously proud of the role it has played in bringing these moments to audiences across the UK, and extremely grateful to the brilliant people who have delivered them, not least the current outstanding team.

BBC show Ski Sunday has been brought to an end after nearly 50 years on television screens

'These decisions are never easy, but as audience viewing habits evolve and we work to deliver value for licence fee payers, we have to make tough choices. We remain committed to bringing audiences the very best of winter sport, above all at the Winter Olympics, across BBC Sport's platforms.'

BBC Sport chief Alex Kay-Jelski, meanwhile, said upon the cancellation of Football Focus that the decision reflected 'the continued shift in how audiences engage with football and our commitment to evolving how we deliver content to reach fans wherever they are.'

Just like the football show, Ski Sunday formed part of weekend show Sunday Grandstand.

It was presented by David Vine for a number of years, with ex-skier Graham Bell taking the reins alongside former snowboarder Ed Leigh.

Chemmy Alcott, who participated in four Winter Olympics, meanwhile, joined the show alongside Leigh five years ago.

Fans were left divided by the news, with one writing on X: 'That's so sad, I'm not into skiing but as a kid used to watch that with my dad with David Vine on comms.'

Another, alongside three crying emojis, posted: 'What's next? Today at Wimbledon? Today at the Test?'

Some, though, weren't fussed.

'I'm 25 and have never seen this on TV,' one X user wrote. 'I've obviously heard people talk about it (mainly its theme tune) and assumed it had ended in the 80s or 90s.'

Another shared: 'How was skiing a TV show on the BBC for 50 years?'

The BBC will continue to show sports broadcasts such as the men's and women's World Cups, the Olympic Games and Match of the Day.

Sports.title: Scott McTominay set to undergo heart surgery - as Napoli release health update on former Man United star
Sports.content:
Scott McTominay is set to undergo corrective heart surgery, his club Napoli have confirmed.

The former Manchester United star, 29, has developed a heart condition known as mild, benign arrhythmia.

According to medical experts, this is an irregular heart rhythm that is non life-threatening and something that should be resolved after the corrective procedure.

In a statement, Napoli said: 'Following the onset of a mild benign arrhythmia, Scott McTominay will undergo corrective surgery using a cardiac arrhythmia ablation (PFA) in the coming days.

'He will be available again after the international break.'

The British Heart Foundation say the procedure that McTominay will undertake is when heat or cold energy is used to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat.

Scott McTominay is set to undergo corrective heart surgery, his club Napoli have confirmed

McTominay (pictured with partner Cam Reading) should return to action after a short period out

He is expected to be able to return to full fitness following a short period out.

However, Napoli's revelation that he will miss the international break means that McTominay will be unavailable for new Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli's first four games in charge.

The midfielder featured in Napoli's 2-1 defeat by Como in Serie A on Sunday, with the 29-year-old substituted after 56 minutes.

He previously played the full 90 minutes in their 2-0 victory over Genoa on the opening day of the season.

McTominay has been a revelation since joining the Italian side from Manchester United in 2024.

The Scottish star has scored 27 goals and added 10 assists in just 82 appearances, while he played a key role in their Serie A triumph in 2024-25.

Under Antonio Conte, he evolved from a dependable squad player at Old Trafford into one of Europe's most effective box-crashing midfielders, scoring 12 Serie A goals and earning the division's MVP award during that superb campaign.

He also came 18th in the Ballon d'Or rankings in 2025, ahead of players including Jude Bellingham, Erling Haaland and Michael Olise.

McTominay repeatedly delivered in big moments, none more so than on the final day of the season when an acrobatic strike put Napoli ahead as they clinched the title over Inter Milan.

His impact prompted comparisons with Napoli icon Diego Maradona, with the Argentine's son even likening the Scot to Jesus.

Napoli added that McTominay is expected to miss Scotland's upcoming fixtures this month

But it is not only McTominay's exploits on the pitch that have won over supporters.

McTominay has embraced life in Naples with his partner Cam Reading and immersed himself in Neapolitan culture, while also learning to speak Italian.

On the day of his medical, he asked to visit the club's home, the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, to pay his respects to the Argentine legend.

He also went viral in April 2025 after hailing the quality of local tomatoes.

'Oh my goodness, the tomatoes,' he said. 'Bellissimo. I never ate them at home, they are just red water.

'Here, they actually taste like tomatoes. Now I eat them as a snack. I eat all the vegetables, all of the fruits. It is all so fresh. It's incredible.'

Moments like this helped McTominay earn the endearing nickname 'McFratm', with 'Fratm' meaning 'my brother' in local slang.

His face has appeared on murals, flags and even birthday cakes, while supporters erected a shrine to him in Naples city centre after the 2025 title triumph.

Sports.title: Tony Romo opens up on private alcohol struggles leading up to drunk-driving arrest as he pleads no contest to charges... and reveals if he plans to return to CBS NFL booth
Sports.content:
NFL legend and CBS analyst Tony Romo candidly opened up on his struggles with pain medication and alcohol dependency as he pleaded no contest over his drunk-driving arrest.

Romo, 46, was pulled over in his Jeep in Milwaukee on July 23 and later charged with OWI after performing poorly in sobriety tests, with humiliating bodycam footage of the incident quickly going viral.

Over a month on from the arrest, the former quarterback took accountability for his action as he pleaded no contest to the offense.

'Football has shaped nearly every meaningful part of my life,' he said in a statement on Tuesday. 'I played for more than 20 years, including 14 in the NFL with the Dallas Cowboys. After my retirement, CBS gave me the profound honor of staying close to the game through broadcasting.

'Playing taught me the power of relationships, the strength of a team, and the toughness to face failure head-on with honesty, resilience, and the determination to do better.

'This is one of those moments when I am leaning on everything football taught me.

NFL legend and CBS analyst Tony Romo pleaded no contest to an OWI charge

The former quarterback was arrested after being pulled over in Milwaukee on July 23

'This morning, I faced a recent personal failure by pleading no contest to a civil offense for OWl in Wisconsin. I own this completely.'

The former Dallas Cowboys star also opened up on his private health battles as he addressed his future with CBS.

Romo revealed that he had been struggling with a dependency on pain medication after multiple back surgeries during his playing career left him in debilitating pain. He said that he turned to alcohol in an effort to wean himself off the medication.

'Multiple back surgeries ended my career earlier than I expected and left me with constant, debilitating pain,' he added. 'That pain led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol.

'As I have taught my three young sons: when you fall short, you stand up and take full responsibility. That is an important first step. The harder and more important step is examining the path that brought you here and making the changes necessary to move forward.

'That path requires honesty.

'None of this is an excuse. These are my failures, and I take responsibility for them.'

Romo was placed on indefinite leave by CBS following his arrest and temporarily replaced by JJ Watt and the future of his $18m-a-year CBS contract has been shrouded in doubt.

Romo has been on leave at CBS since his OWI arrest month in his native Wisconsin

Yet, Romo appeared to hint that he would eventually return to the booth after taking time away to focus on his health.

'The past month has been difficult, but it has also been personally significant,; he continued.

'It has required me to confront and own my mistakes fully - to the Lord, to myself, to my family, and now to the public.

'I am working closely with a team of doctors to address my health and make the necessary changes. I am deeply grateful for the support of my family, my friends, and the NFL community including players, coaches, and owners. Your encouragement has meant more to me than you know.

'As I turn my attention to my health, my family, and, in time, my return to CBS, I kindly ask for privacy during this period.'

Court records show Romo reached a deal with prosecutors on Tuesday to close out the case.

His driving privileges have been revoked for six months and was ordered to attend and complete an alcohol assessment program. Additionally, an ignition interlock device must be installed on his cars for the next year.

Romo was also ordered to pay a $784 fine, records stated.

Romo was on his way home from a golf tournament in Milwaukee when he was pulled over by cops last month, telling them he had not had anything to drink and was on his way to visit 'Grandma and Grandpa'.

A police report later revealed that an officer found an 'open bottle of an alcoholic beverage' on the passenger side of his black Jeep vehicle.

A week on from his arrest, CBS placed him on leave and Romo has been keeping a low profile ever since.

The NFL quarterback legend poses for a photo with his wife Candice at a 2023 golf tournament

CBS Sports president David Berson, meanwhile, spoke to the media ahead of the NFL season and confirmed that the network has no immediate plans for Romo to return to TV screens.

'It's an evolving situation and therefore we are still assessing,' he said on August 11. 'There is no timetable or final decision at this time.

'I hope you can respect and appreciate this is a personnel matter and a legal one for Tony, so I can't speak to that aspect of things.'

Romo is owed $72m over the next four years of his current contract, putting the network in a precarious position as they decide what to do next.

On the air, Romo's work as the lead color analyst for the NFL on CBS has become increasingly divisive with fans.

As he approaches what would be his 10th season with the network, he has been facing calls to step down after being criticized for his strange affectations and errors in commentary.

Whether it was confusing Josh Allen for Patrick Mahomes , letting out a bizarre groan during the Bills-Jaguars game or calling a 4th & 1 carry like a first-down , Romo had his share of blunders in last season's playoffs alone.

Romo, who famously dated Jessica Simpson, is married to wife Candice, a past Miss Missouri

Romo said he felt unwell during the Bills-Jaguars incident, explaining: 'We had a bunch of guys sick, we were just grinding through it. You’re not going to miss a playoff game.'

In December 2023, at the height of 'Tayvis' Mania, Romo bizarrely addressed Taylor Swift as the wife of Travis Kelce while she watched him play for the Kansas City Chiefs.

It came long before the couple announced their engagement back in August of 2025 and got married last month.

Romo, who famously dated Jessica Simpson from 2007 to 2009, is married to Candice Crawford Romo, a former broadcast journalist and past Miss Missouri. They have three children.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
