World.title: Summer favorite Saaremaa drew more tourists this season
World.content:
While the tourism sector still has room for improvement, Saaremaa businesses and officials say the Western Estonian island has seen more visitors this summer.

Ferry statistics confirm what local islanders already noticed this summer: a marked increase in tourists on bike, arriving from both Estonia and abroad.

Eva and Thomas, two Polish cyclists, began their trek in Tallinn two days ago.

"Yesterday we were in Hiiumaa, and we're going to Latvia and Lithuania," said Eva. "And we are going to finish in Suwalki."

Veiko, an Estonian who also traveled from Tallinn, said he takes a similar cycling trip each summer, typically riding more than 100 kilometers in both Hiiumaa and Saaremaa.

"I rode 30 yesterday, today will be 60, and we'll see from there," he said.

Visit Saaremaa director Anu Lomp said new direct flights from Helsinki to Kuressaare have also boosted visitor numbers, with tourism businesses reporting a significant increase in Finnish guests.

"The Finnair route has also made a difference this tourist season," she said.

Room for improvement

Even so, local officials and businesses say the municipality has room to do more to attract visitors and come up with something new.

"People are always looking for something new and exciting, and that's what the tourism sector really needs — something new and exciting," Lomp explained.

Local businessman and politician Mart Maastik likewise said the local government could be doing more to support business, including tourism, on the island.

"You need to create things with a bit of a twist, because they're what draw people in," Maastik said.

Meanwhile, for the first time ever, Kuressaare's Söstar Kitchen & Bar even saw lines for its outdoor seating area. Owner Kristi Kuuse said their busy season kicked off earlier than usual this year.

"We were already seeing a nice flow of people at the beginning of May," Kuuse recalled. "This season has been very different from the previous two — it started early and there have been a lot of foreign tourists."

World.title: Kersti Kaljulaid: In a good school, children learn the art of being human
World.content:
In a good school, our children learn how to be human — empathy, searching for and finding shared interests, understanding and acknowledging different opinions, and also recognizing the boundaries where it is time to stop arguing and accept differing worldviews, writes Kersti Kaljulaid.

When I began school exactly half a century ago, we were starting from a much more equal position than today's schoolchildren. A child's knowledge was mostly a simple function of their age. Humanity's level of knowledge seemed such that in 12 school years one could give everyone an overview of the best of world literature, the cultural development of Estonians from the national awakening to flourishing socialism, the natural sciences through the centuries up to modern astronomy and genetics.

There was time to learn all 14 grammatical cases and to write at a level certainly higher than what journalism's utilitarian texts now offer. There was no "wide" and "narrow" math, no state exams except for literature. Yes, imagine — teachers were allowed to decide themselves what grade to give a child on an exam, and even those awarding medals trusted that result.

Meanwhile, humanity has created an enormous amount of new knowledge in the sciences. The idea of what constitutes a graspable amount of good literature that everyone should read has changed drastically. Access to knowledge is nearly absolute for anyone who knows how to use the internet. A classroom of children will never again have such uniform knowledge as half a century ago.

School, however, has not changed much. Children sit in classrooms sorted by age, lessons follow a predetermined program, and knowledge checks focus on proving that the program has been completed. Teachers' attitudes toward students have certainly changed. In my time, the teacher was always right — at least in my school — whereas today teachers feel they have no room for asserting themselves.

"Social skills still mature through interaction with other people, but the surrounding environment offers few opportunities to validate school acquired knowledge."

School struggles with a rapidly changing world because the human growth cycle remains the same. Social skills still mature through interaction with other people, but the surrounding environment offers few opportunities to validate school‑acquired knowledge — or rather, it shows that outside the prescribed path lie far better ways to cope than those found by diligently following it.

This is neither good nor bad — it simply creates different tensions in the school system, and it is inevitable. Among humanity's vast knowledge, it is increasingly difficult to choose what is absolutely necessary for everyone.

Children's greater autonomy makes classroom management different. Communication skills are more important than knowledge. Curiosity allows one to acquire a unique worldview instead of formal education and turn it into a profession. Some of these professions rely on scientific understanding, but even a fantasy world without any truth can turn out to be lucrative.

At the same time, there is a body of essential knowledge humanity must not lose — otherwise we would no longer know how to treat people, build houses, or create text that is clearly understood across languages.

School must still fulfill the same ultimate goal: to send out young adults who can function acceptably as members of society, achieve their goals without harming others, value others' contributions, and know how to take them into account. These young people must also be equipped with enough classical knowledge to study medicine, engineering, IT, or become creative artists.

So what should we do? Probably accept where humanity is headed and adapt. What does that mean? I suspect it means accepting the imperfection of education.

There are few things we can be certain will benefit the children starting school this week in their future working lives.

But something does remain. And that is the ability to function in human society. I do not use the word "values," because it immediately makes people want to enter a culture war. But something must remain: we must be able to live alongside each other. Even more — we must be able to defend ourselves together, grow the economy, care for the elderly, treat the sick, and distribute society's benefits in a way that results in the greatest number of satisfied people.

Life no longer requires acquiring these basic societal skills in order to grow up. Previously, a young person eventually had to ride the bus alone, buy milk and bread from the store, or agree with a neighbor on how to complete shared tasks.

"School must still fulfill the same ultimate goal: to send out young adults who can function acceptably as members of society."

Society now allows people to avoid human interaction both in stores and when using services. Our natural, life‑acquired ability to be one member of society declines — the ability to understand others' feelings, read body language, or talk through difficult situations. Half a century ago, it was common that there weren't enough balls or bicycles for everyone, and children had to learn to share. And if you didn't want to play alone, you had to make room for both your own and others' interests in the group.

Call these values or emotional intelligence — I call it the art of being human. And this is a person's true competitive advantage over any smart machine, no matter how well the latter pretends to be human.

Compassion. Sensing that something is wrong with someone even if they insist everything is fine. Understanding that a hug helps against sadness even if it doesn't remove the cause. Knowing that you must not hurt others. Knowing that evil must be confronted with lawful force — but not before all other options are exhausted. Understanding that those other options lie in cooperation between people with shared interests, such as neighboring nations who value free choice. Recognizing the necessity of rules and being able to follow them even when short‑term self‑interest suggests otherwise.

Call these things general competencies or values or whatever you prefer — but keep culture wars out of this discussion.

In a good school, our children learn how to be human — empathy, searching for shared interests, understanding and acknowledging different opinions, and also recognizing the boundaries where it is time to stop arguing and accept differing worldviews.

These skills can emerge only in a school environment that values meaningful discussion, and such an environment must be consciously shaped. If it were up to me, I would leave more room for independent decision‑making to every school leader and teacher. I would not impose so much oversight and control — I would let schools prepare children for life as they see best, and let universities measure knowledge at admission according to the needs of each field.

World.title: Narva-Jõesuu eyes €10 million revival for historic resort hall
World.content:
Narva-Jõesuu is buying back its historic resort hall from private owners, with plans to redevelop it with EU support as a mixed-use cultural and community hub.

Completed in 1912, the Art Nouveau-style resort hall, or kuursaal, is listed in Estonia's National Registry of Cultural Monuments. Much of the building was damaged during World War II.

More than two decades ago, a company linked to businessman Tiit Vähi bought the property with plans for a hotel and restaurant, but the project never materialized.

Mayor Maksim Iljin said those plans had once been realistic, but became unfeasible after the global financial crisis, Russia's annexation of Crimea and the ongoing war in Ukraine.

"And that's one of the reasons we've reached the point where we're buying the property back for the city," he said.

Events as soon as next year

Narva-Jõesuu City Council has agreed to pay €375,000 for the resort hall and nearly 3 hectares of adjoining properties, with the aim of seeking EU funding for the redevelopment.

The total investment could reach €10 million, Iljin said, noting that the city has already set aside up to €20,000 this year for basic safety work and plans to begin improving the surrounding grounds.

The Narva-Jõesuu resort hall (kuursaal) during Estonia's first independence era. 1925. Source: Osvald Haidak/Eesti Ajaloomuuseumi kogu/Muis.ee

The city hopes to start holding events in the park behind the hall next year.

The redevelopment could also include a new concert hall, addressing a longstanding shortage of year-round venues in town big enough to host major events.

"Our plan is not only to restore the existing resort hall but also build a concert hall, because outside the summer season, we pretty much have no options for hosting large events," the mayor explained.

High hopes for EU funds

The city plans to finance preliminary work, including surveys, expert assessments and design work, from its own budget.

For the rest, the goal is to secure EU funding when the next Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) begins, with three specific funding measures already under consideration.

The completed complex is envisioned as a year-round hub and destination, combining conference and event facilities with a restaurant, youth center and tourist information center.

World.title: Iraqi PM calls for boosting oil output to 10 million bpd by 2030
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called on Tuesday for an increase in oil output to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during a meeting held to discuss the country’s strategic plan to develop and increase oil production, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq’s oil output should be proportionate to its reserves, oil production capabilities, and the growing number of the population, allowing it to satisfy its residents’ needs as well as development requirements.

The prime minister indicated that it is important to improve infrastructure and export capacity to meet the expected rise in output.

Iraq’s oil production reached approximately 4.5 million barrels per day by the end of 2025.

Al-Zaidi directed an increase in output from oil fields in the Kurdistan region of Iraq and the expansion of exploration activities to achieve the plan’s objectives and reach a production capacity of 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

The prime minister also instructed the full recovery of associated gas to fulfill domestic energy demands, prevent waste, and eventually eliminate the need for imports.

According to al-Zaidi, the Oil Ministry will invite major foreign oil firms to a conference to attract investments, expertise, and technologies.

The Iraqi Oil Ministry is anticipated to reach deals with oil corporations to conduct exploration, production, development, and export projects, therefore improving the country’s position in the global energy market and bolstering its resources and economic capacity.

World.title: China-Nepal flood toll tops 1,000 as tunnel rescue offers last hope
World.content:
Nuwakot – The death toll from devastating Himalayan glacial floods crossed the grim 1,000 mark on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors including dozens feared trapped in hydropower tunnels.

Nearly 4,500 people are missing after the gigantic wave of freezing water, rocks and debris triggered by a high-altitude glacial collapse roared downstream on Wednesday, wiping out entire settlements and carving a path of destruction across Nepal.

Nepali rescue teams are digging, drilling and blasting through debris in a desperate race against time to free around 100 hydropower workers believed trapped in multiple tunnels.

So far, rescuers have recovered only bodies from tunnels blocked by sludge, and hopes of finding survivors are fading.

Excavators worked into the night on Tuesday, but an army update noted that “a large amount of water started flowing” into a hole they were digging, forcing them to start a new opening.

Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah has called the catastrophe “unimaginable and heartbreaking”.

With mortuaries overflowing in Nepal, authorities have begun burying hundreds of unidentified bodies after DNA sampling.

At least 17 bodies have also been pulled from rivers downstream in India.

Police, using a drone to search for survivors, said on Tuesday that they had located 24 corpses inside a single house in Nuwakot district.

Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said he still hoped some of the thousands missing could be alive.

“Miracles do happen,” he told AFP in an interview. “At this point, I do not want to completely give up hope.”

– ‘Find their bodies’ –

In the capital Kathmandu, crowds lined up to search for their missing relatives.

Debu Sapkota, a 58-year-old driver, posted photos of his 83-year-old mother-in-law and her granddaughter, alongside dozens of others.

Sapkota said he had little hope they survived after witnesses saw them being carried away by the torrent.

“I am here hoping to find their bodies,” he said

Some, believing they will never find their missing relatives, held symbolic funerals in accordance with Nepali Hindu customs.

“We searched everywhere, went to morgues across the country, but could not find his body,” said Jeevan Shrestha, as his 12-year-old nephew set fire to a tiny straw effigy representing his missing father.

Aid needs are enormous. Entire communities have been swept away, leaving families homeless and using makeshift shelters as heavy rain lashes down.

Roads and dozens of bridges have been smashed, and power plants destroyed.

“There are too many challenges,” said police officer E. Hawadi in badly affected Nuwakot district.

– Climate change –

AFP photographers in Nuwakot on Tuesday saw people scouring through mud for usable items and stringing up plastic sheeting for shelter in ruins.

Foreigners missing among the list include 583 in Nepal and 261 in China, coming from more than 30 nations.

They include tourists who had come for trekking in the Himalayas, as well as Hindu pilgrims seeking spiritual peace at Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash.

Nepal’s economy is already under pressure, with limited resources to respond to a disaster of this scale.

Kathmandu has warned reconstruction costs could run into the “billions of dollars”.

There is growing anger at the scale of destruction to hit Nepal, a largely rural nation of 30 million people.

The country has contributed little to the greenhouse gas emissions driving global warming, but is among those suffering its consequences.

Khanal, the foreign minister, told AFP that the “disaster should be seen as a warning signal to the risk that climate change poses to Nepal”, adding that support should be seen “from a perspective of climate justice”.

Scientists say the Himalayas, the world’s highest mountain range, are warming rapidly as global temperatures rise, accelerating glacier melt.

Glaciers in the wider Himalayan and Hindu Kush ranges are a crucial water source for around 240 million people in the mountainous regions, as well as for another 1.65 billion people in the South Asian and Southeast Asian river valleys below.

“It impacts the entirety of the Himalayan region’s civilisation,” Khanal said.

– ‘Mourn the victims’ –

Nepal said 1,050 bodies had been recovered by Tuesday, while 3,916 people remained missing.

China’s state media reported 16 dead and 546 missing.

That takes the overall number of reported dead to 1,066 and missing to 4,462.

In China, Tibet is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists, and Chinese authorities are the only source of official information.

More than 2,000 people are aiding rescue operations, including soldiers, Xinhua added.

It said on Tuesday that teams were “working around the clock to search for survivors, repair roads, set up communication base stations and restore power lines”.

Tibetan advocacy groups in exile have questioned China’s account of the disaster, but Beijing insists that the “release of information has been open, transparent and timely”.

World.title: China’s Xi arrives in Egypt as US sanctions threat looms over Iran links
World.content:
Cairo – Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Egypt on Tuesday on a rare trip to the Middle East as both countries face the threat of US sanctions over financial links to Iran.

Xi and his wife were greeted on the tarmac by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and the first lady, as well as a performance by an Egyptian folk dance troupe.

The two-day visit comes as both countries seek to manage the fallout of the months-long Middle East war, which began when the United States and Israel launched strikes against Iran on February 28, throwing the crucial trade region into crisis.

Washington vowed last month to destabilise Iran economically, warning of expanded sanctions against Tehran’s backers and partners that could hit Egyptian and Chinese banks, among others.

Xi’s visit “comes at a time when China’s economic interests are directly exposed to the US-Iran war”, said Gamal Salama, political science professor at Egypt’s Suez University.

China, a major buyer of Iranian oil, has presented itself as a neutral party in the Middle East conflict, repeatedly calling for a lasting ceasefire.

Egypt, a long-time recipient of US military aid, warned against regional escalation after a drone strike hit one of its ports in July.

China is “clearly seeking Egypt’s cooperation in managing and shaping regional affairs”, said Liu Jia, a research fellow at the Singapore-based Middle East Institute.

Beijing works closely with regional actors such as Egypt, which mediates between Israel and Palestinian groups, Liu added.

Both China and Egypt support an independent Palestinian state as part of a two-state solution.

“China sees Cairo as a strategic power broker,” said Salama.

Egypt’s “relations with both Washington and regional actors give Beijing both political access and diplomatic leverage across a region where China wants a much greater say,” he added.

– ‘Renewing the friendship’ –

As part of its economic pressure campaign targeting Iran, Washington last week said it would cut off the operations of Egypt’s Banque Misr in the UAE from the US financial system.

China, in response to the US measures and threats, has vowed to safeguard its interests.

Beijing has also sought to shore up ties with US-friendly regional nations ahead of a meeting between Xi and US President Donald Trump expected this month.

The Chinese and Egyptian militaries carried out joint air combat exercises in August that featured Beijing’s powerful J-16 fighter jet.

Xi’s meeting with his Egyptian counterpart Sisi, scheduled for Wednesday, follows a visit to Beijing by Jordan’s King Abdullah II, whose country has also been caught up in the US war with Iran.

Xi and Sisi are expected to discuss issues including the Gaza war, Iran, and shipping in the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz, according to Egyptian media.

“I look forward to renewing the friendship and working together with President Sisi to… map out a new blueprint for deepening the China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership,” Xi wrote in an editorial published in Egyptian media on Tuesday.

The Chinese leader’s first visit to Egypt in a decade comes as the two nations mark 70 years of diplomatic ties.

China is a major exporter to Egypt, with its trade surplus reaching $12 billion in the first seven months of 2026, according to Chinese customs data.

The leaders are expected to sign agreements on artificial intelligence, transport, energy and investment in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, Egyptian media reported.

The meeting with Xi sets Cairo up to land Chinese investments in its local AI and electronics industries, political scientist Salama said.

“What Egypt is seeking is strategic autonomy: not breaking with Washington, not aligning completely with Beijing, but creating enough room to pursue its own national interests,” he added.

World.title: IMF reaches agreement with Senegal on new $2.2 bn loan programme
World.content:
Dakar – The International Monetary Fund announced an agreement with Senegal on Tuesday for a new $2.2-billion loan programme, after a prior deal was suspended following the discovery of previously unreported debt.

The announcement comes nearly two years after Senegal’s current government, which rose to power on an opposition electoral victory, accused the former administration of ex-president Macky Sall (2012-2024) of having concealed the true extent of the west African country’s worrisome budgetary situation.

As a result, the IMF suspended a $1.8-billion aid programme it had agreed upon in 2023, pending further information and commitments from new President Bassirou Diomaye Faye’s government.

The new 36-month arrangement is meant to support Senegal’s “economic and financial reform program for the 2026–2029 period”.

But given past underreporting, it will also require “decisive corrective measures to support the authorities’ request for a waiver regarding the misreporting of data”, the IMF said in a statement.

The staff-level agreement will still need to be approved by the IMF’s executive board.

After the budget scandal erupted in 2024, the IMF found Senegal’s 2023 budget deficit was 12.3 percent of GDP, when the last government had said it was 4.9 percent.

After several IMF visits to Senegal to examine the country’s financial situation, the IMF and the government began negotiations in mid-October for a new aid programme.

Mercedes Vera Martin, division chief at the IMF African Department, told AFP in an interview Tuesday that “since the misreporting was identified, the authorities have taken efforts to improve the transparency.”

“That includes several audits. They have now reconciled their historical data, and recently they published a revised bulletin with the historical data, incorporating the findings of the debt,” she said.

The IMF said in its statement that it would also require “receipt of the necessary financing assurances from Senegal’s partners”.

– Heavily indebted –

With a total public-sector debt estimated at 132 percent of GDP at the end of 2024, according to the IMF, Senegal is one of the most indebted countries in sub-Saharan Africa.

However, its overall fiscal deficit narrowed sharply from 13.4 percent of GDP in 2024 to 6.4 percent of GDP in 2025, mostly driven by spending rationalisation, the IMF said in June.

Senegal has been able to continue financing itself largely through the regional bond market, but this comes at higher costs than loans from international financial institutions, development banks or governments, according to global ratings agency S&P.

Faye became embroiled in a political feud with his then prime minister, Ousmane Sonko, earlier this year over a variety of topics, including the IMF programme.

Although the president sacked Sonko in May, Sonko was afterwards elected as speaker of the National Assembly — a role that could complicate Faye’s ability to usher in IMF reforms.

While Faye prefers a more conciliatory approach with the IMF, Sonko has rejected any debt restructuring.

Asked whether the deal calls for restructuring, Martin said that it included “debt treatment”.

“It’s a sovereign decision. The authorities have a debt treatment plan that will allow us to move forward in our engagement”, Martin said.

Global ratings agency Moody’s last week downgraded Senegal’s long-term foreign-currency debt rating to Caa2 from Caa1, mid-negotiations with the IMF.

That said, “the Senegalese economy has remained resilient, recording 6.7 percent growth in 2025 driven by the first full year of oil production, although non-hydrocarbon GDP growth slowed to 2.2 percent”, Martin said in the IMF’s statement.

Senegal launched production at its first offshore oil field in 2024.

World.title: Car bomb at Colombian police station kills one, injures 11
World.content:
Los Patios – Colombian authorities said Tuesday that a deadly car bombing outside a police station in a northeastern province was carried out by the country’s largest active armed group, weeks after the government launched a new offensive against guerrillas.

The attack on Monday in the department of Norte de Santander killed one civilian and injured eleven others, including two police officers, local officials said.

It came shortly after President Abelardo de la Espriella’s hard-right administration conducted an airstrike against guerrillas in the southern Amazonian department of Guaviare, killing 20 people.

At around midnight, a stolen vehicle loaded with around 80 kilograms of explosives blew up next to the police station in the town of Los Patios, which borders Venezuela.

Local police commander Colonel Jimmy Belalcazar identified the victim as a 23-year-old Venezuelan man.

One of the wounded officers needed to have part of his leg amputated, Belalcazar told Caracol Radio, attributing the bomb to the National Liberation Army (ELN).

Next to the damaged station, dozens of onlookers stared at the flames roaring from the vehicle amid shards of glass and rubble, AFP journalists observed.

Colombia is the world’s largest cocaine producer and is grappling with its worst violence in a decade.

De la Espriella tapped into security fears to win presidential elections in June, although he only won the ballot by less than a percentage point.

He has pledged to get tough on crime by drawing on military support from the United States and Israel to conduct bombing campaigns against guerrillas on Colombian soil.

Monday’s earlier attack in Guaviare was the deadliest military campaign against armed groups in years and followed two more lethal airstrikes earlier in August.

A source at the forensics authority told AFP on Monday that four minors were among the dead in an airstrike last week.

Rights groups warn that children and teens are increasingly being recruited by these groups through slick social media campaigns.

De la Espriella’s leftist predecessor Gustavo Petro tried and failed to negotiate peace with guerrillas including the ELN as well as dissident factions of the rebel army FARC which disbanded in 2016.

Analysts say armed groups used government talks as cover to grow in strength.

Under De la Espriella, Colombia has joined US President Donald Trump’s anti-cartel coalition known as Shield of the Americas.

The Washington-led alliance includes Latin American countries such as Argentina, Ecuador, and El Salvador.

World.title: PetroChina’s production in Iraq drop during first half of 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – PetroChina, China’s largest oil and gas producer, reported a drop in oil production in Iraq during the first half of 2026 because regional conflicts forced temporary closure of plants.

The Chinese firm’s total crude oil output fell 2.8 percent to 462.9 million barrels in the first half of 2026, driven primarily by a 14.2 percent drop in overseas production.

Following the onset of the US-Iran geopolitical crisis, forced project shutdowns and operational disruptions at the company’s main Middle Eastern oilfields, particularly in Iraq, resulted in this rare supply contraction.

Despite the fall in output, the energy giant had a highly profitable first half. Net profit increased 22 percent on an annual basis to 103.94 billion yuan ($14.65 billion), surpassing the 100 billion yuan mark in a half-year period for the first time.

PetroChina executive director Ren Lixin said that Middle Eastern projects are gradually restarting, with regional output returning to over 90 percent of pre-conflict levels, according to South China Morning Post.

The Chinese company has major stakes in some of the world’s largest oil fields, especially in southern and southeastern Iraq.

PetroChina’s biggest projects in Iraq include the West Qurna-1 oil field, Halfaya oil field, Rumaila oil field, and al-Ahdab oil field.

World.title: Iran president urges return to truce, hails Russian support
World.content:
Bishkek – Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian on Tuesday vowed to match any US move to return to a June deal aimed at ending their war, warning that diplomatic efforts could be endangered by “pressure and threats” from Washington.

He also thanked Russian leader Vladimir Putin for Moscow’s stance on the conflict, in comments during an international summit in the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek.

Russia and Iran — two of the most sanctioned countries in the world — have massively deepened their military and trade ties during Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine.

Putin and Pezeshkian held talks on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit, attended by over a dozen leaders including China’s Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

They met a day after US President Donald Trump — who has warned Moscow and Beijing against arming Tehran — threatened to hit Iran “hard” after it and the United States traded fire for the first time in weeks.

Pezeshkian told the summit that if the United States returns to the deal aimed at ending months of hostilities, Iran “will immediately take reciprocal action”, according to the Iranian presidency’s website.

The deal, meant to set the stage for final peace talks, has collapsed as both sides accused each other of violating its terms.

Pezeshkian warned Tuesday that a return by the United States to “a policy of pressure and threats could derail the path of diplomacy”.

He later met Putin, telling him: “We appreciate and thank you for your positions at every stage.”

He added: “This shows that our relationship is a strategic relationship; it is not an ordinary relationship.”

– Putin hails Iran’s ‘courage’ –

Putin said that Russia was “trying to provide you with the assistance you need”.

“We admire your courage and resilience in the fight for your national interests,” the Russian leader said, according to Russian media.

“Despite the military and political situation, we are maintaining the momentum of our trade and economic relations from last year,” he added.

Russia and Iran are both under massive international sanctions and have become increasingly reliant on each other.

The US on Monday vowed to keep up a pressure campaign aimed at crippling Tehran’s economy.

The Middle East war began in late February with the US and Israeli attacks on Iran that killed its former supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Iran and the United States resumed exchanging fire on Monday following more than a month of relative calm, with the Strait of Hormuz a key flashpoint.

Tehran has maintained its closure of the strategic waterway, while saying it would return to its commitments under the June deal, which included reopening Hormuz, if the United States did the same.

– ‘A multipolar world’ –

The SCO summit takes place four-and-a-half years into Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine and six months into the war between Washington and Tehran.

The Ukrainian conflict was not mentioned publicly at any point but Putin spoke for an hour and a half with his Turkish counterpart Recep Tayyip Erdogan, whose country has hosted several rounds of talks to put an end to the war, according to the Russian news agency Ria Novosti.

Xi said Russian-Chinese ties had become “more solid” and that their “prospects will be even brighter”, while Putin said cooperation was “successfully developing on all fronts”.

Russia’s economy has become increasingly dependent on China since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

The SCO has historically focused on economic issues but has gained momentum in other fields in recent years under Moscow’s and Beijing’s leadership.

“The UN Charter must continue to serve as a key source of international law,” Putin told the summit on Tuesday.

But he added: “It is clear that new multilateral regional structures… are organically integrating into the architecture of a multipolar world alongside the United Nations.”

On top of its 10 members, the SCO now has 15 so-called “dialogue partners”, including Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Qatar, and two observer countries: Afghanistan and Mongolia.

World.title: Man City agree blockbuster deal to sign Chelsea star Fernandez: reports
World.content:
London – Manchester City have agreed to sign Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez in a blockbuster £125 million deal ($167 million) that would equal the British transfer record, according to reports on Tuesday.

City have been chasing Fernandez for several months and the Argentina international is on the verge of moving to the Etihad Stadium on deadline day.

Fernandez’s switch would equal the fee paid by Liverpool to Newcastle for Sweden striker Alexander Isak last year.

Enzo Maresca worked with Fernandez at Chelsea before taking charge of City in the close-season after his January exit from Stamford Bridge.

Maresca was keen to land Fernandez after the recent sale of influential World Cup winner Rodri to Barcelona, as well as the departures of fellow midfielders Bernardo Silva, Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders.

The 25-year-old would partner England’s Elliot Anderson and Moroccan Ayyoub Bouaddi in City’s revamped central midfield.

Anderson joined for £116 million from Nottingham Forest, while Bouaddi cost £86 million to become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso had left Fernandez out of his squad for the last two games as speculation swirled over his potential switch to City.

Fernandez, who signed for Chelsea from Benfica for £106 million in 2023, angered the Blues last season by expressing interest in joining Real Madrid and was dropped for two matches as a result.

The polarising star was sent off in Argentina’s World Cup final defeat against Spain in July.

He also angered England fans with his provocative celebration of his country’s World Cup semi-final over Thomas Tuchel’s men.

Fernandez has won the UEFA Conference League and the Club World Cup in his time at Chelsea.

World.title: NIA court orders attachment of accused’s property share in J&K terror-arms case
World.content:
A special NIA court has ordered the attachment of the share of accused Fayaz Ahmed Mir in multiple properties in Kashmir

JAMMU: A special NIA court has ordered the attachment of the share of accused Fayaz Ahmed Mir in multiple properties in Kashmir while the trial in an alleged terror-linked arms case remains pending. Special Judge Prem Sagar passed the order Monday while allowing NIAâs application filed under Section 33(1) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, officials said.The properties listed in the order include 15 marlas (1 marla = 272.2sqft) of residential land, two shops spread over 2 marlas, and agricultural land measuring 25 marlas in Bumhama village of north Kashmirâs Baramulla district.The court directed that no third-party interest be created in the properties until the trial is over. The attachment applies only to Mirâs share in the listed properties and will remain in force until the proceedings conclude. A copy of the order has been forwarded to the Baramulla deputy commissioner for compliance, officials said.âInvestigators alleged that Mir supplied arms, ammunition, and explosives to terrorists operating in south Kashmir, and received Rs 5.2 lakh in connection with an AK-47 rifle. The allegations are yet to be adjudicated by the trial court,â an official said.Mirâs counsel had opposed the attachment, arguing that the accused and his siblings had jointly inherited the properties, which were neither acquired through nor used for terrorist activities. The court, however, held that UAPA Section 33(1) permits attachment of property belonging to an accused facing trial for specified offences under the Act as a preventive measure.According to the case records, security forces intercepted a four-wheeler on the Srinagar-Jammu highway in Kulgam on Jan 11, 2020, and seized an AK-47 rifle, three pistols, a hand grenade and other incriminating materials. The occupants were identified as J&K Police DSP Devender Singh; Hizbul Mujahideen members Irfan Shafi Mir alias Advocate, Syed Naveed Mushtaq alias Naveed Babu and Rafi Ahmad Rather; former LoC trader Tanveer Ahmad Wani, and Naveed Babuâs brother Syed Irfan Ahmad. Four suspects, including two Hizbul terrorists, were arrested.

World.title: Srinagar ghost mall turns into Rs 422cr jewel in auction
World.content:
SRINAGAR: For years, grass and weeds had more business at Sangarmaal City Centre than shoppers did. Then came the bidders. A 45-kanal (5.625 acre) parcel around Srinagarâs stalled commercial complex fetched an eye-popping Rs 421.75 crore after an overnight auction far exceeded what govt had pegged.

Bidding opened at 11am on Aug 25 for land in front of and behind Sangarmaal, just behind Kashmir Golf Course and opposite Polo View, a pedestrian-only high-street market lined with cafes and boutique stores. One end of the property touches Chunt Khul, a stream running through Srinagar. Dal Lake is about 1km away. Lal Chowk is within easy reach.

That mix of location, scale and commercial potential made this largely underused land a prized piece of real estate.

By 1.48am on Aug 26, Sangarmaal became one of J&Kâs hottest pieces of public real estate, with officials watching the price race far beyond their Rs 200-crore expectations. The highest bid touched Rs 421.75 crore on a full-lease basis.

âMy heart was racing as the bid was going up and up. It is an important project for J&K and this bid will open investment in the Union Territory after a long time,â an official said Tuesday.





Parmesh Construction Company Ltd, a consortium of Pahalgam Green Hotels, a J&K firm and Bhutani Infra Ltd, emerged as the successful bidder.

Sangarmaal City Centre traces its roots to 2015, when then CM Mufti Mohammad Sayeed announced it as a new commercial venture meant to give Srinagar a modern skyline.

What emerged was an ambitious complex with landscaped areas, fountains, basement and surface parking, lifts and escalators.

Its commercial inventory included 62 shops in the main commercial module, 38 spaces in Craft Bazaar, 11 kiosks, two food courts, a restaurant and 11 office spaces.

But the dream never got off the ground. Most shops stayed shut. Buyers who acquired units did not open them. Weeds overran the premises, turning what was meant to be a bustling commercial hub into a near-deserted property.

Now, a fresh lease could mean a fresh start. The front and rear portions have been offered for development on a full-lease basis, with a multiplex and other commercial facilities proposed.

The Sangarmaal auction also set the stage for another high-stakes property bid. At Batamaloo, about 6km away, roughly 70 kanals (8.75 acre) of bus-stand land has remained largely underused and vulnerable to encroachment. Srinagar Development Authority (SDA) is seeking to redevelop it for better use.

Bidding opened at Rs 95 crore on Aug 27 and climbed to Rs 305 crore by evening, with Construction Engineers, another J&K consortium, emerging as highest bidder. Batamaloo is also being offered on a full-lease basis, with plans for shopping, office spaces and housing.

World.title: PM Modi birthday celebrations: BJP plans bike rally from Vadnagar to Varanasi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP has planned a trip of bikers between PM Narendra Modiâs birthplace Vadnagar in Gujarat and his parliamentary constituency Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh as part of its month-long events to celebrate his birthday on September 17, an exercise which will jibe with the partyâs political campaign in the two states where assembly polls are due next year.

With BJP looking to deepen its connect with the youth, Modi is expected to address students at Shri Ram College of Commerce to commemorate the institute's centenary celebrations on Sep 5.

While BJP has been organising events every year to mark the leaderâs birthday, it has scaled up the exercise this time as Modi will complete 25 years as head of govt, including as CM of Gujarat, on Oct 7.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The events beginning on Sept 17, when Modi turns 76, will include drawing and speech contests for school students across the country, hackathon and innovation programme on social media and 25 welfare campaigns, sources said.

A number of Union ministers and organisational functionaries, including Ashwini Vaishnaw, Mansukh Mandaviya, Smriti Irani, V D Sharma and Tejasvi Surya, have been roped in for various events.

Party sources said 10 biker groups each from Vadnagar and Varanasi will travel between the two cities, and their trip will be marked by outreach to people along the way.

While assembly polls are due early next year in UP, they will be held in Gujarat by end of next year.

World.title: Rising rivers inundate over 11,000 hectares across 5 UP districts
World.content:
LUCKNOW: Rivers in Uttar Pradesh reached or crossed danger levels at several monitoring stations as satellite data showed inundation of 11,358.49 hectares across five districts, highlighting the spread of flood conditions in the state.

The affected districts are Ballia, Ghazipur, Gorakhpur, Mau and Deoria.

The inundation figures were released by the Flood Management Information System Centre (FMISC) under the Uttar Pradesh irrigation department. Its satellite-based assessment, prepared using RISAT-1A MRS SAR data analysed by the National Remote Sensing Centre, showed major inundation in Ballia and Ghazipur and minor inundation in Gorakhpur, Mau and Deoria by Monday evening.

Ballia reported flooding in 179 villages across 12 blocks, covering approximately 8,061.63 hectares. Ghazipur saw inundation in 87 villages across six blocks, covering 2,341.33 hectares. Deoria reported flooding in 18 villages across five blocks, Gorakhpur in 14 villages across three blocks, and Mau in 13 villages in one block.

The combined assessment covered 311 villages in 27 blocks. The total submerged area was estimated at 11,358.49 hectares.





The FMISC clarified that the assessment includes riverine flooding, water accumulation in low-lying areas, rainfall-induced flooding and isolated waterlogged patches.

According to the Central Water Commissionâs readings available at 9 pm on Tuesday, water levels were at or above the danger mark at 11 monitoring stations in Uttar Pradesh. The situation was serious along the Ganga, Ghaghra and their tributaries in Budaun, Barabanki, Ballia, Mirzapur, Varanasi and Ghazipur.

At Kachhla Bridge in Budaun, the Ganga was flowing at 162.43 m, exactly at the danger level. Its warning level is 161.80 m.

In Barabanki, the Ghaghra at Elginbridge was flowing at 106.09 m, 2 cm above its danger mark of 106.07 m and more than a metre above the warning level of 105.07 m. The CWC forecast suggested that the river could rise further to 106.07 m by 9 am on Wednesday.

The Sharda also known as Mahakali river at Kukea in Lakhimpur Kheri rose to 139.81 m, marginally above its danger level of 139.8 m and well above the warning level of 138.8 m.

The Ghaghra was also above the danger mark at Turtipar in Ballia, where it stood at 64.08 m against a danger level of 64.01 m. The station recorded 22 mm rainfall during the day. The forecast, however, indicated a fall to 64 m by Wednesday morning.

In Ballia, the Ganga was flowing at 59.37 m, nearly 1.75 m above its danger level of 57.615 m. The district accounted for the largest share of the inundated area recorded by the stateâs FMISC.

The most pronounced river-level exceedances in eastern Uttar Pradesh were recorded along the Ganga and its tributaries. At Tendui in Varanasi district, the Varuna was flowing at 71.35 m against a danger level of 70.21 m. The station recorded 43 mm rainfall.

At Saidpur in Ghazipur, the Ganga stood at 67.52 m against a danger level of 67.19 m. The station recorded 68 mm rainfall. At the Ghazipur monitoring station, the river was flowing at 63.33 m, exceeding the danger level of 63.105 m.

The level was rising and was forecast to reach 63.47 m by 8 am on Wednesday. The station recorded 63 mm rainfall.

In Mirzapur, the Ganga was above the danger mark at Ahraura and Chunar. At Ahraura, the river stood at 74.75 m against a danger level of 74.30 m, though the trend was declining. At Chunar, it was flowing at 72.82 m against a danger level of 72.78 m.

At Narayanpur in Mirzapur, the Ganga was at 72.59 m, above the warning level of 71.41 metres but 21 cm below the danger mark of 72.41 m.

The station recorded the highest rainfall among the locations shown in the CWC data, at 75.4 mm.

The CWC data also recorded a high level at Chausa in neighbouring Bihar, where the Karamnasa was flowing at 61.86 m against a danger level of 60.39 m. The reading is significant for the downstream flood situation in eastern Uttar Pradesh.

âThe readings suggest that flood pressure is spread across multiple river systems rather than being confined to one stretch. While some stations showed a declining trend, water levels at several locations remained above danger marks, leaving riverbank settlements, agricultural fields, roads and embankments vulnerable,â said an official source.

BETTIAH: Unidentified and unusual fish swept into the Gandak river and its floodplains by floodwaters from Nepal have prompted the Bihar govt to issue a safety advisory, asking residents of West Champaran and Gopalganj not to consume or trade in such fish until their identity and safety are confirmed.The fisheries division of the dairy, fisheries and animal resources department issued the caution on Tuesday after unusual fish were found in local water bodies and low-lying areas across the flood-hit Gandak basin.Floodwaters from Nepal have entered the Gandak system, inundating several areas of West Champaran and Gopalganj. The department said fish can be swept away from ponds, rivers and other water bodies during floods and carried over considerable distances. During this movement, they may come into contact with contaminated drains, dead animals and other pollutants, raising the risk of contamination by bacteria, viruses and fungi.âDo not consume any unidentified or unusual-looking fish. Until confirmation by the concerned department, an unfamiliar fish should not be considered fit for consumption,â the advisory said.Residents have also been asked not to buy or sell unfamiliar fish caught from floodwaters or assume an unusual-looking species is safe merely because it resembles a commonly eaten fish.Anyone developing vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, dizziness or breathing difficulty after consuming such fish has been advised to seek immediate medical attention.Wildlife Trust of India director Sameer Kumar Sinha said most fish swept into the Gandak in Bihar following the Nepal floods are believed to be âBagarius bagariusâ, commonly known as the goonch catfish and locally called âGochitaâ.He said the large freshwater catfish is found in fast-flowing rivers of India, Nepal and parts of Southeast Asia. The carnivorous species feeds on smaller fish, crabs and other aquatic organisms and often hides among rocks in deep stretches with strong currents.Sinha said local communities consume the fish, but it spoils quickly after death and may pose health risks if eaten after deterioration. He urged people to follow the Bihar govt advisory and exercise caution. The species is listed by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) as threatened.

World.title: From marble inlay, silk to Mahabharata: What PM Modi gifted Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan leaders at SCO summit
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who participated in the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic, presented a range of traditional Indian handicrafts, textiles, tea, musical instruments and literary works to leaders and dignitaries from Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan.

The gifts showcased India's diverse cultural heritage while highlighting the country's longstanding cultural and diplomatic ties with Central Asia.

Gifts for Uzbekistan's president

Modi gifted president of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev a marble inlay decorative plate, featuring floral and foliate motifs in blue, green and red set into polished white marble. The craft is particularly associated with Agra in Uttar Pradesh and reflects generations of Indian artisan skill.

The Prime Minister also presented Mirziyoyev with two boxes of premium Kangra tea, Kangra First Flush Black Tea and Kangra Green Tea, housed in a carved wooden box. The tea represents the heritage of Kangra Valley in Himachal Pradesh, where cultivation dates back to the 19th century.

Another gift was a sandalwood Shata Tantri Veena, popularly known as the Santoor, a many-stringed instrument associated with Jammu and Kashmir.





Its resemblance to Uzbekistan's traditional Chang was highlighted as a link between the musical traditions of the two countries.

Modi also presented Mirziyoyev with the original handwritten scoresheet of Uzbek Grandmaster Javokhir Sindarov from the 2025 FIDE World Cup final in Goa. Sindarov defeated China's Wei Yi to become the youngest FIDE World Cup champion and qualify for the 2026 Candidates Tournament.

Gifts for Uzbekistan's prime minister

Uzbekistan Prime Minister Abdulla Aripov received a marble inlay decorative plate, showcasing India's traditional stone-inlay craftsmanship and intricate floral designs.

He was also gifted a marble inlay casket with a Banarasi silk stole. The white marble casket carries floral patterns created with coloured stones, while the blue Banarasi silk stole features a paisley zari design, bringing together craft traditions from Agra and Varanasi.

Gift for the President's spouse

PM Modi gifted Uzbekistan presidentâs spouse and first lady Ziroat Mirziyoyeva, a marble inlay casket paired with a Banarasi silk stole, blending Agraâs stone craftsmanship with Varanasiâs weaving heritage.

The floral marble work and blue paisley zari design reflected Indiaâs artistic traditions.

Gift for the President's daughter

Modi gifted the daughter of Uzbekistan's president a fine silver brooch featuring a floral bouquet in an ornamental basket. The piece incorporates openwork, latticework, leaves, blossoms, green cabochons and clear stones.

Gifts for Kyrgyzstan's leadership

For the prime minister of Kyrgyzstan, Modi presented a Dokra artwork depicting a pair of traditional musicians.

The handcrafted pieces use India's traditional lost-wax metal-casting technique.

Meanwhile, Kyrgyzstan's president was gifted a Ladakhi Tsug-dul blanket, a traditional woollen textile from Ladakh featuring geometric, floral and stylised motifs.

A 10-volume English translation of the Mahabharata by Bibek Debroy was also presented to the president.

Together, the gifts showcased India's regional crafts, artistic traditions, literature and cultural heritage while underscoring the longstanding cultural affinities between India and Central Asia.

World.title: Sudhikaran row: BJP SC Morcha performs ‘buddhi-shuddhi’ ritual for Rahul Gandhi
World.content:
Image credit: PTI

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The political row over the alleged purification ritual at Haldwani's Ramlila Ground following Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's rally last month has intensified, with the BJP Scheduled Caste Morcha performing a âbuddhi-shuddhiâ ritual for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi at Panchayati Temple in Dehradun.The development came as Uttarakhand Congress chief Ganesh Godiyal led a massive protest march towards the state Secretariat, condemning the alleged âpurificationâ ritual conducted after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's August 8 rally in Haldwani.Accompanied by AICC co-in-charges Surendra Sharma and Manoj Yadav and hundreds of Congress workers, Godiyal attempted to gherao the Secretariat. Heavy police deployment was made to disperse the protesters, while several workers were detained as they raised slogans.The controversy centres on allegations that a âsuddhikaran yajnaâ was conducted at Haldwani's Ramlila Ground after Kharge's address. Congress leaders have criticised the alleged ritual, calling it an insult to the party president and an instance of caste discrimination."The rally happened in Haldwani, and then that place has a suddhikaran and havan. Then, the BJP State President justifies it and says that it is okay.What else could be more shameless?...BJP is working on the RSS agenda," Uttarakhand Assembly Leader of Opposition Yashpal Arya told ANI.The controversy also led to an FIR against Rahul Gandhi following a complaint by a member of the Scheduled Caste community, who alleged that the Congress leader's remarks about the purification ritual hurt the sentiments of the community.According to the complaint, members of the Valmiki community participated in cleaning the venue and conducting the ritual after the Congress rally attended by Kharge and other leaders.Godiyal, along with Surendra Sharma, Manoj Yadav and Congress workers, had also reached Dehradun's Kotwali Police Station on Monday seeking registration of an FIR against those responsible for the Haldwani incident.The row has since spread beyond Uttarakhand, with Congress units in several states protesting over the alleged ritual. Rahul Gandhi and AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi have also criticised the incident, describing it as a manifestation of a "Manuvadi mindset" and alleging that it was an attempt to demean a Dalit leader.The BJP has denied involvement in the ceremony. Union Minister and Leader of the House JP Nadda condemned the act in Parliament, saying the BJP had no association with the organisers and that the matter would be investigated.The organisers, Shri Ram Sena, along with local BJP representatives, maintained that the havan was not conducted because of Kharge's caste. They claimed the ritual was performed because religious decorum had allegedly been violated at the Ramlila Ground.

World.title: The Rs 2.05 crore question: Can Meta be blamed for what its glasses record?
World.content:
A Delhi man has sent a legal notice to an Instagram creator and Meta Platforms after he was allegedly harassed and covertly filmed at a cafÃ© using Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses.

The footage was subsequently posted on Instagram and viewed more than 4.19 lakh times.

He has demanded that the video be removed, an apology issued and â¹2.05 crore paid in damages.

But the notice, issued on August 24, goes beyond the actions of the creator. It seeks to hold Meta responsible in two capacities: as the owner of Instagram, which allegedly continued to host the reel after receiving complaints, and as the technology company behind the design and marketing of the camera-equipped glasses used to record it.

The Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF), which provided the victim pro bono legal assistance, says this is, to its knowledge, among the first legal actions in India to directly raise the liability of a smart-glasses maker for harm allegedly enabled by its product design.

The case has not been decided by a court yet and the claims in the notice, so far, remain allegations. The man, whose identity has been withheld and who is referred to as X, is represented by advocate Apar Gupta.





So, what allegedly happened?

According to IFF, X was sitting alone at a Costa Coffee outlet in Delhiâs Khan Market on July 24 when a stranger, who eventually turned out to be a creator, approached him.

The creator allegedly pestered and insulted him with unsolicited questions and remarks and followed him inside the cafÃ©. X complained to the staff and eventually moved to another seating area to get away from the unpleasant situation thrust upon him.

What he did not know, IFF says, was that the encounter was allegedly being recorded through Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses. One or more of the creatorâs associates also allegedly filmed the exchange from other angles without his knowledge or consent.

The footage was posted as an Instagram reel on July 26. By August 6, according to IFF, it had received more than 4.19 lakh views, approximately 15,700 likes and over 500 comments.

X reported both the video and the account to Instagram on July 27. According to IFF, the reporting menu offered no category specifically covering invasion of privacy or non-consensual recording. The victim, therefore, selected âbullying or harassmentâ.

He also submitted a separate complaint to Metaâs grievance officer for India under âPrivacy violation â sharing of personal information or representation without consent.â

Instagram subsequently informed him that the reported material doesnât go against its âCommunity Standardsâ, according to IFF.

Why has Meta been named?

The most significant part of the notice concerns the glasses themselves.

Developed by Meta in partnership with eyewear company EssilorLuxottica, Ray-Ban Meta glasses resemble conventional eyewear but allow users to take photographs and record videos hands-free. They were launched in India in May 2025 at a starting price of â¹29,900.

The glasses have a small white capture LED on the front that indicates when the camera is being used. The notice argues that this warning is inadequate because it can easily be missed by someone who does not know that the glasses contain a camera.

âThe recording indicator on the said devices is inadequate and easily overlooked, and the harm that eventuated to our client is due to a design that is foreseeably enabled,â the notice states.

It argues that Meta âowed and breached a duty of careâ to X and was negligent in contributing to the alleged intrusion into his privacy.

Crucially, the notice argues that this liability arises from Metaâs own product-design and marketing decisions and is therefore separate from its role as an online intermediary.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Section 79 of the Information Technology Act provides conditional protection to online intermediaries against liability for content posted by third parties.

The notice contends that such protection cannot extend to a negligence claim arising from Metaâs own product design.

That argument has not yet been tested in court.

The Delhi dispute could now test a different question: whether a company that makes wearable cameras has a responsibility not merely to indicate that recording is taking place, but to ensure that an unsuspecting bystander can reasonably understand that they are being filmed.

To know more, subscribe and read the full story on TOI+ â

World.title: Driver held for unauthorised transport of 15 tonnes of blue metal in Tirupattur
World.content:
A 38-year-old driver was arrested by Natrampalli police near Jolarpet town on Tuesday for illegal transportation of 15 tonnes of blue metal without valid permit documents.

The police said the arrested person was identified as R. Kumar, a resident of Tirupattur. Initial inquiry revealed that special teams were formed in the district to prevent illegal sand mining, smuggling of ganja and other banned substances.

The police said a police team was on routine patrol near the railway station in Pachur village at Jolarpet town when they intercepted a lorry carrying loads of blue metal.

The police said Chittoor was a major site for stone quarries and crusher units for industrial purposes. The lorry was heading to Tirupattur to deliver the consignment at a private industrial unit when the police team intercepted it.

The police said that the driver had only photocopies of bill receipts of the consignments. During such large transportation of blue metal, original receipts should be carried for verification. The lorry driver was also unable to produce a valid permit issued by the Regional Transport Office (RTO) for the vehicle. A case was registered against the driver and the lorry was seized. A probe is under way.

World.title: Woman chopped into pieces identified in Salem
World.content:
A woman who was murdered and chopped into pieces in Salem has been identified. The investigation revealed that she was murdered over her jewellery.

On Monday, chopped pieces of a woman’s body were found in the overhead water tanks of a house at Arisipalayam. The police sent the body parts to the government hospital for a postmortem.

Subsequently, the victim was identified as J. Thangamani, 55, of Mettupatti Thadanur. Her family members confirmed her identity.

The police nabbed three persons, including a woman, in connection with the murder. Police sources said the deceased used to work as a maid at a few houses at Sankar Nagar.

The police recovered the weapons used in the murder from the water tanks, and further investigation is on.

World.title: NHAI restores two-way traffic movement around Green Circle in Vellore town
World.content:
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has restored regular two-way traffic arrangement around Green Circle, a roundabout below the elevated corridor of Chennai - Bengaluru National Highway (NH 48) in Vellore town on Tuesday.

NHAI officials said that the traffic restrictions around the Green Circle were in place since July 12 to facilitate the second and final phase of subway work there. As the underground work of the ₹7.50-crore project was completed, NHAI opened the carriageway around Green Circle for regular traffic movement. “Restoration of traffic movement will help reduce waitinng time for motorists,” said a NHAI official.

Earlier, only light vehicles such as two-wheelers, auto rickshaws, and cars were allowed to use the service lane to proceed towards Green Circle. Other vehicles had to use the carriageway of Chennai - Bengaluru Highway. Heavy vehicles had to take a detour of at two km to reach Green Circle due to traffic diversions that was in place since July 12.

“Restoration of regular traffic movement is a great relief for motorists and pedestrians as movement of vehicles is steady and gradual. It also helps walkers cross the Green Circle safely,” said G. Sugan, a motorist.

As the roundabout was identified as a ‘black spot’ (accident prone), NHAI decided to build a subway. The entire work will be completed before the northeast monsoon.

World.title: Urban areas get 30% of funds despite accounting for 40% of population: Karnataka Minister for Municipal Administration H.C. Balakrishna
World.content:
Minister for Municipal Administration H.C. Balakrishna, who has been batting for greater priority on resource mobilisation by urban local bodies (ULBs), said urban areas account for around 40% of the population, but receive only about 30% of funding from the Centre and State.

Mr. Balakrishna’s observation came during a meeting he was holding with officials of ULBs from Hassan and Mandya districts at the Regional Commissioner’s office in Mysuru on Tuesday (September 1).

Mr. Balakrishna also directed officials to create awareness among the property owners to get their properties assessed for obtaining A or B khata as applicable.

He also called upon the officials to ensure that the merchants of commercial shops rented out by the ULBs pay their rent regularly within the stipulated deadline. “If they fail to do so, notices should be issued and the shops closed,” he said, while warning that action would also be taken against officials if rent from commercial properties was not collected due to their negligence.

Officials were directed to prepare district-wise lists of drinking water and underground drainage works that were being delayed and arrange for separate meetings of the respective MLAs with the contractors and officials to resolve the issues.

The ULBs had already been instructed to reserve two acres of land for developing residential layouts for pourakarmikas, and the work was in progress. In addition, the Department of Municipal Administration would write to the district administrations to reserve five acres of land either on the outskirts of ULBs or in rural areas to provide sites to pourakarmikas after their retirement, he said.

Excise Minister Shivalinge Gowda, who also participated in the meeting, said many town panchayats in Hassan district were facing a shortage of staff and requested that at least the minimum required personnel be posted to them. He said the implementation of the directions issued by the Urban Development Minister to officials at the divisional level would be reviewed at district-level meetings.

Responding to this, Mr. Balakrishna said officials and staff currently deputed to other departments would be recalled and posted to areas within the Municipal Administration Department that are facing staff shortages.

In ULBs that were able to mobilise higher revenues, officials should engage eligible personnel through outsourcing, in accordance with the rules, he said.

MLAs A. Manju, A.B. Ramesh Babu Bandisiddegowda, Director of the Municipal Administration Department P. Ravindra, and other officials were present at the meeting.

World.title: Minister announces welfare measures for drivers, gig and construction workers
World.content:
Tamil Nadu government on Tuesday announced a 50% subsidy up to a maximum of ₹75,000 to 1,000 workers to purchase new electric autos, and a 50% subsidy up to a maximum of ₹30,000 to 1,000 workers to convert their existing autos to CNG systems. This is for those registered with Tamil Nadu Unorganised Drivers and Automobile Workshop Workers Welfare Board, Minister for Labour Welfare and Skill Development, J. Mohamed Farvas told the Assembly.

The Minister, presenting demand for grants for his department, also announced a provision of accidental insurance worth ₹10 lakh to gig workers registered with the Tamil Nadu platform based gig workers welfare board.

The Tamil Nadu government will establish Construction Skill Centres of Excellence in five government Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) at a cost of ₹76.46 crore to provide training in modern technologies to registered construction workers of Tamil Nadu Construction Workers Welfare Board. Mr.Farvas said that ‘Transit Accommodation Centres’ will be established with basic amenities in Chennai and Coimbatore at a cost of Rs.14 crore to provide safe accommodation for construction workers migrating to metropolitan areas in search of work.

A scheme called ‘Ayalagam Sellum Tamil Nadu Kattumana Vettri Karangal’ will be introduced to provide international standard skill training and foreign language training to facilitate overseas employment opportunities for 1,000 registered construction workers at a cost of ₹15.06 crore, the Minister said.

World.title: Bill to provide statutory framework to Indian Statistical Institute referred to House panel
World.content:
A Bill seeking to widen the remit of the Indian Statistical Institute and align its legal framework with evolving needs was on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) referred to a parliamentary committee for threadbare examination.

The Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026, was referred to the Department-Related Standing Committee on Finance by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla. The committee has been asked to submit its report "within three months", a Lok Sabha bulletin said.

Amid protests by its faculty, the Opposition had demanded that the Bill be referred to a standing committee.

The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha on August 2 during the Monsoon Session. It seeks the institute's incorporation as a 'body corporate' to strengthen its governance, promote academic excellence and research and allow it to serve the emerging needs in the field of statistics and allied fields.

The Bill says the President will be the Visitor of the institute and provisions for a Board of Governors that will be its principal policy executive body. The board will be headed by the chairperson, who will be an eminent person from the field of academia, industry, education, public policy, and statistical sciences. It will be accountable to the Central government, the Bill notes.

Academic Council

The institute will have an Academic Council, which will act as its principal academic body and will be headed by the institute's director. All full-time professors and full-time faculty will be members of the Academic Council.

The Indian Statistical Institute Act, 1959, declared the institute to be an institution of national importance and empowered it to grant degrees and diplomas in statistics. The Act was amended in 1995 to empower the Institute to grant degrees and diplomas in statistics, mathematics, quantitative economics, computer science and such other subjects related to statistics as may be determined by it from time to time.

The 1959 Act, according to the Bill, has limited provisions in respect of the governance, administration, finance, accountability and functioning of the Institute and is not adequate to enable it to respond to the requirements of an evolving academic and research environment.

Therefore, it says, the government decided to repeal the Indian Statistical Institute Act, 1959, to bring out comprehensive legislation providing for the incorporation of the Indian Statistical Institute, an institution of national importance, to excel as a globally recognised centre in Statistical Sciences and allied fields.

The legal reform will enable an ecosystem to train a new generation of high-quality data scientists and statisticians, bridging the massive talent gap currently facing India's tech and financial sectors, the Bill says.

World.title: Mysuru faces 55% rainfall deficit, drought crop loss estimated at ₹122 crore
World.content:
Deputy Chief Minister and Revenue Minister G. Parameshwara on Tuesday (September 1) expressed concern over the severe rainfall deficit, decline in employment generation and poor crop insurance enrolment in Mysuru district, and directed officials to step up relief measures.

Presiding over a drought review meeting at the zilla panchayat here after touring affected areas in Hunsur and K.R. Nagar taluks, Dr. Parameshwara said Mysuru district should have received 310 mm of normal rainfall between June and the end of August, but had received only 140 mm, resulting in a 55% rainfall deficit. The deficit stood at 56% in June, 61% in July and 45% in August.

Eight taluks — H.D. Kote, Hunsur, K.R. Nagar, Mysuru, Nanjangud, Saligrama, Saragur and T. Narasipura — have been declared severely drought-affected, he said.

Expressing concern over the decline in employment generation, Dr. Parameshwara said only 1.91 lakh person-days of employment had been generated in Mysuru since July 2026, a 55% decline compared with last year. “If 4.33 lakh person-days of employment were generated during the same period last year with good rainfall, why has the figure fallen so sharply this year? Are people not demanding work? What are the zilla panchayat CEO and the officials under him doing?” he asked.

Crop insurance

He also pulled up the Agriculture and Horticulture departments over the poor enrolment of farmers under crop insurance. While crop insurance has been taken for 49.64 lakh farmer applications covering 33,17,167 hectares across the State, only 20,836 farmers in Mysuru, covering 8,046 hectares, have enrolled.

“Why are officials showing such negligence? Why have they not encouraged farmers to enrol? Irresponsibility will not be tolerated,” he warned.

On fodder availability, Dr. Parameshwara said Mysuru district had 7,04,890 tonnes of fodder, sufficient for about 33 weeks. However, availability was lower in Mysuru and Hunsur taluks at 25 weeks each and Periyapatna at 26 weeks. “Farmers who have borewells should be given fodder seeds and encouraged to cultivate fodder,” he said.

The government has already released ₹25 crore to the Animal Husbandry Department for distribution of fodder kits, he added.

Drinking water

Drinking water problems have been reported in 14 gram panchayats across six taluks. Six villages are being supplied water through six tankers, while nine villages are receiving water through 10 hired private borewells. In urban areas, 14 tankers are supplying water to 13 wards across three Urban Local Bodies (ULBs).

He said drought review meetings for the Belagavi and Kalaburagi Revenue divisions had been completed and that he had personally reviewed the situation and conducted field inspections in Belagavi, Chitradurga, Tumakuru, Chickballapur and Kolar districts.

Crop loss

The estimated crop loss due to drought in Mysuru district is around ₹122 crore.

Joint Director of Agriculture K.H. Ravi told the meeting that 2,12,751 hectares, or around 56% of the cultivable area, had been sown this year. Of this, nearly 50% of the sown area had been affected and crops destroyed due to deficient rainfall.

Last year, sowing had been taken up on 3,76,609 hectares, accounting for around 76% of the cultivable area. The district experienced deficient rainfall during both the pre-monsoon and monsoon periods this year.

Mysuru district in-charge Minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah, MLAs, MLCs and senior officials attended the meeting.

World.title: Pala MLA Mani C. Kappan sentenced to one year in jail in cheque case
World.content:
The Additional Metropolitan Magistrate’s Court in Borivali, Mumbai, on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) sentenced Pala MLA Mani C. Kappan to one year’s imprisonment and directed him to pay ₹1.20 crore as compensation in an alleged cheque-bounce case related to shares in the Kannur International Airport.

The court directed Mr. Kappan to pay the compensation, along with simple interest of 9% from the date of the order until realisation, within one month. Failure to do so will invite an additional three months’ imprisonment. The case follows a complaint filed by Mumbai-based businessman Dinesh Menon.

“The accused Mani C. Kappan is hereby convicted for the offence punishable under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, vide Section 255(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. The accused is sentenced to suffer simple imprisonment for a period of one year and he shall pay a compensation of ₹1.20 crore with simple interest of 9% from the date of this order till realisation of the entire amount towards compensation within a period of one month,” the order said.

The court further directed that the compensation be paid to the complainant, subject to any orders passed by the appellate court. It also directed the police to issue a non-bailable warrant against the legislator for execution of the sentence.

MLA plans to appeal

Mr. Kappan was unavailable for comment despite repeated attempts to contact him. Sources close to the legislator said he would appeal against the verdict. They said Mr. Kappan maintained that the court had pronounced the judgment without hearing his side and that he had not appeared for the hearing.

Mr. Kappan, a United Democratic Front legislator, has also alleged that the case was aimed at preventing him from assuming a ministerial position that, he claimed, had been promised to him.

World.title: 5 security personnel among 6 martyred in Balochistan Customs House attack, 21 terrorists killed across province: ISPR
World.content:
Five security personnel, including two officers, and a Customs official were martyred during a “coordinated attack in an attempt to breach the Customs House” on the night of August 31-September 1 in Balochistan, the military’s media wing said.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that on the night of Aug 31-Sept 1, during multiple incidents in Nokcha, Chagai District, and Ziarat Cross, Pishin District, twenty-one terrorists belonging to Indian-sponsored proxies of Fitna al-Hindustan and Fitna al-Khawarij were sent to hell due to effective responses by the Security Forces.

The state uses the term Fitna-al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

“During the night of Aug 31-Sep 1, terrorists belonging to Fitna al- Khawarij launched a coordinated attack in an attempt to breach the Customs House.

“Security forces responded effectively and, after an intense fire exchange, killed 10 terrorists,” ISPR added.

Moreover, fleeing terrorists were also engaged by the security forces, inflicting further casualties, the ISPR said.

“During the exchange of fire, six brave sons of the soil, including two officers and a government official from the Customs Department, made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty and embraced shahadat,” it said.

The attack on the Customs House was a “manifestation of the terror-crime nexus, orchestrated to prevent Customs officials from performing their lawful duties and thereby facilitate the continuation of criminal activities in the area”, the ISPR stated.
